entries.name: The Revised Ranger
entries: Welcome back to Advanced Abilities! The 2024 edition of Dungeons & Dragons brought changes to every core class in the game, some of which were more appreciatively received as others. This section aims to revise 2024 Ranger class by making simple, easy to implement changes that maintain the designer's vision for the class, whilst correcting the most painful and restrictive elements currently baked into its foundation.

The aim isn't to remake the Ranger from scratch, but to bring the flavour and fun factor to the fore. Consider allowing your players to use this Ranger in your games, or talking with your GM about including some or all of these changes to allow the Ranger to reach its full potential.

classFeature.name: Hunter's Instinct
entries: When a creature marked with your {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB} drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or dies before the spell ends, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to move the mark to another creature you can see within 90 feet.

entries.name: Design Note
entries: This simple ability allows the Ranger to wield {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB} in combat without having it dominate the player's bonus action. This allows various Ranger subclasses (such as the Beast Master) room to shine, and opens up opportunities for a greater variety of builds and multiclasses to benefit from the new Ranger's reliance on {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB}.

classFeature.name: Hunter's Mind
entries: When you cast {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB} with your Favoured Enemy feature it doesn't require {@status Concentration|XPHB} and lasts until the end of its full duration or until you choose to end it (no action required).

entries.name: Design Note
entries: Just in time for our Ranger's 3rd level spells, we give them the opportunity to cast {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB} twice per day without concentration. The reliance upon {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB} for many late-game Ranger features in the core class restricts their ability to cast other flavourful and powerful concentration spells - this alleviates that burden.

classFeature.name: Focused Hunter (Revised)
entries: {@i This 13th-level feature replaces the Relentless Hunter feature.}
While an enemy is marked by your {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB}, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Constitution saving throws to maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB} on your Ranger spells.

entries.name: Design Note
entries: The current Relentless Hunter feature is low-impact at the best of times, and is made almost useless by the Revised Ranger's Hunter's Mind feature. Focused Hunter instead preserves the flavour of a toughened warrior with unshakable focus, extending the staying power of all Ranger spells (including {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB}, if it requires concentration).

classFeature.name: Champion of the Wilds
entries: {@i This 20th-level feature replaces the Foe Slayer feature.}
Your Constitution and Wisdom scores increase by 4, to a maximum of 25.

entries.name: Design Note
entries: A buff to the Ranger's spellcasting, Wisdom-based skills and toughness at this final level represents the apex of the "warrior of the wilds" fantasy. It's a comparable feature to the 2024 Monk and Barbarian capstone: a simple and effective design space worthy of retreading.

subclassFeature.name: Warrior of the Ignis Soul
entries: Renowned for their incredible courage, warriors of the Ignis Soul adopt a philosophy of blistering aggression and passion in battle. As daring as they are dangerous, these monks lean into their enemies' attacks, spurred on by pain and adrenaline. By throwing caution to the wind, they are capable of incredible feats of speed and power, unleashing precision strikes and devastating counters designed to break through any guard and end combat as decisively as possible. This power comes at a price, of course, and few who walk such a path live to an old age. The hottest fires burn fast, but blinding, and there are none who can claim a more spectacular combat style than a warrior whose soul blazes with Ignis.

subclassFeature.name: Ignis Soul
entries: When faced with harm that would leave others cowering, you lean into the pain, igniting your soul and enhancing your body.

When you take damage, you can use a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to roll {@dice 1d6} and increase the damage you take equal to the result. When you do, you gain a bonus to your weapon attack rolls equal to the result on the {@dice d6} until the end of your next turn.
The additional damage you take when you use this feature increases to {@dice 1d10} at 10th level, as does the bonus you gain to attack rolls.

subclassFeature.name: Warrior's Mind
entries: You can add your Wisdom modifier to your Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) and Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) checks.

subclassFeature.name: Warrior's Resilience
entries: Well accustomed to pain, your body is tougher than most. Your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point maximum} increases by 3, and it increases by 1 whenever you gain another Monk level.

subclassFeature.name: Gift of Ignis
entries: In place of one attack when you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can touch another willing creature within 5 feet of yourself and expend a number of unspent {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|hit dice} up to your Constitution modifier. Roll the expended dice; the target regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the result plus your Wisdom modifier. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier, regaining all expended uses upon finishing a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Precision Strikes
entries: Once per turn, when you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} or beat a creature's AC by 5 or more on an attack roll, you can choose one bonus effect from the following options:

items.name: Dizzy Strike
entries: The target cannot take {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions} until the end of its next turn.

items.name: Guard Break
entries: Creatures within 5 feet of you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against that target until the end of your next turn.

items.name: Hamstring Strike
entries: The target must expend 2 feet of movement for every 1 foot it moves until the end of its next turn.

items.name: Qi Thief
entries: You gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Wisdom modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Daring Counter
entries: Once per turn, when a creature makes an attack roll against you that isn't at {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}, you can expend two Focus Points to prepare a ferocious counter, leaving a conscious hole in your defense and granting the target {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on that attack. Immediately after the target hits or misses, you push it up to 15 feet away from you horizontally in any direction, and it must succeed on a Strength saving throw or fall {@condition Prone|XPHB}. If the target's attack roll missed, it also takes damage equal to three rolls of your martial arts die and has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on its saving throw.

subclassFeature.name: Ignis Ignited
entries: You resist Bludgeoning, Slashing, and Piercing damage. In addition, when you take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to use your Ignis Soul feature, you can make a single weapon attack as part of that same {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Spirit Thief
entries: Glittering jewels and gilded trinkets might make a worthwhile prize for the common, plundering criminal, but spirit thieves possess the formidable psionic power to claim a treasure beyond any value - a fragment of soul. Spirit thieves are rarer than rare, with only a handful of known operatives active across the entire continent of Avestros.

Their skills are as feared as they are coveted, for the Spirit Thief strikes directly at the soul of their victim, seizing a portion of the magical essence that exists within all life - and wielding it as a weapon. Doing so forges a mystical connection between thief and victim, granting the rogue insight into a target's thoughts and memories, and a small portion of the target's power to claim as their own. Though technically illegal as a practice, the few spirit thieves known to the great kingdoms act above the law, granted a pass by the ruling class in exchange for their invaluable talent for political espionage and infiltration.

subclassFeature.name: Soul Catcher
entries: When you deal Sneak Attack damage to a creature within 30 feet of you, you can forgo {@dice 2d6} from the Sneak Attack damage dice you roll to instead capture a fragment of that target's spirit, which remains with you for 1 minute, or until you die or choose to release it, or until you lose {@status Concentration|XPHB} (as if concentrating on a spell). A released spirit fragment returns to its original host. You can use this feature to capture a spirit fragment a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier, regaining all expended uses upon finishing a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
While you possess a spirit fragment, you gain the following benefits:

items: You can use your Sneak Attack against the creature you stole the fragment from, even if you would not otherwise meet the requirements to do so.
You share any damage {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|resistances} of the creature you stole the fragment from.
The creature you stole the fragment from has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against creatures other than you.

subclassFeature.name: Spirit Vision
entries: You have proficiency in the {@skill Insight|XPHB} skill. If you already have proficiency in {@skill Insight|XPHB}, you can choose another skill to gain proficiency in using this feature.

Additionally, you can cast the spell {@spell Detect Thoughts|XPHB} once per {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} without a spell slot or components (save DC = 8 + your Charisma modifier + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}). When you cast it using this feature, it doesn't require {@status Concentration|XPHB}. You can also cast the spell with any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.
If you possess a spirit fragment of a creature, that creature automatically fails any saving throw made to resist {@spell Detect Thoughts|XPHB} when you cast it.

subclassFeature.name: Spirit Guard
entries: While you possess a spirit fragment, you gain the following benefits:

items: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Constitution saving throws.
You gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the Constitution modifier of the creature you stole the spirit fragment from at the end of each of your turns (minimum of 1).

subclassFeature.name: Misty Projection
entries: You know the {@spell Dream|XPHB} spell, and you can cast it once per {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} without a spell slot or components (save DC = 8 + your Charisma modifier + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}).

subclassFeature.name: Fleeting Soul
entries: While you possess a spirit fragment, when you would fall to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} as a result of taking damage, you can instead use a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to release the spirit fragment to take no damage instead.

subclassFeature.name: Soul Embodiment
entries: While you possess a spirit fragment, you can cast the spell {@spell Shapechange|XPHB} as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, but the spell is modified in the following ways:

items: The spell doesn't require {@status Concentration|XPHB} or components
You must adopt the form of the creature you stole the spirit fragment from
You can adopt the form of that creature even if its {@variantrule Challenge Rating|XPHB} is higher than your level
The spell lasts until the end of your next turn

entries: Once you cast {@spell Shapechange|XPHB} in this way, you cannot do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of the Arrow
entries: Evil fears little more than a righteous warrior of divine power, blade in hand, standing resolute before them. Perhaps the only thing that strikes a greater terror in such cruel creatures is the warrior who can strike them down with divine fury from 1000 feet away.

Paladins who swear the Oath of the Arrow eschew the typical melee weapons of most holy warriors, instead mastering the art of infusing divine power within bows, slings, and firearms. Masters of ranged combat, such heroes strike from afar as devastating hunters, hailing the fury of the gods with bolt after bolt of magically charged ammunition.

items.name: Precision
entries: In all things, act with precision. Focus your energies and attention on your goal, and see it through with speed and fidelity.

items.name: Harmony
entries: Seek not to interfere with the natural ways of the world. Ours is the task to protect and preserve, not destroy and rebuild.

items.name: Detachment
entries: In life, as in battle, ours is a path of detachment. Do not allow passion to cloud your actions. Remain detached, rational, and focused on the horizon.

subclassFeature.name: Spiraling Smites
entries: Your power flows through your weapon and is carried as a spark of divine potential in every piece of ammunition. You can cast Smite spells, such as {@spell Divine Smite|XPHB}, immediately after hitting a creature with a Ranged weapon, as well as with a Melee weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}.

Additionally, when you reach 11th level, your Radiant Strikes feature triggers when you hit a target with an attack roll using a Ranged weapon, as well as with a Melee weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Divine Focus
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to enter a trance-like state of acute, divine focus. For 1 minute or until you use this feature again, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Ranged weapon attack rolls and you ignore the {@itemProperty L|XPHB|Loading} property of ranged weapons.

subclassFeature.name: Aura of Agility
entries: You and your allies' movement does not provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} while within your Aura of Protection. Additionally, you and your allies have a bonus to Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|XPHB} and {@skill Stealth|XPHB}) checks equal to your Charisma modifier while within your aura.

subclassFeature.name: Determined Sharpshooter
entries: When you miss an attack roll made at {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}, you gain a bonus to the next attack roll you make this turn equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of +1).

Additionally, you can forgo any {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on one Ranged weapon attack roll of your choice on your turn. The chosen attack roll mustn't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}. If the chosen attack roll hits, you can immediately cast {@spell Divine Smite|XPHB} without expending a spell slot.

subclassFeature.name: Divine Hunter
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you gain the benefits below for 10 minutes or until you end them (no action required). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5 spell slot (no action required).

items: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can make one additional attack with a Ranged weapon as a part of that action.
When you make a Ranged attack roll, you can use a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to immediately take the {@action Dash|XPHB} or {@action Dodge|XPHB} action.

subclassFeature.name: Battlemage
entries: You are a battlemage, a warrior trained in the devastating union of spellcasting and martial mastery.

Battlemages are brazen warriors, clad in armour and charging headlong into the fray. Though many use weapons, be they hewn from steel or conjured blades of darkness and flame, all rely on the explosive power of close range magic, braving the front lines to deliver an explosive blow with a single touch.

Bolstering the raw firepower of common infantry tenfold, these specialised warcasters are an awesome force on the battlefield, often finding roles as battalion commanders and generals, leading from the front in a blaze of fearless magic.

entries.name: GM Note: 2014 Sorcerer
entries: If you are using the 2014 rules for the Sorcerer, you receive your 3rd level features at 1st level instead. Additionally, you receive one additional trait at 1st level.

entries.name: Innate Sorcery
entries: {@i 1st-Level Battlemage Feature}

As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can unleash the simmering magic that rests within you for 1 minute, during which you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the attack rolls of Sorcerer spells you cast. You can use this feature twice, and you regain all expended uses of it when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Battlemage Training
entries: You have proficiency with light and medium armour, shields, and martial melee weapons.

subclassFeature.name: Battlemage Spells
entries: When you reach a Sorcerer level specified in the Battlemage Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Battlemage Spells
rows: {@spell Abyssal Blade|DMSecretWeapon24}, {@spell Flame Blade|XPHB}, {@spell Inflict Wounds|XPHB}, {@spell Mirror Image|XPHB}, {@spell Shocking Grasp|XPHB}
{@spell Fire Shield|XPHB}, {@spell Otiluke's Resilient Sphere|XPHB|Resilient Sphere}

subclassFeature.name: Warrior's Focus
entries: While your Innate Sorcery is active, you gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Charisma modifier at the end of each of your turns for the duration.

Additionally, while your Innate Sorcery is active, when you hit a creature with a melee weapon or melee spell attack, you can enhance the strike with fervorous magic once per turn. Choose one effect from the following:

items: The target subtracts {@dice 1d6} from its next attack roll or ability check made before the start of your next turn
The target takes additional damage equal to your Charisma modifier from that attack
The next attack roll that targets the creature has a {@dice 1d6} bonus to hit.
The target is pushed {@dice 1d6 * 5|1d6 x 5} feet horizontally away from you.

subclassFeature.name: Extra Attack
entries: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn.
In addition, you can cast one of your cantrips that has a casting time of an action in place of one of those attacks.

subclassFeature.name: Battlemage's Resilience
entries: The magic that ripples through you fortifies your mind and body.

items: You can add your Charisma modifier to your Constitution saving throws.

When another creature hits you with a melee attack, you can use a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to the damage of that attack. That creature must then succeed on a Constitution saving throw or take Force damage equal to the damage you took from the attack. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier, regaining all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Battlemagic Virtuoso
entries: You are a masterpiece of magic and martial virtuosity, a perfect union of meticulous technique and overwhelming power. The benefits conferred when you use your Warrior's Focus are enhanced in the following ways:

items: You gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to twice your Charisma modifier at the end of each of your turns.
You can enhance a melee attack roll with your Warrior's Focus ability up to thrice per turn, rather than just once (but only once per hit).

You can take one additional action each turn. That action can only be used to take the {@action Dash|XPHB}, {@action Disengage|XPHB}, {@action Dodge|XPHB}, or {@action Help|XPHB} actions, or make a single melee spell attack.

entries: Additionally, when you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, if you have no uses of your Innate Sorcery feature remaining, you regain one use.

subclassFeature.name: Creation Knight
entries: Bonds forged in blood and toil are bonds forged with magic.

Just as the shepherd is to the hound, as the calligrapher is to the brush, the warrior is to the blade. For Creation Knights, this bond between weapon and warrior is as deep as childhood comrades in arms. Such Fighters are those whose zeal bends the latent magic of the universe into a facsimile of life; their weapon becoming not only an extension of themselves, but a being all of its own. Such warriors are rewarded with a steadfast companion and ally: a sentient, living weapon.

subclassFeature.name: Living Weapon
entries: When you adopt this subclass, and any time you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can form a magical bond with a melee weapon you are holding that lacks the {@itemProperty H|XPHB|Heavy} or {@itemProperty 2H|XPHB|Two-Handed} property. The weapon becomes a sentient, animated weapon, which hovers in place while not carried or sheathed. You can attack with the bonded weapon even if you are not holding it in your hands as long as it is within 60 feet of you, using your Strength or Dexterity modifier for attack and damage rolls (your choice). The weapon remains bonded to you until it is destroyed, you die, or you use this feature again on a different weapon.
On your turn, you can command your bonded weapon to move up to 30 feet. Any time you make a weapon attack, you can choose to attack with your bonded weapon, targeting a creature within its reach.

subclassFeature.name: Bonded Strike
entries: You can make a single attack as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, but that attack must be made with your bonded weapon. You can make a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} attack in this way a number of times equal to your Strength or Dexterity modifier (minimum of once), regaining 1 expended use upon finishing a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, and all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Companion Magic
entries: Your bonded weapon's magic can extend to those who carry it. While you or an allied creature wields your bonded weapon in its hands or carries it on its person, it gains a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to its walking speed and can hover.

subclassFeature.name: Animating Magic
entries: You can now bond with any melee weapon using your Living Weapon feature, even if it has the {@itemProperty H|XPHB|Heavy} or {@itemProperty 2H|XPHB|Two-Handed} property.

Additionally, you can use a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make an {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|opportunity attack} with your bonded weapon targeting any creature that enters or exits a space within 5 feet of it.

subclassFeature.name: Allied Armament
entries: Your bonded weapon magically moves and feints to aid your companions and harry your enemies in combat. Allied creatures within 5 feet of your bonded weapon gain a +2 bonus to their AC.

subclassFeature.name: Flurry
entries: When you expend a use of your Bonded Strike, you can make two attacks with your bonded weapon as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, rather than just one.

subclassFeature.name: Spiritfarer Domain
entries: To most Clerics, life is the core philosophical tenet. So much of our divine energies are focused on its extension, preservation, or even eradication. But there is an order of Clerics who look beyond life itself. Beyond the beckoning veil, in the void and the cold, there is a gentle, guiding light. Not a trembling light, but a light that shines obstinate and proud and tiny, guiding every soul to its final home with a welcoming hand.

Spiritfarer is the name given to Clerics of this order, dedicated to shepherding souls to their final resting place - they are not worshipers of death, simply the lantern to lead all of us to what comes after. Higher powers the Clerics of this order might worship include Charon, Thanatos, the mightiest Valkyries, and other beings who usher souls as they make their final journey.

subclassFeature.name: Spiritfarer
entries: When a creature fails its save against your Turn Undead feature, in place of the feature's normal effects, you can choose for that creature to be {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by you for 1 minute, or until you or an ally damages it. Undead of a CR equal to or lower than your Cleric level that are {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by you obey your commands (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: Spiritfarer Spells
entries: Your connection to this divine domain ensures you always have certain spells ready. When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Spiritfarer Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Spiritfarer Domain Spells
rows: {@spell Calm Emotions|XPHB}, {@spell Find Familiar|XPHB}, {@spell Hex|XPHB}, {@spell Summon Beast|XPHB}

subclassFeature.name: Undead Shepherd
entries: When you cast a spell from your Spiritfarer Spells table that summons a creature, you can choose for that creature's type to be Undead, instead of its usual type.
Additionally, Undead {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by you or under your control can benefit from spells that preserve life but that normally don't affect Undead (such as {@spell Cure Wounds|XPHB}, etc.).

subclassFeature.name: Ghost Form
entries: Undead creatures of your choice that start their turn within 30 feet of you have a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to their walking speed and resist Bludgeoning, Slashing, and Piercing damage from nonmagical, nonsilvered weapons until the start of their next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Ghost Summoner
entries: When you cast a spell from your Spiritfarer Spells table that summons an Undead and requires {@status Concentration|XPHB}, you can modify the spell so it doesn't require {@status Concentration|XPHB}. It instead lasts for 1 minute, and ends early if you cast that spell again. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: One With The Void
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can become one with the void temporarily. Your creature type becomes Undead for the next minute. Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Final Rest
entries: You learn the spell {@spell Power Word Kill|XPHB}, and can cast it once per {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} without a spell slot or components.

subclassFeature.name: Blightsower
entries: In these tolerant days, even in cities where spellcraft is outlawed, it is scarcely more than a misdemeanor. Mages, once hounded and feared across all lands, are now welcome across the realms. The exception is held for the blightsower, brewers of rot and necrosis. For them, the old punishments remain; burning, hanging and the rack.

Blightsowers are universally despised. Common knowledge tells us how they fester like tumors, gathering sickly power and creeping like poison through the blood of a community. To the blightsower, plague and necrosis are allies; they willingly offer their body as sanctuary to microscopic killers that diminish and destroy life, in exchange for toxic power.

To the blightsower, there is no resource that can't be held gambit for greater strength. Such wizard's magic ravages their own body and mind to grow. Captured blightsowers are often found gormless and rabid, having strayed too far in pursuit of necrotic power, their own mind plundered to nothingness.

Although it may be possible for someone to wield these powers for good, it is unheard of. To be a blightsower is to commit to secrecy, necrosis, and rot. The reward is magical, microbiological allies with the power to topple nations and keel gods, but the price is one's own humanity, body, and mind.

subclassFeature.name: Shared Sentience
entries: Your body harbors a festering, necrotic disease or curse. You may have crafted this force yourself or contracted it naturally, but in either case, it is a source of power and an ally. You can grant the power within you a measure of sentience, empowering the necrotic force within you at the cost of your mind.

At the end of a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can choose a number of boons from the Shared Sentience Boons table, up to your Intelligence modifier +1. Each boon is granted by the ally within your body, the living disease imbued and magnified by a fragment of your mind. For each boon you choose, you receive a −1 penalty to your Intelligence checks and saving throws. These boons last until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, at which time your mind returns to you, and the penalty to your Intelligence checks and saving throws ends.

entries.caption: Shared Sentience Boons
rows: You have {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} with a range of 10 feet. Within that range, you can effectively see anything that isn't behind {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Total Cover}, even if you're {@condition Blinded|XPHB} or in {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}. Moreover, you can see an {@condition Invisible|XPHB} creature within that range, unless the creature successfully hides from you. Your eyes turn jet black.
You gain a bonus to Strength-based attack rolls and Strength checks equal to your Intelligence modifier. The veins running through your body glow an eerie blood red, visible through your flesh.
Once, you can cast a spell you have prepared of a level up to half your Intelligence modifier (rounded up) without expending a spell slot. Your body occasionally shakes and spasms uncontrollably.

While you aren't wearing armour, you can calculate your AC as 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Intelligence modifier. You can wield a {@item Shield|XPHB} and still gain this benefit. Your skin grows a waxy sheen and is painfully coarse to the touch.

Once per turn, when you hit a creature with a melee weapon or spell attack, it must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} for the next minute. A creature can repeat this save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. You emit a strong, sickly odour.
You gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in one skill of your choice. Your body creaks and cracks with every movement.
You gain proficiency in two skills of your choice. You have no sense of smell or taste.

As an action, you can make a melee spell attack against a creature within 5 feet of you. Hit or miss, the target cannot take {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|reactions} until the start of your next turn. On a hit, the target also takes {@damage 1d12} Necrotic damage. This damage increases by {@damage 1d12} when you reach 5th level ({@damage 2d12}), 11th level ({@damage 3d12}) and 17th level ({@damage 4d12}). Your finger and toenails grow long, jagged, and shift in hue to a poisonous green.

subclassFeature.name: Rot Caster
entries: When you cast a spell that forces a creature {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} by you to make a saving throw, you can impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on that save. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier, regaining all expended uses upon finishing a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Sickly Swarm
entries: As an action, you summon a swarm of fey spirits in the form of rats, bats, or spiders that flit around you in a 15-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} for the next minute, or until you fall {@condition Unconscious|XPHB}. While the swarm persists, you gain a +3 bonus to your AC, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) checks, and creatures of your choice that enter the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} for the first time on a turn or start their turn there must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or take {@damage 2d4} Necrotic damage and be {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} for the next minute. A creature {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} in this way can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of their turns, ending the effect on a success.
Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, unless you expend a spell slot of 3rd level or higher to regain a use of it (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: Viral Curse
entries: Your grim powers carry a magical curse, able to strike and infect the soul as well as the body. Your blightsower features and spells you cast that inflict the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition can affect creatures of your choice typically immune to the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.

subclassFeature.name: Viral Ally
entries: The microscopic, magical allies within your bloodstream fortify you against other necrotic forces, and can warn you against incoming harm. You gain the following benefits:

items.name: Evasion
entries: When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

items.name: Immunity
entries: You resist Necrotic damage, and you are immune to Poison damage and the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.

items.name: Uncanny Dodge
entries: When an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to halve the attack's damage against you.

subclassFeature.name: Spiraling Necrosis
entries: The necrotic power of your spells spreads like an airborne, noxious cloud of decay. When you cast a spell with a spell slot that targets only one creature and doesn't have a range of self, you can target a number of additional creatures within 30 feet of the initial target up to half the level of the spell slot expended (rounded down).
Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Plaguecrafter
entries: Assassination is unpleasant work, but no harbingers of death are so feared as the plaguecrafter. These killers wield poisons and disease as lethal weapons alongside the cloaked dagger. Plaguecrafters are unique among rogues for their terrifying magical powers, drawn from necrosis and decay. Able to vanish into toxic fog and dominate the minds of victims they have infected, such rogues harness magical disease as a means of infiltration and murder, wreaking a painful and ugly death upon those who draw their poisonous ire.

subclassFeature.name: Spellcasting
entries: You have learned to cast spells. See the Player's Handbook for the {@book rules on spellcasting|XPHB|7}. The information below details how you use those rules as a Plaguecrafter.

items.name: Cantrips
entries: You know three cantrips: {@spell Poison Spray|XPHB} and two other cantrips of your choice from the Wizard spell list.
Whenever you gain a Rogue level, you can replace one of these cantrips, except {@spell Poison Spray|XPHB}, with another cantrip of your choice from the Wizard spell list.
When you reach Rogue level 10, you learn another Wizard cantrip of your choice.

items.name: Spell Slots
entries: The Plaguecrafter Spellcasting table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

items.name: Prepared Spells of Level 1+
entries: You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose three level 1 spells from the Wizard spell list, two of which must be from the Conjuration and Necromancy schools of magic.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Rogue levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Plaguecrafter Spellcasting table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional spells from the Wizard spell list until the number of spells on your list matches the number on the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 7 Rogue, your list of prepared spells can include six Wizard spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination.

items.name: Changing Your Prepared Spells
entries: Whenever you gain a Rogue level, you can replace one of the spells on your list with another Wizard spell for which you have spell slots.

items.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Wizard spells.

items.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: You can use an {@item Arcane Focus|XPHB} as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your Wizard Spells.

subclassFeature.name: Plaguecrafter
entries: Well accustomed to poisons and disease, you gain the following benefits:

items.name: Plague Resistance
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Poison damage, {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to resist or avoid the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition, and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to nonmagical diseases.

items.name: Seeping Venom
entries: When you damage a creature with a weapon attack, the target takes an additional {@damage 1d6} Poison or Necrotic damage (your choice). Additionally, when you deal Sneak Attack damage to a target, you can choose for the Sneak Attack damage to be Poison or Necrotic.

items.name: Toxic Influence
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB} and {@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) checks made to interact with {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} creatures.

subclassFeature.name: Viral Strike
entries: You gain the following benefits:

items.name: Efficient Poison (2024 Version)
entries: When your Sneak Attack deals Necrotic or Poison damage to a target, you can apply the Poison option of your {@classFeature Cunning Strike|Rogue|XPHB|5|XPHB} without paying the die cost.

items.name: Efficient Poison (2014 Version)
entries: When your Sneak Attack deals Necrotic or Poison damage to a target, that target must make a Constitution saving throw (DC equals 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your Dexterity modifier). On a failed save, the target is {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} for 1 minute. The target can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition on a success.

subclassFeature.name: Viral Touch
entries: You harbor a magical virus that can infect others. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can attempt to infect a creature you are touching with the magical virus. If the creature is unwilling, it makes a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a successful save, the target doesn't realise anything has happened and is immune to your Viral Touch for the next 24 hours.

On a failed save, the target is infected for {@dice 1d6} days, until its body's natural defenses destroy the infection. While the creature is infected, you always know its exact location as long as you are on the same plane of existence, and you can use a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to see through that target's eyes and hear what it hears until the start of your next turn, gaining the benefits of any special senses the target has. During this time, you are {@condition Blinded|XPHB|blind} and {@condition Deafened|XPHB|deaf} with regard to your own senses.

You can have a number of creatures infected in this way up to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of one creature). If another creature fails its save against this feature, you choose which of the previously infected creatures recovers.

subclassFeature.name: Plague Form
entries: You know the {@spell Gaseous Form|XPHB} spell and always have it prepared. If you cast {@spell Gaseous Form|XPHB} targeting yourself, you can modify it in the following ways: your {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} increases to 30 feet and the spell's maximum duration increases to 24 hours. Finally, while under the spell's effects, you can use a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to force a creature whose space you occupy to make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. A {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} creature, or a creature infected by your Viral Touch feature, has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on this saving throw.

On a failed save, the target takes Necrotic damage equal to your Sneak Attack damage dice and is {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} for 1 minute. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage only.

subclassFeature.name: Viral Takeover
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can force a creature that is {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} or infected by your Viral Touch feature that is within 30 feet of you to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, you control that creature on its next turn, determining its actions precisely. If you do not force it to act on that turn, it does nothing.
Once a creature fails its save against this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} unless you expend a level 4+ spell slot to restore your use of it.

subclassFeature.name: College of Weaving
entries: No man chooses his flesh, no bird her feathers, no fish her scales, no bull his hide, no dog her fur. Choice! Fashion is the magic drawn from exercising choice; the very thing that draws the boundary between sentient creatures and the stones at our feet.

Bards of the College of Weaving are maestros of this magic, able to weave the primordial forces of the multiverse alongside cotton and thread. They are master artisans; cobblers, tailors, hatters, and couturiers. A group of adventurers fortunate enough to ally with a Weaving Bard are easy to spot, not only for their spectacular garb and style, but for the mighty, magical power that ripples through the clothes on their back.

subclassFeature.name: Swift Tailor
entries: You gain proficiency with Sewing Tools, and you can add your Charisma modifier to all skill checks you make using them.

In addition, you have the talent to weave subtle abjuration magic into your own clothes. While wearing regular clothing or Light Armour, you can choose one damage type other than Psychic. You resist that damage type. You can change your choice any time you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Grandeured Garb
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can use your Sewing Tools to imbue a number of pieces of armour or clothing you are touching up to your Charisma modifier with shimmering magic. You can imbue a number of additional pieces of armour or clothing in this way equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} by expending a Bardic Inspiration die for each additional one. The items lose their magic when you use this feature again.
An item imbued with magic by this feature gains the following properties:

items: The creature wearing or carrying it can cast {@spell Disguise Self|XPHB} without components. The save DC is equal to your Bard save DC. Once this ability of the item has been used, it cannot be used again unless the magic of the item is restored.

When a creature wearing or carrying it is targeted by an attack, it can use a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to roll a Bardic Inspiration die, and add the result to its AC until the start of its next turn, potentially causing the attack to miss. Once this ability of the item has been used, it cannot be used again unless the magic of the item is restored.
A creature wearing or carrying this item can use your Charisma modifier for its Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB} and {@skill Performance|XPHB}) checks, in place of its own.
You can restore an imbued item's magic by expending a Bardic Inspiration die while touching it.

subclassFeature.name: Weaving Spell List
entries: Bards of this College focus their magical expertise in the schools of transmutation, illusion, and abjuration. When you reach a Bard level specified in the Weaving Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Weaving Spells
rows: {@spell Armor of Agathys|XPHB}, {@spell Disguise Self|XPHB}, {@spell Invisibility|XPHB}, {@spell Mending|XPHB}, {@spell Pass without Trace|XPHB}

subclassFeature.name: Twinned Garments
entries: When you cast a spell from your Weaving Spells table that targets yourself, you can extend its magic to a willing creature within 30 feet of you that bears a piece of clothing or armour imbued with magic from your Grandeured Garb feature. That creature is also targeted by the spell. If the spell requires {@status Concentration|XPHB}, it is tied to your {@status Concentration|XPHB}. If the spell calls for a save DC, it uses yours.
You can use this feature twice, regaining all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Reality Stitcher
entries: The magic you weave into clothing is now so potent it allows the bearer to channel its power. Once per {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, a creature bearing a piece of clothing or armour imbued with magic from your Grandeured Garb feature can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to gain one of the following magical benefits:

items: It gains {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to one damage type of its choice for the next 8 hours.
It gains a +2 bonus to its AC for 10 minutes.
It gains a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to its walking speed and can hover for 1 hour.
It gains a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to its walking speed and can breathe underwater for 8 hours.
Its walking speed increases by 20 feet and it gains a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} equal to its walking speed for 8 hours.
It gains a bonus to all {@skill Stealth|XPHB} checks equal to twice your Charisma modifier for 1 hour.

subclassFeature.name: The Eye Tyrant
entries: The dreams of certain Aberrations can warp reality. These powerful beings, slumbering in hateful tranquility, unravel the fabric of the material world in their sleep. These dreams poison the material world with shards of the supernatural.

Sometimes such dreams manifest in the form of monstrous creatures, and sometimes, they manifest within an individual. You are one such individual, granted aberrant power by a twist of reality wrought on the world by a sleeping aberration.

Often, warlocks of this type are unknown to their tyrannical creators. Some seek out their originator seeking favour and greater power, while others use their magic to destroy the evil that birthed it. Either way, yours is a strength of nightmares; a magic birthed from the dreams of aberrations.

subclassFeature.name: Aberration Ray
entries: When you hit a creature with your {@spell Eldritch Blast|XPHB}, you can choose to infuse the beam with hateful, aberrant power, before you roll damage. If you do, the {@spell Eldritch Blast|XPHB} gains one additional effect, depending on the result on the {@dice d10} damage roll, as shown in the Aberration Ray table.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier, regaining all expended uses upon finishing a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}.

entries.caption: Aberration Ray
rows: Target takes an additional {@damage 1d10} Necrotic damage.
Target makes a Dexterity saving throw. {@actSaveFail} 9 ({@damage 2d8}) Force damage.
Target makes a Constitution saving throw. {@actSaveFail} Target is {@condition Restrained|XPHB} until the start of your next turn.
Target's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is halved until the end of your next turn.
Target makes a Strength saving throw. {@actSaveFail} You move the target up to 20 feet in any direction.
Target makes a Constitution saving throw. {@actSaveFail} Target is {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} and cannot regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} until the end of your next turn.
Target makes a Charisma save. {@actSaveFail} Target is teleported up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space of your choice within 5 feet of another creature.
Target makes a Wisdom saving throw. {@actSaveFail} Target is {@condition Charmed|XPHB} for 1 hour or until it takes damage.
Target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Strength and Dexterity saving throws until the start of its next turn.
Target is {@condition Frightened|XPHB} until the end of its next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Beholding Eyes
entries: The source of your power is an ever-watchful, distrustful aberration. You have a bonus to your {@skill Perception|XPHB} checks equal to your Charisma modifier.
Additionally, you have 60 feet of {@sense Darkvision|XPHB}. If you already have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB}, its range increases by 60 feet.

subclassFeature.name: Eye Tyrant Spells
entries: The magic of your patron ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Warlock level specified in the Eye Tyrant Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Eye Tyrant Spells
rows: {@spell Bane|XPHB}, {@spell Eldritch Blast|XPHB}, {@spell Guiding Bolt|XPHB}, {@spell Hold Person|XPHB}, {@spell Levitate|XPHB}
{@spell Arcane Eye|XPHB}, {@spell Evard's Black Tentacles|XPHB|Black Tentacles}

entries: If you are playing using 2014 rules, you gain your 3rd level Warlock features at 1st level instead, and your spell list grants you the spells {@spell Bane|XPHB}, {@spell Eldritch Blast|XPHB} and {@spell Guiding Bolt|XPHB} at Warlock level 1, rather than level 3.

subclassFeature.name: Gravity Warp
entries: The aberrative magic that birthed your power has begun to alter the capabilities of your physical form. You have a 20-foot {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB}, and you can hover.

subclassFeature.name: Antimagic Beam
entries: The gift that granted you magic also offers the power to take it away from others. You can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to cast {@spell Dispel Magic|XPHB} at 5th level, without a spell slot or components, a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier, regaining all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
When you cast {@spell Dispel Magic|XPHB} and successfully end a spell, you regain one expended use of your Aberration Ray feature.

subclassFeature.name: Minor Reality Warp
entries: The twist of reality that birthed your power now allows you to alter reality around yourself, too. When you or a creature within 30 feet score a 1 on a d20 roll, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to change the result on that d20 to a 20 instead.

subclassFeature.name: Warrior of the Demon Soul
entries: Wherever tyrants are met with a clenched fist; wherever terror is faced with unflinching bravery; wherever, in short, heroes are found, their strength is fueled by an inner fountain of courage. That fountain is the soul - the locus of energy and magic that blooms sustains living things. All great warriors know this, but only the most fervent (and dangerous) view the fountain itself as a resource. To such warriors, the soul is not a well to be drawn from, but a pit of coals to be burned — a destructible resource of vast power.

Monks of the demon soul follow the philosophy of Ashura, the warrior spirit yokai. They battle with inhuman aggression, devouring their own lifeforce to enhance their body with incredible, temporary bursts of supernatural might. The price is high, however, and few who walk this path live to a great age. While warriors who fight in this manner are terrifying to behold, few are evil; most are simply propelled by a passion that supersedes their will to survive. Be it vengeance, a need to protect others, or divine impetus, Monks who follow Ashura's path understand that deadly risk yields spectacular reward, and sacrifice is the fuel of transformation. A demon's soul is still a soul — one that burns, and burns enemies with it.

subclassFeature.name: Soul-Charged
entries: Your Focus Points represent a flowing, rejuvenating force of energy, which you can devour for a burst of demonic power. When you devour a Focus Point, the Focus Point is expended and your maximum Focus Point total is reduced by 1 until the end of your next {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

items.name: Ashura's Fury
entries: When you expend a focus point to use your Flurry of Blows, you can devour it instead. If you do, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on all attack rolls made as part of that Flurry of Blows, and you can make one additional {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} as part of that {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

items.name: Ashura's Counter
entries: When you expend a Focus Point to use your Deflect Attacks feature, you can devour it instead. If you do, the triggering creature automatically fails its Dexterity saving throw to avoid the retaliating damage, and creatures of your choice within 10-feet of it (including the target) take additional damage equal to 1 roll of your martial arts die, as you return the attack with a shockwave of devastating power. This damage is the same type dealt by the attack.

items.name: Ashura's Shadow
entries: When you expend a Focus Point to use your Patient Defence feature, you can devour it instead. If you do, your body also morphs into a translucent haze of shadow until the end of this turn. During that time, you can move through creatures and objects as though they were {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}. Creatures you move through take Necrotic damage equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die, but a creature can only take this damage once per turn. If you end your turn inside a creature or object, you are pushed out to the nearest unoccupied space, taking {@damage 1d10} Force damage for each 5 feet you are pushed.

items.name: Ashura's Duplicity
entries: When you expend a Focus Point to use your Step of the Wind feature, you can devour it instead. If you do, you also cast the spell {@spell Mirror Image|XPHB}, without components, which lasts until the end of your next turn. You can extend its duration by one turn on each of your turns by using Step of the Wind, but it cannot last longer than 1 minute.

subclassFeature.name: Demon's Guile
entries: You can add your Wisdom modifier to Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB} and {@skill Deception|XPHB}) checks.
Additionally, you gain the {@spell Thaumaturgy|XPHB} cantrip if you don't already have it.

subclassFeature.name: Ashura's Hand
entries: As your power grows, so does your ability to trade your focus for bursts of power. You gain the following new ways to devour Focus Points:

items.name: Stunner
entries: When a target fails its save against your Stunning Strike, or you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} against a target, you can devour one Focus Point. If you do, creatures of your choice up to your Wisdom modifier within 30 feet of you are {@condition Frightened|XPHB} until the end of your next turn.

items.name: Ashura's Blast
entries: Once per turn, when you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can devour 1 Focus Point. Doing so allows you to replace any attack made as part of that {@action Attack|XPHB} action with a spherical blast of energy that you hurl towards a creature within 30 feet of you. The target makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking Force damage equal to three rolls of your martial arts dice on a failed save, or half as much on a success.

subclassFeature.name: Ashura's Tenacity
entries: You are immune to the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} and {@condition Frightened|XPHB} conditions, and, while {@status Bloodied|XPHB|bloodied}, whenever you devour a Focus Point, you gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts die.

subclassFeature.name: Form of the Demon
entries: When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, you can channel Ashura's wrath through your body, granting you the following benefits for 1 minute. Once you do so, you cannot use this feature again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, unless you devour 5 Focus Points to restore a use of it (no action required).
Channelling Ashura in this way grants you the following benefits:

items: If there is room and you are smaller than Large, you become Large, along with anything you are wearing. Your reach increases by 5 feet, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength checks and Strength Saving Throws.

At the start of each of your turns while you are {@status Bloodied|XPHB|bloodied}, roll {@dice 1d6} and choose attack rolls or Saving Throws. You have a bonus equal to the result on the {@dice d6} to all rolls of the chosen type until the start of your next turn.

When you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}, the target takes additional damage equal to twice the number of Focus Points you have devoured since the end of your last {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: College of Ceramics
entries: {@i Imbue Effigies with the Might of the Material World}

Most Bards work in ephemera: songs with a final chord, dances that wrap with a bow, stories that end in happily-ever-afters. Bards from the College of Ceramics, however, seek to inspire with a far more permanent source, for while dance, music, and words can echo across generations, only that which is tangible truly endures. An effigy, hewn from earth and magic, is a physical manifestation of the passions, tenacity, and skill of its creator, shaping thoughts across millennia.

Bards who study under the College of Ceramics hold a song in their hearts, much like their peers. Theirs is not a song to be performed before an audience, however, but a vocalised ritual capable of fueling a kiln as it is sung. Bards fuel fire with this magic as they work, sculpting a masterpiece of spellcraft and clay. These effigies carry power, with intricate symbols carved upon them informing the magic they impart. Bards of this order are masterful artisans, infusing life into clay, warding allies with magical effigies, and wielding the implacable power of the material world in their process of creation.

subclassFeature.name: Artisanal Master
entries: You gain proficiency with {@item Potter's Tools|XPHB}, or with another type of {@item Artisan's Tools|XPHB} of your choice if you have it already. You can use Charisma as the ability for all checks you make with the {@item Potter's Tools|XPHB}, and you can use {@item Artisan's Tools|XPHB} you are proficient with as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your Bard spells.

subclassFeature.name: Ceramic Effigy
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can use {@item Potter's Tools|XPHB} to create a number of Tiny effigies equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one), each made in the likeness of a creature within 60 feet of you. Each effigy carries magic, and the creature who shares its likeness can wield its power while carrying it. The power the effigy imparts varies depending on the magical symbols you imprint onto its surface. When you create each effigy, choose from the symbols listed below to inscribe on it. A creature can only gain the benefits of one effigy at a time. The effigies remain magical until they are destroyed, or until you use this feature again to create new ones.

items.name: Etching of Beasts
entries: The effigy is adorned with dramatic renderings of wild animals. The {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} of the creature carrying the effigy increases by 10 feet. While that creature has a Bardic Inspiration die from you, it also has a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with weapons and {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes}.

items.name: Etching of Bloom
entries: The effigy is adorned with an intricate design of blossoming flowers. The creature carrying the effigy has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} and {@condition Frightened|XPHB} conditions. While that creature has a Bardic Inspiration die from you, it also has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to one damage type of your choice (choose when it gains this feature).

items.name: Etching of Ideograms
entries: The effigy is adorned with a multitude of complex symbols. The creature carrying the effigy has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws made to maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB}. While that creature has a Bardic Inspiration die from you, it also has a +1 bonus to its spell attack bonus and the damage rolls of its spells.

subclassFeature.name: Figurine of Power
entries: When you create effigies with your Ceramic Effigy feature, you can also make one Figurine of Power—a special effigy imbued with an etching of sentience. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend a use of Bardic Inspiration to infuse the Figurine of Power with magic, causing it to animate and grow into a living effigy. It appears as a creature made of clay, with the form you sculpted, though its shape has no impact on its abilities. It uses the {@creature Living Effigy|DMSecretWeapon24} stat block, is {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} to you and your allies, and obeys your commands.

In combat, the living effigy shares your {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} count, but it takes its turn immediately after yours. It can move and use its {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} on its own, but the only action it takes on its turn is the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action, unless you take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to command it to take an action in its stat block or some other action. If you are {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}, the living effigy acts on its own and isn't limited to the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action.
When you use your Bardic Inspiration feature, or you animate the living effigy, you can command it as part of the same {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} you used to do so.

Once you animate the living effigy with this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. After 1 hour, or when the living effigy is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it reverts to an inanimate, Tiny figurine.

subclassFeature.name: Figurine of Greater Power
entries: Your {@creature Living Effigy|DMSecretWeapon24} now deals additional damage when it hits with its Rend attack equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum +1 damage).

Additionally, when you cast a spell that targets yourself, you can also affect your {@creature Living Effigy|DMSecretWeapon24} with the spell if the {@creature Living Effigy|DMSecretWeapon24} is within 30 feet of you. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Shattered Effigy
entries: When a creature carrying an effigy created with your Ceramic Effigy feature is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, the creature can choose to destroy the effigy, producing an effect depending on the symbols the effigy bears.

items.name: Etching of Beasts
entries: The creature regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to one roll of your Bardic Inspiration die plus your Bard level, and can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make one weapon attack or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, with a bonus to the attack roll equal to the result on the Bardic Inspiration die.

items.name: Etching of Bloom
entries: The creature regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to three rolls of your Bardic Inspiration die plus your Bard level, it resists all damage until the start of its next turn, and can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to move up to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.

items.name: Etching of Ideograms
entries: The creature regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to one roll of your Bardic Inspiration die plus your Bard level, and can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to cast a cantrip or level 1 spell with a casting time of an action.

subclassFeature.name: Path of Calamity
entries: {@i Channel the Power of Primal Chaos}

Barbarians of the Path of Calamity draw upon the primal chaos that roils beneath the surface and atop the skies of the Material Plane. They embrace the reality that the whims of nature humble all—earthquakes topple the kingdoms, tsunamis decimate fleets, kaiju consume armies. Contrary to what tyrants and kings believe, there are no heights mortals can reach that cannot be torn asunder by natural disaster.

Embracing this chaotic power, a Barbarian's greataxe may be struck by lightning as it falls in a bolt of power, or a javelin may ignite in flame as it blisters through the air. When angered, you are a walking natural disaster, channeling the immeasurable wrath of a calamity.

subclassFeature.name: Calamity Manifestation
entries: Choose a Calamity from which you channel your power. Each Calamity has an associated damage type and a boon you have while it is your chosen Calamity, as specified in the Calamity Effects table. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can change your choice.

entries.caption: Calamity Effects
rows: At the start of each of your turns while your Rage is active, you gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to twice your Rage Damage bonus.

While your Rage is active, your {@variantrule High Jump|XPHB} and {@variantrule Long Jump|XPHB} are up to 15 feet without a running start. If you jump at least 15 feet in any direction, the ground in a 10-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} around the space you land becomes {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} until your Rage ends.

While your Rage is active, whenever you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} or a creature scores a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} against you, you explode in a ball of fire, dealing Fire damage equal to twice your Rage Damage bonus to each other creature within 10 feet of you. Once this effect has triggered, it can't trigger again until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Disaster Strike
entries: When you hit a creature with a Melee weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} while your Rage is active, you can empower the attack with cataclysmic power. The target of the attack takes extra damage of the type associated with your chosen Calamity, and you create an additional effect based on your chosen Calamity, as detailed below. To determine the extra damage, roll a number of d8s equal to your Rage Damage bonus, and add them together.

You can use this feature twice, but only once per use of Rage, and you regain all expended uses of it when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can use this feature three times before a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} starting at Barbarian level 9 and four times before a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} starting at Barbarian level 16.

items.name: Blizzard
entries: Layers of ice shield you and others from damage. You can distribute {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} to creatures of your choice within 30 feet of yourself, which can include you. The total number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} is equal to the extra Cold damage of your Disaster Strike.

items.name: Earthquake
entries: The land shakes with your impact. Creatures of your choice within 30 feet of you that are on ground that is {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} fall {@condition Prone|XPHB}.

items.name: Volcano
entries: Cooled magma coats your body in a brittle, but resilient, shield. You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to all damage for 1 minute or until you are hit by an attack roll, and the first attack roll that hits you is a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Cataclysmic Aura
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to the damage type associated with your chosen Calamity.

In addition, while your Rage is active, chaotic energy flows in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} that originates from you. The aura's effects depend on your chosen Calamity, as detailed below.

items.name: Blizzard
entries: Once per turn, when an ally of yours that has {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} is hit by a melee attack while in the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}, the blizzard retaliates. The attacker takes Cold damage equal to your Rage Damage bonus.

items.name: Earthquake
entries: While in the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}, {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} doesn't cost you or your allies extra movement.

items.name: Volcano
entries: When you or an ally of yours in the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} rolls a 1 on the d20 for a saving throw, you explode in a ball of flames, as per your Calamity Manifestation feature.

subclassFeature.name: Invoke Calamity
entries: Your connection with the elemental chaos allows you to force calamities onto others. When a creature that you can see within the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} of your Cataclysmic Aura makes an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the attack roll.

If the attack misses, the target of the attack can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make an attack with a Melee weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} against the attacker. On a hit, the attack deals extra damage equal to half your Barbarian level. The damage is of the type associated with your chosen Calamity.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Disaster Incarnate
entries: When you activate your Rage or as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} while it's active, you can expend a use of your Rage to transcend into a maelstrom of elemental power, granting you the following benefits until your Rage ends. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

items.name: Damage Immunity
entries: You have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the damage type associated with your chosen Calamity.

items.name: Never-Ending Calamity
entries: When you activate this feature, you regain one expended use of your Disaster Strike.

items.name: Shared Resistance
entries: Allies in the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} of your Cataclysmic Aura have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to the damage type associated with your chosen Calamity.

items.name: Shifting Calamity
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can change your chosen Calamity to another one from your Calamity Manifestation feature.

subclassFeature.name: Origami
entries: The art of binding magic to paper is as ancient as spellcasting itself, but some Wizards see potential beyond the traditional spell scroll. These mavericks treat parchment as more than a two-dimensional canvas upon which magic is inscribed, understanding it as a three-dimensional object and conduit of power.

Such wizards are masters of origami, able to fold spell-infused paper to magnify the magic contained within. This meticulous artform produces spectacular results, with sentient, paper-craft allies and a spellbook folded into fortified paper armour among the jealously guarded weapons of spellcasters who master this path.

subclassFeature.name: Paper Companion
entries: Over the course of a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you are able to fold and infuse a piece of parchment with potent magic. Choose a spell you can cast with a casting time of one action, of a level no higher than your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, to infuse into the parchment. You then fold that parchment into a three dimensional form—common shapes are that of cranes, swans, dragons, boats, or airships. The folded parchment is animated by your magic, becoming a sentient companion, which uses the {@creature Paper Companion|DMSecretWeapon24} stat block.

In combat, the Paper Companion shares your {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} count, but it takes its turn immediately after yours. It can move and use its {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} on its own, but the only action it takes on its turn is the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action, unless you take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to command it to take an action in its stat block or some other action. If you are {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}, the paper companion acts on its own and isn't limited to the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action.

If your paper companion falls to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you can expend a spell slot to perform a 10-minute ritual, after which time it reanimates at full {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. You can only have one Paper Companion at a time, and creating a new one destroys the first.

subclassFeature.name: Spellbook Armour
entries: Your talents allow you to construct your spellbook as magical, paper armour you can wear, which fortifies you against harm. It is considered Light Armour that you are proficient with, you can use it as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your Wizard spells, and while wearing it, you can calculate your AC as 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Intelligence modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Origami Specialist
entries: You have proficiency in the {@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB} skill, and time spent to craft {@item Spell Scroll|XPHB|spell scrolls} is halved for you.

subclassFeature.name: Origami Armour
entries: The magic within your spellbook armour has grown powerful enough to manifest magical properties. While wearing it, you resist damage from spells, and at the start of your turn, you can choose to grant yourself a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} or {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to your walking speed for 1 minute.
Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, unless you expend a spell slot of 3rd level or higher to do so.

subclassFeature.name: Infused Companion
entries: Your paper companion can now draw power directly from the spell you infuse into its form. When it hits a creature with an attack, it delivers a bonus effect depending on the school of magic the infused spell is from.

items.name: Abjuration
entries: The companion or a willing creature within 15 feet of it gains a +2 bonus to its AC until the start of the companion's next turn.

items.name: Conjuration
entries: The companion or a willing creature within 15 feet of it can use its {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to teleport up to 15 feet to an unoccupied space it can see.

items.name: Divination
entries: The companion or a willing creature within 15 feet of it can add {@dice 1d6} to the next saving throw it makes before the start of its next turn.

items.name: Enchantment
entries: The target has a {@dice 1d4} penalty to the next saving throw it makes before the start of its next turn.

items.name: Evocation
entries: The target takes an additional {@damage 2d10} Force damage.

items.name: Illusion
entries: The companion or a willing creature within 15 feet turns {@condition Invisible|XPHB} until the start of the companion's next turn. This invisibility ends early if the creature makes an attack, casts a spell, or forces a saving throw.

items.name: Necromancy
entries: The companion or a willing creature within 15 feet regains {@dice 2d10} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

items.name: Transmutation
entries: The target's weight is magnified eightfold until the start of the companion's next turn. While under this effect, its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by half, and it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Dexterity saving throws.

subclassFeature.name: Spell Fold
entries: Your prodigious talent for folding spell scrolls manifests in an ability to fold magic itself. When you cast a non-concentration spell using a spell slot at least three levels higher than that spell's lowest level, you can choose to concentrate on it. As an action on your next turn, you can end your {@status Concentration|XPHB}, recasting that spell at its lowest level without expending a spell slot.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier, regaining all expended uses upon finishing a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Path of the Juggernaut
entries: Fury is most dangerous untethered. An unshackled body is the rage-fueled machine of the barbarian warrior, but juggernauts train ceaselessly to wield that primal power in a cage of iron and steel. Heavily armoured barbarians are rare and terrifying. Each juggernaut is a battering ram, able to stride undaunted through hailing arrows and clashing swords, and few warriors are so deadly in one-on-one combat. A charging juggernaut is a union of aggression and fortification that is nigh-unstoppable.

Notably, juggernauts observed across all realms are found in collectives, adventuring parties, and armies at a staggeringly higher rate than any other type of barbarian. Lone-wolf juggernauts are unheard of - perhaps due in part to their reliance on expert ironsmiths. Others suggest that the philosophy of the juggernaut, an iconoclast who unites the fury of the wild with the calculated precision of the smith, leads one to embrace connection and solidarity on a path few other barbarians tread.

subclassFeature.name: Stalwart Champion
entries: When you hit a creature with a weapon attack roll, you can invoke a binding challenge to battle. The target of your attack makes a Wisdom saving throw (DC = 8 + your Strength modifier + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}). On a failed save, they are compelled to meet your onslaught face-to-face. For the next minute, the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against creatures other than you. This effect ends early if you make an attack roll against a creature other than the target. On a successful save, they are instead {@condition Frightened|XPHB} of you until the start of your next turn.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Strength modifier, regaining one expended use upon finishing a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, and all expended uses upon finishing a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Heavily Armoured
entries: You have proficiency with {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB} and Heavy Armour. Additionally, your Barbarian class features ignore any restrictions imposed by wearing Heavy Armour, except for Unarmored Defense.

subclassFeature.name: Modified Armour
entries: Over the course of a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can modify your Heavy Armour. Choose two of the following modifications to apply. These modifications remain until you modify your armour again. Your armour can only hold a maximum of two modifications from this feature at a time.

items.name: Critical Reinforcement
entries: Any {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} against you becomes a normal hit.

items.name: Ergonomic Flight Fit
entries: If you are a species that has an innate {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB|flying speed}, you can fly without restriction while wearing this armour.

items.name: Spiked Gauntlets
entries: You can roll {@dice 1d10} in place of the normal damage for your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes}, which deal Piercing damage on a hit. Additionally, if you hit a target with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can push them up to 10 feet away from you.

items.name: Spiked Armour
entries: When a creature hits you with a melee attack, it takes {@damage 1d4} Piercing damage.

items.name: Superheavy
entries: You can add a +10 to {@variantrule Saving Throw|XPHB|Saving Throws} and {@variantrule Ability Check|XPHB|Ability Checks} made to avoid being knocked {@condition Prone|XPHB} or moved against your will.

items.name: Wetsuit
