entries.name: Natural Artisan
entries: You gain proficiency with three types of tools of your choice.

entries.name: Undermin's Aid
entries: In place of one attack when you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can take the {@action Help|XPHB} action.

entries.name: Undermin's Courage
entries: As long as at least one of your allies is within 5 feet of you, you and your allies within 5 feet of you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} and {@condition Frightened|XPHB} conditions.

entries.name: Undermin's Sacrifice
entries: When a creature within your reach is hit by an attack with a weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to be hit by the attack instead.

entries.name: Languages
entries: Common and one other you and your GM agree is appropriate for your character.

race.name: Accursed One
entries: You can choose this lineage at character creation, or adopt this lineage in response to an event that places a curse upon you in your story. Whichever you choose, select a species as normal, and then replace all your species traits with those from this lineage, except for Creature Type, Size, and Speed. If your tale unfolds in such a manner that removes this curse, you can choose to revert to your original species, or retain this lineage and power.

entries.name: Player Tip!
entries: The loss of your old species traits can form a powerful part of your story and identity. In the case of a dragonborn, for example, consider how and why your breath weapon and damage resistance has been taken by the curse; how does this change impact you and your goals? Does it manifest as a physical transformation, or is the change purely internal? Do you cling to your old identity and kin, despite the curse, or embrace a new identity and path forged by your newfound power?

entries.name: Accursed Knowledge
entries: You know {@language Deep Speech|XPHB}. Additionally, whenever you fail an {@skill Arcana|XPHB}, {@skill History|XPHB}, {@skill Medicine|XPHB}, {@skill Nature|XPHB}, {@skill Religion|XPHB}, or {@skill Survival|XPHB} check, you can expend {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB} up to a number equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. Roll them and add the result to your check, potentially turning the failure into a success.

entries.name: Accursed Power
entries: You have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to one condition of your choice from among the following: {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB}, {@condition Frightened|XPHB}, or {@condition Stunned|XPHB}.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Grim Transformation
entries: Your curse slumbers within you, actualising itself in times of stress. Choose one Grim Transformation from among Bloodpact, Frenzied, and Soulkeeper. Your curse can actualise twice, regaining all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Bloodpact
entries: When you become {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, your curse actualises for 1 minute or until you end your turn while no longer {@status Bloodied|XPHB}. While actualised, your curse imparts the following effects:

items: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Poison damage and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.

The first time each turn you take damage, you expend one of your {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}, roll it, add your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and reduce the damage by the result. If you have no unexpended {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}, take 2 points of Force damage instead.

entries.name: Frenzy
entries: When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, your curse actualises for 1 minute or until you have dealt a total amount of damage equal to ten times your character level. While actualised, your curse imparts the following effects:

items: Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 feet.

The first time each turn you deal damage to a creature, expend one of your {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}, roll it, and add the result to the damage dealt. If you have no unexpended {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}, take 2 points of Necrotic damage instead.

entries.name: Soulkeeper
entries: When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you falls to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, your curse actualises for 1 minute or until another creature you can see within 30 feet of you falls to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. While actualised, your curse imparts the following effects.

items: At the start of each of your turns, if a creature you are fighting is within 120 feet of you, expend one of your {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB} and roll it. You gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the result. If you have no unexpended {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}, take 2 points of Psychic damage instead.

While you have {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}, you have a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and can hover, and you can move through creatures and objects as if they were {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}. If you end your turn inside a creature or object, you are shunted back to the last unoccupied space you occupied.

entries.name: Optional Rule: Myriad Curse
entries: At the GMs discretion, you can add an element of chaos to your curse. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, roll {@dice 1d6}. Your Grim Transformation changes to Bloodpact on a 1-2, Frenzy on a 3-4, and Soulkeeper on a 5-6.

items.name: Grim Transformation (Bloodpact)
entries: Your curse slumbers within you, actualising itself in times of stress. Your curse can actualise twice, regaining all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

When you become {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, your curse actualises for 1 minute or until you end your turn while no longer {@status Bloodied|XPHB}. While actualised, your curse imparts the following effects:

items: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Poison damage and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.

The first time each turn you take damage, you expend one of your {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}, roll it, add your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and reduce the damage by the result. If you have no unexpended {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}, take 2 points of Force damage instead.

When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, your curse actualises for 1 minute or until you have dealt a total amount of damage equal to ten times your character level. While actualised, your curse imparts the following effects:

items: Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 feet.

The first time each turn you deal damage to a creature, expend one of your {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}, roll it, and add the result to the damage dealt. If you have no unexpended {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}, take 2 points of Necrotic damage instead.

When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you falls to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, your curse actualises for 1 minute or until another creature you can see within 30 feet of you falls to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. While actualised, your curse imparts the following effects:

items: At the start of each of your turns, if a creature you are fighting is within 120 feet of you, expend one of your {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB} and roll it. You gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the result. If you have no unexpended {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}, take 2 points of Psychic damage instead.

While you have {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}, you have a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and can hover, and you can move through creatures and objects as if they were {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}. If you end your turn inside a creature or object, you are shunted back to the last unoccupied space you occupied.

raceFluff.name: Omenix

entries: The Gods are, by and large, intensely prideful bastards, even the very nice ones. It's something you have to get used to in our line of work. Hells, if you'd built a continent or crafted your own race, you'd probably enjoy the smell of your own farts too. That's how we know just how good the omenix are. When you get down to it, they're the only species that we know for sure the Gods love to watch.

The omenix are a towering avian species native to the wetlands of Avestros, known across the lands for their delicate grace and stunning plumage. Legends say that the Gods enjoyed watching the omenix dance so much they blessed them with the gift of flame, causing omenix wings to blaze crimson and trail embers when in motion. While it is undeniable the omenix are regarded as an objectively attractive species, and naturally move and balance well, it is equally true their weight and height make them gawky and comical fliers. With a reputation for beauty comes a certain degree of pride, and many omenix prefer to avoid flying while in public, though they are capable of brief stints in the air at a pinch.

A reputation for beauty also invites suppositions of ditziness, and while many omenix do have a habit of losing the thread of a conversation mid-sentence, there is no evidence to suggest they are less intelligent than any other sentient folk. Omenix are not stupid, they simply have an intense focus that shifts very quickly. Even when standing still, they are a pleasure to watch, with their long necks darting back and forth and their heads rotating quizzically as they systematically examine every object and creature in sight.

raceFluff.name: Mob-mob
entries: The Vortex Sea is a body of ferocious, frothing, and murderous water off the southern coast of Avestros. Countless sailors have lost their lives attempting to navigate its tides, but not all who dwell below the surface of these evil waters are wicked. Mob-mobs are the most populous water dwelling species in Avestros - a statistic made all the more impressive considering they live exclusively in the Vortex Sea. Jovial folk, mob-mobs resemble very large jellyfish; their heads are crowned with a bulbous bell, and they have four long limbs which trail gracefully behind them in water, and clumsily support them on land.

Mob-mobs are well regarded by almost all other species as aimable, cheerful, and kind; practically all voyages across the Vortex Sea that succeed do so only due to mob-mob intervention. Despite a pleasant reputation, particularly among seafaring folk, mob-mobs are fierce hunters. Their bioluminescent bulb lures prey close, before they strike in a whirlwind of raking limbs. Their arms are ridged with barbs that deliver a stinging poison on contact, which they use to subdue prey before devouring it. Fortunately, mob-mobs prefer a diet of fish and mollusks while below water, and small mammals if hunting on land. Even close allies are known to be wary of the mob-mob's poison, and there is great wisdom to the common Avestrosian saying: "Everyone loves a mob-mob, but nobody wants to shake their hand."

raceFluff.name: Avestrosian Goblin
entries: Goblins are among the most populous species in the multiverse, sprawling across countless worlds and planes of existence. Although they all share ancestry and key physical traits, every world is a canvas that paints a different culture of goblin, with unique habits and cultures.

In Avestros, goblins are renowned for their brazen courage in battle. Fierce and sprightly warriors, they prefer to tackle any given problem head on; be it charging a rampaging dragon or finishing a particularly spicy gumbo, no self-respecting goblin will shy away from the task at hand. They apply the same frenetic gusto to all things, most notably the arts of crafting and architecture. Goblins have a crafting culture on par with dwarves and gnomes, with a reputation for constructing excellent weapons, armour, and vehicles at a terrific pace from meagre, scavenged materials. Goblins on Avestros enjoy a degree of respect that is regrettably denied to goblins on many other planes. Here, they are well regarded, celebrated, and can be found living side by side with other species in all major settlements across the continent.

raceFluff.name: Molimpodsea
entries: Though few in number and small in stature, the molimpodsea stand as titans in economic trade and politics across all of Avestros for a simple reason: they are the guardians, overseers, and occasional plunderers of the vicious Vortex Sea. Any trade that hopes to make it from the south to the north must either travel through endless miles of mountains, swamps, and forests, or leave via the southern ports and cross the deadly waters over which molimpodsea claim dominion. Though friendlier species, like the mob-mobs, will aid struggling cargo ships to save the souls on board, the molimpodsea are significantly more mercenary. They control the shipping lanes across the Vortex Sea, and sell the safest routes to the highest bidder. By taking a tax on all incoming shipments at the guarantee of safe passage, the molimpodsea ensure themselves a steady supply of wealth and a miserable reputation among other species.

Not all molimpodsea are so rapacious, however. Some aid sailors willingly and without charge to minimise lives lost to the treacherous deep, and other campaign for an end to controlled trade and free passage for all over the Vortex Sea. Many individuals who aspire to be more than glorified pirates seek out adventure for themselves, often putting their superlative aquatic skills to good use as heroes for hire up and down the Avestosian coastline. The molimpodsea who remain endure strained relationships with most other peoples. The primary exception is the mob-mobs, with whom the typical molimpodsea shares little in character, but a great deal in culture and mutual respect. As unlikely a pairing as it might seem, few separate groups of people share bonds stronger than these two seafaring species; perhaps the crushing ferocity of the cruelest biome known to Avestos is responsible for forging a fellowship so deep and unshakable between these unlikely allies.

raceFluff.name: Avestrosian Elf
entries: Elves are just like everybody else, only more so.

Avestrosian elves can be found in every major settlement across the continent - from the Oroborus Jungle to depths of the Vortex Sea. Well known for their seemingly endless fervor and enthusiasm, they often find work as miners, farmers, and warriors; rarely will one find an elf in an occupation that demands a lot of sitting still. Even sleeping still is near impossible for elves native to Avestros - ever electrified with energy, they retain the ability to move and undertake simple tasks while unconscious, leading many to pick up extra work as talented artists and entertainers while sleeping.

It is far from unheard of for an Avestrosian elf to be a well regarded performer by night and unaware of their talents by day. As such, it's customary for Avestrosian elves to attempt feats of extreme acrobatics or musical virtuosity every few years, in the off chance their sleeping self has mastered the art without their knowledge.

raceFluff.name: Powgarfoot
entries: Making their home in the temperate, mountainous forests of Avestros, Powgarfoot are an ursine race of humanoids. Hulking, sociable, and independent, they typically prefer to keep out of conflict, unfettered by the politics and warfare of other species. All are welcome in a Powgarfoot village - free to stay as long as they wish and free to take as much food as they desire.

Powgarfoot find enormous pleasure in food; eating, cooking, sharing, and storing it are acts of delight and great cultural significance. All events, be they funerals, weddings, birthdays, weekends, or weekdays, are marked with a great feast. Their cuisine is famous across the land as delicious and eclectic - there is no dish a Powgarfoot will not sample, no person with whom a Powgarfoot will not share, and very few meals they will not enjoy.

raceFluff.name: Heartling
entries: Few among the mighty and powerful are content to share power, but needs must in a world of constant danger and treachery. For many an archlich or necromancer, the answer to such problems lies in the creation of a Heartling, a magical Construct with the power to learn, serve, and kill in defence of their master. Heartlings are no mere puppet, they are a fully realised being capable of independence and free will. Creating such life requires a towering investment of magical power, and no small amount of risk, but the rewards are well worth it.

Able to grow and learn, Heartlings are invaluable allies to those who create them; a cut far above the easily corrupted allegiances of cultists or the mindless servitude of Undead. Many act as their master's chief lieutenants and overseers, handling matters as varied as defense, housekeeping, and trade. In rare cases where a creator dies but a Heartling lives on, they are free to pursue their own ends. While it is true that most Heartlings pursue the path of evil in their master's name, some seek out fortune through fellowship, acting as dark guardians and distant allies to mortal folk.

raceFluff.name: Avestrosian Dwarf
entries: The dwarves of Avestros are as distant from their multiversal cousins in environment as they are united in spirit. Skybound beings, Avestrosian dwarves walk upon clouds and mine the magical materials of the stratosphere, building castles, cities, and palaces many miles above the ground. Dwarves native to these lands can be divided into two lineages: the skyhoppers and the terrestrial.

Terrestrial dwarves prefer to spend time on the ground as well as in the air - trading enthusiastically with other land-bound species and claiming territories atop high mountains and peaks as well as among the clouds. Much of their architecture reflects the flowing, spiraling clouds they mine.

Skyhopper dwarves prefer to remain in the heavens as much as possible, caring very little for the toings and froings of beings on the ground. Typically, skyhoppers converse with ground folk only through their terrestrial cousins or other flying species, but have been known to descend in moments of great catastrophe or importance. By and large, however, the affairs of the land are figuratively (and quite literally) beneath their notice.

raceFluff.name: Mimikin
entries: Of all the curiosities that crawl from the ocean deep or fall from the heavens high, settle on land, and declare themselves sovereign, none are so peculiar as the mimikin - humanoids who trace mimic blood in their ancestry. Shapeshifters are not unheard of in Avestros, but the mimikin draw distinction from changelings and doppelgangers for their ability to unerringly borrow the forms of inanimate objects. Their true shape is similar to that of a typical human, with a waxy sheen to their skin and pitch black eyes and hair. This form is rarely seen, however, as typically mimikin roam the lands in a preferred skin, be it elf, human, goblin, or wheelbarrow.

The origin of the mimikin is a mystery even to themselves - certainly, they do not trace their lineage to couplings between humanoid species and mimics. Most likely, they are the result of technomagical experimentation or explosive Wild Magic. Mimikin don't have much in the way of a shared culture; they adopt the forms, customs, and traditions of the communities in which they are born.

raceFluff.name: Epta
entries: The locus of all druidic power lies in the earth, and sometimes, it stands up and walks around. In areas where ancient leylines of magic converge, and the crusty, outer shell of our world becomes electrified with power, its only exhaust is sentience. This is how epta are born.

Epta are mounds of living rocks, said to be the first (and only naturally occuring) golems. The size and shape of individual epta vary, but all bear a flat faced, heptahedron head - a seven-sided geometrical rock with no natural cavity, dent, or furrow. Despite possessing no mouth, nose, ears, or internal organs, epta can see, speak, hear, smell, and feel like any other humanoid - theirs is simply a sentience born of magic over biology.

Despite lacking a typical "face", epta are easy to discern from one another. The rivers of magic that grant them life run over their body in a glowing array of geometrical lines. On some epta, these lines glow, on others they are dull; some bear very few lines, and other carry thousands. Every epta's body is different, in much the same way fingerprints are unique among humans. Many societies that revere druidic magic have adopted epta's geometric markings into their own culture in the form of tattoos and decorative art.

The most striking element of the epta is their minds. Innate mathematical and technological virtuosos, epta delight in exploration of the natural world through a scientific lens. They are enamored by the patterns, statistics, and calculus that can be used to understand living systems — despite being born from magic, and innately magical beings, most seem drawn to a wholly scientific exploration of the world around them. Coupled with their titanic natural lifespan, they are often revered as great historians, scientists, wizards, and artificers.

raceFluff.name: Einherjar
entries: The life of a noble warrior is one of danger and bravery. The death of such a warrior is little different. Einherjar are spirits of warriors who fell in battle, restored to an undead existence by a mighty, divine influence. These are not the ghosts of legend - foul undead, clanking chains, wails, moans, groans, and gutteral, gurgling cries - you will not find such fairy tale phantoms among the einherjar.

They are a warrior people, sentient and articulate as any Humanoid. They usually share the motivations and values they held in life, although in some cases, einherjar are returned to the material realms under impetus from a divine being, which imparts new purpose. In all cases, every einherjar is a warrior at heart, undaunted by pain and danger. Only those deemed worthy of resurrection can become an einherjar, though one's "worthiness" is subject to the whims of the divine being that restores their spirit to life. Though they might be good or evil, as might any other sentient being, there are no cowards among the einherjar.

raceFluff.name: Vidjamare
entries: When the Ancient Beings first created life, they drew from the raw, primordial material of the universe. The secrets of biogenesis were guarded closely by these Gods, with the power to birth consciousness from crude matter deemed too dangerous to fall into the hands of "lesser" deities. However, one such "lesser" God desired above all else to create a people of its own. Possessing not the strength to challenge the Ancient Beings, nor the knowledge to construct life from nothing, the God was wracked with endless, fruitless longing. Across countless eons it watched in lonely envy as the first creatures built lives and communities on the first worlds, ever dreaming of a family of its own. So it dreamed and dreamed, and its desperate hope for children grew and grew, until one day, the dreams burst through the veil of reality. This is how the vidjamare were born - beings manifested from the dream of the Lonely God.

The truth to this tale is as unprovable as any story of creation, but the indisputable truth is that Vidjamare are a people born from dreams. Vidjamare are tied to the realm of sleep — at home in slumber, they are able to live a life every bit as real in dreams as they do while awake. They possess the power to visit willing creature's dreams while they rest, often bringing comfort and driving off nightmares. They reproduce by connecting with another of their kind while asleep, and together dreaming of a child. When the vidjamere awake, both hold a new, delicate life in their arms.

Other species view vidjamere with reverence, in part due to their scarcity and in part due to their ability to commune with others through dreams regardless of distance, borders, and language. Their unique abilities make vidjamere valued negotiators and messengers, able to share messages across the world as swiftly as it takes to fall asleep, and communicate with distant communities without the risk of travel or hostility. Though travel through the medium of sleep is sufficient for many vidjamere, some are satisfied only by the promise of exploring the world materially. To such vidjamere, the path of the adventurer is common.

raceFluff.name: Hakkai

entries: What reason have we not to be brave in the face of battle? There are far worse fates than death. Fear them, child.

As a peeking sun crests the horizon, the verdance of the Eiravam Meadows thrums with life and dawn. The most numerous creatures here are the hakkai, swine-folk guardians of all burgeoning life in a land of eternal, delicate spring. Theirs is a culture of detached custodianship, a duty to ward against all interlopers who would exploit and slaughter the innocents of Eiravam. It is a duty painfully earned.

Hakkai were among the first peoples, and the first to fall under Humanoids' destructive obsession with hierarchy and control. For millenia, hakkai were enslaved, tortured, and slaughtered at the whim and pleasure of other species. Only upon escaping did the hakkai find a destiny to claim their own, and cultivate a land of peace. Here, in Eiravam, they remain, and defend others against the fate that befell their ancestors with extreme force. Few hakkai are known to leave this place, harbouring a justified mistrust of other peoples.

It is said that the hakkai are blessed with a divine, haunting ward, perceptible only to evildoers. To such creatures, the hakkai are accompanied by a wrathful vortex of gas that lunges and claws and spirals. As it grasps and ensnares, it torments the hateful with the distant, spectral screams of innocents from ages past. To most, the hakkai are a rare symbol of self determinism, and to the evil, there is nothing more terrifying.

entries.name: Additional Hakkai Traits
entries: In addition to the traits already mentioned, Hakkai have the following traits when using the 2014 version of the rules.

entries.name: Ability Score Increase
entries: Your Strength score increases by 1, and your Intelligence score increases by 2.

entries.name: Languages
entries: You can speak, read, and write {@language Common}.

raceFluff.name: Geist
entries: The haunting, choking mists of Wadebottom Bay are home to more than strangling vines and babbling bogs. Here, in the cradle of necromantic ley line scars left in the wake of the Undying Wars, fallen warriors find no path beyond mortality. Geist is the name given to any who dies in Wadebottom Bay, upon rising again as a translucent, physical shade tethered to the material world. Geists are as varied as any other species, retaining the memories, personality, and visage they held in life, and as such have little in the way of shared culture and tradition. Most adopt the Bay's gift of unlife as a chance to stride onward, continuing on their journey forever changed, but the same. Others see the transformation from living being to undead as a true rebirth, abandoning all ties to the old and embracing a new outlook and quest. In any case, geists are truly their own species, with the power granted by Wadebottom's curse drowning any prior abilities, and filling the void with sinister magic of its own.

entries.name: Additional Geist Traits
entries: In addition to the traits already mentioned, Hakkai have the following traits when using the 2014 version of the rules.

entries.name: Ability Score Increase

raceFluff.name: Vindivar
entries: Many compassionate gods create life in their own image, but what happens when a malevolent god does the same? This is the tale of the vindivar, a species of Humanoids birthed by the hand of a tyrannical deity, a legion of beings crafted to sow hate and discord across all of creation, and given the cruel power to do so.

However, the will of life is harder to tame than even the mightiest of gods recognise, and the vindivar were born not as mindless servants of evil, but independent beings capable of reason and choice. The influence of their dark creator eternally whispers at the back of every vindivar's mind, but some resist. Granted, many vindivar surrender to these impulses, acting out the machinations of their creator, but those that fight resist the powers that would sway them to wickedness.

Such vindivar are dedicated to expunging evil where they see it. They harbor the ultimate aim of slaying the god that created them. Doing so will free their brothers and sisters of its vile influence forever, and such vindivar dream of a world where every newborn is free to think and feel without the spectre of another's hatred and ambition clouding their heart.

The life of a vindivar is hard. The battle for freedom over one's mind is constant, and it can never truly be won until the vindivar's creator god is slain. It may take millenia, but brave vindivar gladly take up the challenge. The freedom to live with joy and love is worth fighting for.

raceFluff.name: Dukaput
entries: The sprawling Ouroboros Jungle that crests our crimson globe is home to countless fascinating creatures, but none so unusual as the dukaput—perhaps the most curious sapient species ever recorded. Dukaput are double-headed humanoids, possessing a bipedal body crowned with a twin neck and heads. Much like elves, dwarves, and humans, the dukaput brain is split into two hemispheres. In this fascinating case, each hemisphere is housed in a separate cranium.

Dukaput are born perfectly mirrored down their spine, and remain identical to the millimeter from arm to leg to head as they grow. Their brains are two halves of a single whole — each individual has one name and one mind, but possessing two heads grants many advantages. Dukaput are able to sing in harmony with themselves, keep watch while sleeping, and communicate telepathically. It is this telepathic connection that enables each half of the brain to remain in synchronicity with the other, and also grants the dukaput a measure of innate magical power.

Life in the Ouroboros Jungle is hard, and often demands a hard attitude from those who call it home. Dukaput society reflects their perfectly mirrored bodies; an intensely hierarchical social structure of upper and lower class. Those in the upper class have everything the Jungle can provide, maintaining a luxurious lifestyle of gluttony and excess. Those in the lower strata of dukaput life struggle daily for food and shelter, with the majority of their labour's fruits stolen by the dukaput above them. Upper dukaput almost never leave the Ouroboros Jungle, but the bravest among the lower dukaput who resist the hierarchy vanish into the darkness of the Jungle, setting out to carve a life for themselves as adventurers or hermits. It is a life of isolation and danger, but it is a life that is lived free.

raceFluff.name: Undermin
entries: Undermin are a sapient species crafted by Zulth, the Schemer in millenia past to serve as the perfect lackeys. The earliest undermin were unambitious and eager to aid their master, making for effective albeit bumbling minions to the lich prince.

They were set to work toiling in mines across the multiverse in pursuit of valuable gems and precious resources Zuth might use in his experiments. Upon Zulth's destruction, the undermin were freed from his dark control, and having long since spread across all creation, were left to their own devices.

Today, undermin are independent, but some of the traits they were crafted to exemplify remain. They operate best in groups, happiest when finding fulfillment on large-scale, collaborative endeavors. Undermin cities are spectacular—endless carnivals of stunning architecture and ambitious expansion that spread above and below ground. Undermin love the earth and mining through it, often doing so for pleasure rather than profit, content to leave precious gems and gold in the ground as stunning features in their twisting, labyrinthine metropolises.

Though Zulth was evil, undermin themselves have no natural inclination toward any alignment. Many undermin travel the world seeking heroes to serve, but some stumble into the role of hero themselves, forging a new destiny beyond the role of minion assigned to them by their cruel creator.

raceFluff.name: Accursed One
entries: In a multiverse of crackling magic and tyrannical monsters, there are countless poor souls who fall victim to vengeful fury. It may be that a mistake in your past earned you the ire of a powerful demon. Perhaps a malevolent object came into your possession, or your curse could be hereditary, passed across generations for an ancestor's crime that few recall. No matter its origin, yours is a path forever transformed by a curse that warps your body and soul, granting you power at a terrible cost.

entries: The manifested nightmare's appearance, creature type, and the damage type of its attacks are determined by the worst nightmares of the being that conjured it. For example, a creature afraid of dragons might give the nightmare the shape of a dragon, the Dragon creature type, and Fire damage for its attacks. A GM can flavour the nightmare's attacks to suit the form it has been given.

trait.name: Vicious
entries: The manifested nightmare has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against {@condition Frightened|XPHB} creatures.

trait.name: Worst Nightmare
entries: The creature that conjured the manifested nightmare is {@condition Frightened|XPHB} of it.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The manifested nightmare makes two attacks.

action.name: Nightmare Slash
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 6} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}13 ({@damage 2d8 + 4}) damage.

action.name: Nightmare Bolt
entries: {@atk rw} {@hit 6} to hit, range 30/90 ft., one target. {@h}11 ({@damage 1d12 + 4}) damage.

trait.name: Aura of Despair
entries: While the nightmare is {@variantrule Bloodied|XPHB|bloodied}, other creatures within 30 feet of it have a -6 penalty to saving throws.

trait.name: Aura of Fear
entries: A creature that starts its turn within 30 feet of the nightmare must succeed on a {@dc 17} Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition Frightened|XPHB} of the nightmare until the start of its next turn.

trait.name: Vicious
entries: The Manifested Nightmare (Compound) has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against {@condition Frightened|XPHB} creatures.

action.name: Multiattack

action.name: Razor Quill Arrow

trait.name: Magic Staff
entries: The Carnie Acrobat carries a Lesser Quarterstaff of the Acrobat, granting them {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|XPHB}) checks and a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls (included in the attack).

action.name: Slam

trait.name: Great Showman! (2/Day)
entries: If Enriquo scores a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} on his turn, he can take an additional action this turn.

trait.name: Manipulator
entries: When Enriquo makes a Flaming Whip attack, one creature he can see within 60 feet must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition Charmed|XPHB} until the end of its next turn. On its next turn, if still {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by Enriquo, it obeys his commands. If Enriquo orders it to harm itself or an ally, it repeats the saving throw, ending the {@condition Charmed} condition on a success. Beasts with an Intelligence score of 6 or less automatically fail saving throws made to resist Enriquo's control.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Enriquo makes two Flaming Whip attacks.

action.name: Flaming Whip
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d4 + 3}) Slashing damage, plus 2 ({@damage 1d4}) Fire damage.

reaction.name: Flame Thrower
entries: Enriquo magically commands the Fire from an open flame within 60 feet of him to surge towards a creature within 10 feet of it. The target makes a Dexterity saving throw. {@actSaveFail} 9 ({@damage 2d8}) Fire damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half Damage.

trait.name: Mirrored
entries: When the psuedo-self rolls {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, it alters its form to become identical to that of one player character it can see within 120 feet, except it is mirrored. It gains an additional Mirrored Ability trait depending on the class of that player character (if the character is a multi-class, it gains the ability associated with its primary class).

trait.name: Mirrored Ability: Spellcaster
entries: {@note (If the psuedo-self took the form of an Artificer, Bard, Cleric, Druid, Sorcerer, Warlock, or Wizard)}
The pseudo-self can use its action to cast any spell of 1st-level or below with a casting time of 1 action that the creature it took the form of can cast, without a spell slot or components.

trait.name: Mirrored Ability: Warrior
entries: {@note (If the psuedo-self took the form of a Barbarian, Fighter, Monk, Ranger, Rogue, or Paladin)}
The pseudo-self has a +1 bonus to its AC, and can attack twice, rather than once, when it takes the {@action Attack|XPHB} action.

trait.name: Magical Construct

trait.name: Ceramic Aura

trait.name: Disembodied
entries: The snatcher lacks a true form of its own, existing as a shade of a true snatcher in a different plane of existence. Acting only as a projection of another being, it has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws.

action.name: Infest
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 4} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}7 ({@damage 2d4 + 2}) Psychic damage. If this attack reduces the target to 10 or fewer {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it is {@condition Paralyzed} for 1 minute, or until the snatcher dies. The target can make a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

action.name: Soul Seize
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 4} to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. {@h}8 ({@damage 1d12 + 2}) Necrotic damage.

action.name: Body Snatch (1/Day)
entries: The snatcher attempts to seize the body of a {@condition Paralyzed} creature within 5 feet of itself. The target makes a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw. On a fail, its mind is utterly dominated by the snatcher, as it moves into the target's body, and the target cannot take any action the snatcher does not dictate. The snatcher is killed when the body is killed, otherwise, it cannot be removed by means shorter than a {@spell Wish|XPHB} spell.

trait.name: Stolen Mind
entries: The snatcher has stolen and corrupted the form of a Humanoid. It has access to all the knowledge and memories the Humanoid had in life.

trait.name: Painless
entries: The snatcher has no regard for the pain of its host, attacking recklessly. At the start of its turn, the snatcher (minor) can gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on all melee weapon attack rolls during that turn, but attack rolls against it have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} until the start of its next turn.

trait.name: False Appearance
entries: While the faerie ring remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from an ordinary fungus.

trait.name: Spore Storm

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The faerie ring makes three Spore attacks.

entries: {@atk rs} {@hit 5} to hit, range 120 ft., one target. {@h}10 ({@damage 3d4 + 3}) Poison damage, and the target has a -3 penalty to Wisdom saving throws until the end of the faerie ring's next turn.

action.name: Enchanting Spores
entries: {@dice 1d4} creatures of the faerie ring's choice within 120 feet make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target is {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by the ring, attack rolls made against them have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB|advantage}, and they must use all their movement each turn to dance in a circle around the ring, as close to the center as possible. A creature can repeat the Wisdom save at the end of each of their turns, ending the effect on a success.

trait.name: Water Form
entries: The spirit can enter a hostile creature's space and stop there. It can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without squeezing.

trait.name: Watery Restraint

action.name: Multiattack

action.name: Whelm

On a failed save, the target is also {@condition Grappled|XPHB|grappled} by the spirit and submerged in its watery body. While {@condition Grappled|XPHB|grappled}, it cannot breathe, speak, or perform the verbal components of spells.

action.name: Siren Call
entries: One creature the spirit can see must succeed on a {@dc 17} Wisdom saving throw, or become {@condition Charmed|XPHB|charmed} by the spirit. While {@condition Charmed|XPHB|charmed} by the spirit, the first thing it must do on each turn is use all its movement to move as close to the nearest body of water. Creatures {@condition Charmed|XPHB|charmed} by the spirit that are also fully submerged in water are also {@condition Restrained|XPHB|restrained}. A creature can repeat this save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

bonus.name: Water Rush
entries: The spirit takes the {@action Dash|XPHB|dash} or {@action Disengage|XPHB|disengage} action.

trait.name: Draconic Familiar

rows: The wyrmling gains the Elemental Absorption reaction.
The wyrmling can communicate telepathically with any creature within 100 feet of it that can understand a language.
The wyrmling gains the Courageous Companion trait.

trait.name: Courageous Companion (Metallic Only)
entries: The wyrmling and any allied creature within 5 feet of it automatically succeed on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The wyrmling has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB|advantage} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

action.name: Bite

action.name: Tiny Tornado {@recharge 6}
entries: One Medium or smaller creature within 15 feet of the wyrmling must succeed on a {@dc 12} Strength saving throw or be lifted 10 feet into the air, then slammed to the ground, taking {@damage 1d6} Bludgeoning damage and falling {@condition Prone|XPHB|prone}.

reaction.name: Elemental Absorption (Chromatic Only)
entries: When the wyrmling and/or any creatures within 5 feet of it are subjected to a spell or effect that requires a saving throw and would deal Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Poison damage on a failed save, creatures making the save only take half damage if they fail the save, and no damage if they succeed (even if they would normally take half).

trait.name: Grafted Gift
entries: Roll {@dice 1d4}. The reverter gains one additional trait determined by the roll.

rows: The reverter has a fly speed equal to its walking speed.
Attack rolls made against the reverter have disadvantage.
The reverter can use its chemical blast action.
The reverter has resistance to Bludgeoning, Slashing, and Piercing damage.

hp.special: 5 + five times your Monk level (the Spirit Beast has a number of Hit Dice [d6s] equal to your Monk level)

trait.name: Spirit Bond
entries: Your Spirit Beast is a reflection on your soul; its alignment and powers reflect your own alignment. The damage of its Rend attack deals damage that is Radiant if you're Good, Necrotic if you're Evil, or Force if you are neither Good or Evil.

trait.name: Spirit Guidance
entries: Your Spirit Beast has proficiency in one of the following skills based on your alignment: {@skill Persuasion|XPHB} (Good), {@skill Deception|XPHB} (Evil), or {@skill Survival|XPHB} (neither Good or Evil). When it makes an ability check with a skill it is proficient in, it can use your Wisdom modifier as the ability score modifier.

trait.name: Spirit Strike
entries: When the Spirit Beast hits a creature with a Rend attack, it can force the target to make a Wisdom saving throw (DC equals 8 plus your Wisdom modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}). On a failure, the target is {@condition Blinded|XPHB} (if you're Good), {@condition Frightened|XPHB} (if you're Evil), or {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} (if you're neither Good or Evil) until the end of its next turn. The Spirit Beast can use this trait a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and it regains all expended uses when it finishes a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

action.name: Rend
entries: {@atkr m} Bonus equals your Wisdom modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}One roll of your Martial Arts die plus your Wisdom modifier plus 3 damage of the type determined by the Spirit Beast's Spirit Bond trait.

action.name: Spirit Magic (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest)
entries: The Spirit Beast casts {@spell Bless|XPHB}, {@spell Shield of Faith|XPHB}, or {@spell Bane|XPHB}, depending on its alignment (Good, Neutral, or Evil respectively) using your Wisdom as the spellcasting ability.

action.name: Scrapheap Slam
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}8 ({@damage 1d8 + 4}) Bludgeoning damage plus 4 ({@damage 1d8}) Poison damage.

action.name: Spew Trash {@recharge 5}
entries: The golem unleashes a wave of rotting trash in a 15-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. Each creature in that area must succeed on a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw or fall {@condition Prone|XPHB} and have the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. A {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

immune.note: from nonmagical attacks not made with silvered weapons

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: Momma Mulberry has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB|advantage} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 6} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}8 ({@damage 1d8 + 4}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Eldritch Blast
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 5} to hit, range 90 ft., one target. {@h}11 ({@damage 2d10}) Force damage.

bonus.name: Endless Empowerment
entries: Momma Mulberry channels potent nature magic, choosing from one of the following boons she is not currently benefiting from, which lasts for 1 minute.

items.name: Flight
entries: Momma Mulberry gains a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to her {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and can hover.

items.name: Fey Beguilement
entries: When Momma Mulberry hits a creature with Eldritch Blast, the target must succeed on a {@dc 13} Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition Charmed|XPHB} for 1 minute. A {@condition Charmed|XPHB} creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

items.name: Mage Armor
entries: Momma Mulberry gains a +3 bonus to AC.

items.name: Raking Claws
entries: Momma Mulberry's Claw attack deals an additional {@damage 1d8} Slashing damage on a hit.

items.name: Regenerate
entries: Momma Mulberry gains 4 ({@damage 1d8}) {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} at the end of each of her turns.

immune.note: from nonmagical attacks not made with silvered weapons

trait.name: Otherworldly Fortitude
entries: The Rag and Bone Man has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB|advantage} on Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution saving throws.

action.name: Skeletal Blade
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}10 ({@damage 1d10 + 5}) Slashing damage plus 2 ({@damage 1d4}) Necrotic damage.

action.name: Skeletal Bow
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 7} to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. {@h}9 ({@damage 1d8 + 5}) Piercing damage plus 2 ({@damage 1d4}) Necrotic damage.

bonus.name: Endless Despair
entries: The Rag and Bone Man weaves an enchantment of despair, which billows out from him in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} for 1 minute. The area includes one of the following options of his choice; each time he takes this Bonus Action while the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} remains, he adds a different option of his choice to the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}.

items.name: Disintegration
entries: Any creature that ends its turn in the area takes 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Necrotic damage.

items.name: Easy Target
entries: Attack rolls made against creatures in the aura have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}.

items.name: Enfeeble
entries: Creatures in the aura suffer a {@dice 1d4} penalty to damage rolls.

items.name: Magic Quash
entries: Magical properties of magic items don't work inside the area or on anything inside it.

items.name: Spell Squash
entries: Creatures in the aura cannot cast spells using higher-level spell slots.

trait.name: Corrupted Serum
entries: The failed test subject rolls {@dice 3d8} at the start of each of its turns while in combat. It gains a bonus to damage rolls equal to the result, and its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point Maximum} is reduced by the same amount.

trait.name: Unstable Experiment
entries: When the failed test subject falls to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it explodes. Creatures in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|emanation} make a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes damage equal to half the failed test subject's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point Maximum}.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The failed test subject makes two attacks.

action.name: Frenzied Daggers
entries: {@atk mw,rw} {@hit 8} to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d4 + 5}) Slashing damage, and the target falls {@condition Prone|XPHB|prone} if it's Medium sized or smaller.

trait.name: Mutagenic Adaptation
entries: After the spider takes damage of a damage type other than Psychic or Force, it gains {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to that damage type until the start of its next turn.

trait.name: Spider Climb
entries: The spider can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

trait.name: Web Walker
entries: The spider ignores movement restrictions caused by webs, and it knows the location of any other creature in contact with the same web.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d8 + 3}) Piercing damage plus 13 ({@damage 2d12}) Acid damage.

action.name: Stinging Web {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 13}, one creature the spider can see within 60 feet. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition and takes {@damage 2d12} Acid damage at the start of each of its turns until the web is destroyed (AC 10; HP 5; {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB|Vulnerability} to Fire damage; {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunity} to Acid, Poison, and Psychic damage).

trait.name: Experiment Amalgam
entries: When the test subject rolls {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB|initiative}, it gains the benefits of two random Serums for the next hour, ignoring any drawbacks (see page XX).

trait.name: Immortal Amalgamation
entries: If the test subject dies, it reforms {@dice 1d4} days later at full {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (2/Day)
entries: If the test subject fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The test subject has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The test subject makes three attacks.

action.name: Acid Spit
entries: {@atk rs} {@hit 10} to hit, range 90 ft., one target. {@h}19 ({@damage 3d12}) Acid damage, and the target is {@condition Blinded|XPHB} until the start of its next turn.

action.name: Poison Claw
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 11} to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}20 ({@damage 2d12 + 7}) Slashing damage, and the target must succeed on a Constitution Saving Throw ({@dc 18}) or be {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} until the end of its next turn.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
entries: If Fernda fails a saving throw, she can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Sentinel Shield
entries: Fernda has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} rolls and Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: Fernda casts one of the following spells, using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 21}, {@hit 13} to hit with spell attacks):

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Fernda makes two attacks. She can replace one with a use of her Serum Shot.

action.name: Arcane Armament
entries: {@atk rs} {@hit 12} to hit, range 90/320 ft., one target. {@h}31 ({@damage 9d6}) Force damage.

action.name: Serum Shot
entries: Fernda injects one of her serums, ignoring its drawbacks (see page 25)

reaction.name: Flash of Genius (6/Day)
entries: If Fernda or a creature she can see within 30 feet fails an ability check or saving throw, she adds a +6 bonus to the roll, potentially causing it to succeed.

reaction.name: Mind Sharpener (4/Day)
entries: If Fernda fails a Constitution saving throw to maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB}, she can choose to succeed instead.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Bow
entries: You can use your action to create a pact weapon in your empty hand, which takes the form of a bow or firearm. You are proficient with this weapon while you wield it, and it counts as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

Your pact weapon disappears if it is more than 5 feet away from you for 1 minute or more. It also disappears if you use this feature again, if you dismiss the weapon (no action required), or if you die.

You can transform one Magic Weapon that is a bow or firearm into your pact weapon by performing a special ritual while you hold the weapon. You perform the ritual over the course of 1 hour, which can be done during a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}. You can then dismiss the weapon, shunting it into an extradimensional space, and it appears whenever you create your pact weapon thereafter. You can't affect an artifact or a sentient weapon in this way. The weapon ceases being your pact weapon if you die, if you perform the 1-hour ritual on a different weapon, or if you perform a 1-hour ritual to break your bond to it. The weapon appears at your feet if it is in the extradimensional space when the bond breaks.

You can use your pact weapon to make ranged attack rolls, which generates its own magical ammunition. When you do, you use your Charisma modifier in place of Dexterity for your attack and damage rolls. When you cast {@spell Eldritch Blast|XPHB}, you can also choose to fire it through your pact weapon.

When you make an attack roll using your pact weapon, you can choose to infuse the shot with a burst of eldritch magic. Choose one of the following Eldritch Shots to infuse into your strike. You can infuse a shot in this way a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier per {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, regaining one expended use when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Blazing Shot
entries: Attack rolls made against the target have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} until the end of this turn, including this shot.

entries.name: Commanding Shot
entries: Up to one ally that can see the target within 30 feet of them and can hear you can use its {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to move up to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} towards the target. If it ends its movement within reach of the target, it can make a single weapon attack or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} against it.

entries.name: Execution Shot
entries: This attack roll scores a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} on a {@dice d20} result of 17, 18, 19, or 20.

entries.name: Explosive Shot
entries: Creatures of your choice within 5 feet of the target take additional Force damage equal to twice your Charisma modifier.

entries.name: Sapping Shot
entries: The target of your attack takes Necrotic damage equal to twice your Charisma modifier, and you gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the damage dealt in this way.

entries.name: Seeking Shot
entries: Treat any result on the {@dice d20} that is less than a 15 on this attack roll as a 15.

entries.name: Smoking Shot
entries: The area in a 10-foot radius of the target is {@variantrule Heavily Obscured|XPHB} by magical, pitch darkness for the next minute.

entries.name: Terrifying Shot
entries: The target takes Psychic damage equal to your Charisma modifier and is {@condition Frightened|XPHB} of you until the end of your next turn.

optionalfeature.name: Eldritch Hunter
entries: You can cast the spell {@spell Hex|XPHB} without a spell slot a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier, regaining all expended uses upon finishing a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, and its range increases to 300 feet when you cast it in this way. Attacking at long range doesn't impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on your ranged weapon attack rolls when targeting a creature cursed with the {@spell Hex|XPHB} spell.

optionalfeature.name: Eldritch Volley
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action and make a ranged weapon attack with your pact weapon, you can cast {@spell Eldritch Blast|XPHB} as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} that turn.

optionalfeature.name: Ravenous Bowstring
entries: You can attack with your pact weapon twice, instead of once, when you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Cauldron
entries: You gain proficiency with {@item Brewer's Supplies|XPHB}, and can use your Charisma modifier for any ability checks you make using them.

Over the course of 1 hour, which can be done during a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, you can perform a ritual to conjure a cauldron filled with bubbling magic. When you finish the ritual, you can extract a number of Eldritch Concoctions equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one). You choose each Eldritch Concoction's type from the options below. Each concoction is enough for a single use. Concoctions remain magical for 24 hours, or until you perform this ritual again. You can perform the ritual twice, regaining all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Eldritch Concoctions
entries: There are two types of Eldritch Concoctions, Banes and Boons, which behave in the following ways.

entries.name: Banes
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, a creature can drink a Bane concoction or apply it to a weapon or piece of ammunition. If a creature drinks it, the next time it hits a creature with a spell attack roll or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} it inflicts its effect on that target. If applied to a weapon or piece of ammunition, the first time that weapon or ammunition hits a creature, that target suffers the effect of the concoction. If the effect requires a saving throw, it uses your spell save DC.

entries.name: Boons
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, a creature can drink a Boon concoction, gaining its effects.

entries.name: Ink of the Kraken (Bane)
entries: A mist of pitch ink obscures the target's eyes. The target makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the target is {@condition Blinded|XPHB} for 1 minute or until it or a creature within reach of it uses an action to wipe away the ink. On a success, the target is {@condition Blinded|XPHB} until the start of its next turn.

entries.name: Jelly of the Gelatinous Cube (Bane)
entries: The target is engulfed in a wave of cloying ooze. It makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the target is {@condition Restrained|XPHB} until the end of its next turn. On a success, its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is halved until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Saliva of the Slaad (Bane)
entries: The target is wracked with a vicious, painful curse. At the start of its next turn, the target takes {@damage 1d4} Poison damage. On each of its subsequent turns, it takes additional Poison damage. To determine this damage, roll a number of {@dice d4}s equal to the highest roll on a {@dice d4} from the last time it took damage from this effect. An affected creature makes a Constitution saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. The target automatically succeeds after 1 minute.

entries.name: Venom of the Purple Worm (Bane)
entries: The target takes an additional {@damage 3d6} Poison damage from the attack, and its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum is reduced by the same amount until it finishes a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Blood of the Displacer Beast (Boon)
entries: For 1 minute, whenever you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the save and half damage if you fail. This effect is suppressed while you are {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}.

entries.name: Ichor of the Platinum Dragon (Boon)
entries: You regain {@dice 2d6} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum increases by the same amount for 1 hour. Your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} maximum cannot be raised in this way again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Sap of the Treant (Boon)
entries: For 1 minute, your size becomes Large if there is room and you aren't already larger, your reach increases by 5 feet, and you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Tears of the Tarrasque (Boon)
entries: For 1 minute, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Fire and Poison damage, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, {@condition Deafened|XPHB}, {@condition Frightened|XPHB}, {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB}, and {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} conditions.

optionalfeature.name: Alchemist
entries: When you perform the ritual to summon your cauldron, you can add one {@filter Common potion|items|rarity=common|type=potion} to it. If you do, the potion is destroyed and you can add that potion's properties as an additional Eldritch Concoction option available to you as part of this use of the feature.

optionalfeature.name: Cauldron Keeper
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, choose one Boon Eldritch Concoction. You gain one vial of that concoction, which remains magical for 24 hours. If you drink the concoction, its effects last for 8 hours.

optionalfeature.name: Deadly Concoctions
entries: Each creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the first saving throw it makes to avoid or end a condition imposed by each use of your concoctions.
When one of your concoctions deals damage to a creature, roll {@dice 1d10} and add the result to the damage roll.

optionalfeature.name: Superior Alchemist
entries: When you perform the ritual to summon your cauldron, you can add one {@filter Uncommon potion|items|rarity=uncommon|type=potion} to it. If you do, the potion is destroyed and you can add that potion's properties as an additional Eldritch Concoction option available to you as part of this use of the feature.

optionalfeature.name: Potent Concoctions
entries: If one of your concoctions gives a creature {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to a damage type, it grants {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to that damage type instead.
If a concoction restores {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} to a creature, it restores {@dice 1d10} additional {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

optionalfeature.name: Ultimate Alchemist
entries: When you perform the ritual to summon your cauldron, you can add one {@filter Rare potion|items|rarity=rare|type=potion} to it. If you do, the potion is destroyed and you can add that potion's properties as an additional Eldritch Concoction option available to you as part of this use of the feature.

variantrule.name: Terrifying D&D
entries: Why is D&D so easy these days? How can Game Master's compete with the slew of incredible abilities given to players as early as level 1? How do we craft a compelling game when it feels players are given tools for every imaginable situation?

The answer is simple, we must remember that {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} are not a hero's only resource! In fact, they are arguably the least important resource in the game, seeing as a hero is 100% functional whether they have full HP or are down to their final one. So, why does almost every trap and monster in the game exclusively target a hero's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}? It's like trying to take down a fully operational Death Star, it'll never work. Instead, you can use these truly fiendish traps, curses, and monsters to whittle down each player's resources so when they step into the arena with the Big Bad, they're in a position to feel true terror!

entries.name: Draining Encounter: The Magitech Engine
entries: The magitech engine is a simple encounter that gives your spellcasting heroes a choice and an opportunity to work together. You can adapt this concept to any number of traps or puzzles, but the core magitech engine encounter works like so:

The heroes stumble into a large, open room while venturing through a dungeon, and an iron portcullis slams shut behind them; they're locked in! In the center of the room is a colossal machine, belching thick smoke and jets of flame. This is the Magitech Engine, and it has been overclocked by the denizens of the dungeon; it's going to explode in 3 rounds, dealing Xd10 Fire damage to all heroes in the room (X equals the average player level).

Magitech Engines can be dampened by magic, however. Any spellcaster can use their turn to cast any spell targeting the machine. It takes no damage, but the level of the spell slot expended will dampen magitech's power, reducing the damage of its explosion by {@dice 1d10}.

Thus, a party of level 5 heroes can expend 5 levels of spells (a 3rd level spell + two 1st level spells, for example) to reduce the explosion damage to 0. If they choose not to use any spells to reduce the explosion, all heroes will take {@damage 5d10} Fire damage as the engine bursts.
This challenge forces spellcasting heroes to evaluate the value of their spell slots, potentially burning precious resources to ensure an already injured party can survive the trap.

entries.name: Hard Mode: Magitech Engine Encounter
entries: The core magitech engine trap is a simple non-combat encounter to spice up a dungeon, but if you want to REALLY ratchet up the threat, consider also throwing a few monsters for the party to battle at the same time.

Now, non-spellcasting heroes have something to do, and spellcasters will be forced to either use their magic to aid in defeating the monsters, or cooling down the machine that will burst in 3 rounds, dealing catastrophic damage to everyone.

entries.name: Draining Encounter: Soul Tearing Spirit
entries: Too few monsters in D&D hit players where it REALLY hurts. Sure, striking at {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} is all well and good, but the Soul Tearing Spirit aims to destroy a far more precious resource. If you want to really make your players sweat, throw a couple of Soul Tearing Spirits their way across your next adventure, either early in a dungeon to strip them of resources swiftly, or alongside the Big Bad to give them something really nasty to worry about beyond big damage.

entries.name: Draining Curses
entries: A great way to add an extra challenge to a hero is with a good old fashioned curse. Curses are fantastic because they offer a simple way to add a temporary restrictive mechanic to a dungeon or adventure. The following curses are examples that might impair a hero for a single session, and fade after a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. The intent of curses like this is to restrict a heroes options in some way, forcing the players to adopt new strategies, try new things, grow, explore, and, yeah, maybe sweat a little bit!

These curses could be triggered in any number of ways: perhaps a player attunes to a cursed item, perhaps they fail a Saving Throw against a magical rune trap, or maybe they slept with the wrong temptation demon (we've all been there, right?)

entries.name: Curse: Overwhelming Selfishness
entries: A hero bearing this curse becomes overwhelmed with concern for their own preservation. They cannot target any creature aside from themselves with beneficial spells, features, or traits. For example, a Cleric bearing this curse who casts the {@spell Bless|XPHB} or {@spell Aid|XPHB} spell can be the only beneficiary of those spells. Similarly, a Paladin cannot use their Lay on Hands feature on any creature but themselves.

entries.name: Curse: Lethargy Tether
entries: A hero bearing this curse becomes magically tethered to an allied creature within 300 feet. The two remain tethered until the cursed hero finishes a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. The pair share a single source of energy, between the two they can only cast a single levelled spell, take a single {@action Attack|XPHB} action, move a total of 30 feet, and take a single {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} per round.

entries.name: Curse: Magical Taxation
entries: A hero bearing this curse is strained with magical lethargy. Whenever they cast a spell using a spell slot, they must expend an additional spell slot of any level, otherwise the spell fails.

variantrule.name: Honor Mode D&D
entries: The following are simple house rules you can use to raise the challenge in your games. Feel free to incorporate any/all of the following rules that you feel will add to the tension and fun at your game table!

entries.name: Resurrection Costs
entries: Whenever a hero falls to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, they immediately gain 1 point of {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB}, unless they have a feature or species trait that activates and immediately restores their {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} upon falling to 0.
Any time a hero is returned to life from death, such as with the spell {@spell Revivify|XPHB}, the save DC for their {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB|Death Saving Throws} increases by 3.

entries.name: Short Rest Limitations
entries: Heroes can only benefit from a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} twice. Any subsequent {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short Rests} confer no benefit until the hero finishes a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
You cannot expend {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice} to recover {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} over the course of a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Long Rest Limitations
entries: You do not recover {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} upon finishing a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, but all other benefits of a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} apply as usual.

You spend {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice} to recover {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} over the course of a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You regain a number of expended {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Die} equal to half your maximum at the end of a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Rest Interruptions
entries: Whenever players attempt to {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} in a place that isn't a protected, safe location (such as a tavern), roll {@dice 1d20} to see if the rest is interrupted by an encounter. If the location is actively dangerous, the party is ambushed on a result of 2 or below. If it is a neutral location, they are ambushed on a natural 1. If a rest is interrupted, the heroes gain no benefit from that rest.

Each time the party successfully rests in a location that isn't safe, add {@dice 1d20} to the next roll made to see if they are interrupted (increasing the likelihood they will be interrupted next time).
The number of d20s you roll to see if a party is interrupted resets back to {@dice 1d20} after the heroes finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} in a safe location.

entries.name: Wild Magic Bursts (Round 1)
entries: Are you looking for ways to spice up combat? Add some challenge without putting tons more bodies on the board and dragging a battle out? Maybe you also want to give your players exciting new options and game-impacting combat decisions? Well look no further than the Wild Magic Burst!

The concept here is simple: when your heroes roll for {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, a surge of wild magic washes over the battlefield! For this combat only, the laws of reality are turned on their head; new mechanics are introduced, and one monster of the GMs choice is imbued with the very essence of this wild magical phenomenon, growing even more terrifying. Don't worry though! Players can also harness the wild magic for themselves with wild magic surges of their own.

Below, you'll find three wild magic surges to use in your games - ways to elevate a combat encounter with fun new mechanics. Each one will also include a Surge of Power, a Surge of Hope, and a Monstrous Adaptation. The Monstrous Adaptation infuses one monster with the power of wild magic, and the players themselves can wield wild magic too via the surges of Power and Hope.
This is a concept I've been really enjoying, and hope to make more of in the future - let's make magic WEIRD!!

entries.name: Wild Magic of Leaping Flame
entries: When players roll for {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, a wave of burning wild magic washes across the battlefield. Magical Fire spirals through the air, infusing every living being with blistering, frenetic flame. For the duration of this encounter, all creature's movement {@variantrule Speed|XPHB|Speeds} increase by 20 feet, and all damage rolls deal additional Fire damage equal to the party's average {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} (PB).

entries.name: Monstrous Adaptation: Molten Surge
entries: When this wild magic surge activates, one {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile} creature of the GMs choice undergoes a magical transformation. With a soul ignited by magical Fire, that creature gains the following trait and action:

items: It resists Fire damage.

{@b Molten Surge (Recharge 6).} In place of one of your attacks when you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can release a burst of flame from your mouth or body in a 5xPB foot cone. Creatures in that area must succeed on a DC 12+PB Dexterity Saving Throw, taking PBd12 Fire damage on a failed save, or half as much on a success.

entries.name: Surge of Power: Sparks
entries: When a hero rolls a natural 20 on an Attack roll or Ability Check while this wild magic surge is active, they find the power to bend it to their will. For the next minute:

items: You radiate heat - the air around your body bounces and shimmers and you are hot to the touch.

Once per turn, when you deal Fire damage to a creature with an attack or spell, that creature must succeed on a DC 12+PB Constitution Saving Throw or be {@condition Blinded|XPHB} until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Surge of Hope: Fire Shield
entries: When a hero rolls a natural 1 on an Attack roll, Ability Check, or Saving Throw while this wild magic surge is active, their moment of desperation spirals into The Weave, and it answers with new strength. For the next minute:

items: Your body is wreathed in spectral, crimson flame.

You gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to 5 x your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. For as long as you have these {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}, you resist Fire damage and are {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|immune} to Cold damage.

entries: Once a creature has triggered a Surge of Power or a Surge of Hope, they cannot do so again until they finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Wild Magic of Furry Fury
entries: When players roll for {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, a wave of transmutational wild magic washes across the battlefield, ravaging everything in the area with polymorphic energy. The coarse bark of trees shift into soft fur, grass and moss become fuzzy, and every creature undergoes a bestial transformation, sprouting dense hair, razor teeth, and raking claws.

All creatures are {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|immune} to Bludgeoning, Slashing, and Piercing damage from nonmagical, nonsilvered weapons. {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} deal {@damage 1d8} magical Slashing damage. If a creature's Strength modifier is lower than 19, it becomes 19.

entries.name: Monstrous Adaptation: Bestial Rampage
entries: When this wild magic surge activates, one {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile} creature of the GMs choice undergoes a magical transformation, surrendering itself fully to the beast within. It gains the following traits:

items: It's attacks deal magical damage.
Its movement {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 5xPB feet.
{@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} made against it have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.
It can make PB-1 {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} (minimum 1).

entries.name: Surge of Power: Fuzzy Frenzy
entries: When a hero rolls a natural 20 on an Attack roll or Ability Check while this wild magic surge is active, they find the power to bend it to their will. For the next minute:

items: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can make a number of {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.
If you hit a creature with 3 or more {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} on your turn, you can make an Unarmed Strike as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} this turn.

entries.name: Surge of Hope: Animal Instincts
entries: When a hero rolls a natural 1 on an Attack roll, Ability Check, or Saving Throw while this wild magic surge is active, their moment of desperation spirals into The Weave, and it answers with new strength. For the next minute:

items: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB} and {@skill Insight|XPHB}) checks.
Creatures cannot have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Attack rolls against you.
Your thick hide grants you a +1 bonus to AC.
Once per turn, you can use 10 feet of movement to leap 10xPB feet. This leap does not provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.

entries: Once a creature has triggered a Surge of Power or a Surge of Hope, they cannot do so again until they finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Wild Magic of Sizzling Thought
entries: When players roll for {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, a wave of psionic wild magic washes across the battlefield - an invisible, infinitely adaptable force of creativity and consciousness runs giddy and dizzying through the minds of all creatures. Creatures with an Intelligence score of 18 or lower are {@condition Poisoned|XPHB|Poisoned}, overcome by their own racing, inarticulate mind.

entries.name: Monstrous Adaptation: Intellect Burst
entries: When this wild magic surge activates, one {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile} creature of the GMs choice undergoes a magical transformation, its mind electrified with the chaos and opportunity of wild thought magic. It gains the following traits:

items: Intelligence score becomes 19 if it is lower.
It learns two spells from the {@filter Wizard spell list|spells|class=Wizard} of spell level PB or lower (GMs choice), and it can cast those spells once each without a spell slot or components.
It can {@status Concentration|XPHB|concentrate} on two spells at once.
