The target gains a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} of 20 feet and can hover, and can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} each turn to force one creature within 30 feet of it that is Huge or smaller to make a Strength saving throw (use your Spell Save DC). On a fail, that creature is pushed or pulled 20 feet directly towards or away.

spell.name: Spellpower Surge
entries: You blast a surge of invigorating magical energy towards a willing creature within 30 feet. The target regains {@dice 1d12} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, and it can then use its {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make a single weapon attack at {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}, cast a cantrip, or move up to its speed without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: The {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} restored by this spell increase by {@dice 1d12} for each level you cast it at above 2nd.

spell.name: Invoke Error
entries: You weave a distracting enchantment around a creature within 30 feet of you. The target suffers a -5 penalty to its next Attack Roll.

spell.name: Into Flutter

time.condition: which you take when a creature you can see casts a spell that targets only you

entries: As a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, when a creature you can see casts a spell that targets only you, can unwind the magic that surges towards you. The spell fails, and a swarm of butterflies bursts into life around you, as you transmute the magic into a harmless dissipation.

spell.name: Droug's Gambit
entries: You perform a devastating invocation of sacrificial, spiteful magic. Roll a number of {@dice d12|d12s} up to your level. You take Necrotic damage equal to the result, and one target creature of your choice within 60 feet takes Force damage equal to the Necrotic damage you take.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell at 8th level or above, you can target one additional creature within range to take the Force damage.

spell.name: Immortal Moon
entries: Gentle moonlight spills from your eyes and skin, imbuing those around you with the strength to keep fighting against all odds so long as your will holds. You emit moonlight, which is {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB}, in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} for the duration. Creatures can't benefit from being {@condition Invisible|XPHB} within the area, and creatures of your choice within the area have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunity} to the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} and {@condition Frightened|XPHB} conditions.

Whenever damage would reduce a creature in the area to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you can choose to strengthen its resolve by making a saving throw using your spellcasting ability. The DC equals 15 or the damage taken by the target, whichever is higher. On a failed save, you take {@damage 2d4} Radiant damage. On a successful save, the creature is reduced to 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} instead.

spell.name: Infiltrate
entries: You confound and distort the minds of all who lay eyes on you, so as to gain their trust. For the duration, any creature that can see you perceives you to be a known and trusted ally that it might reasonably encounter, such as a colleague, relative, or friend. Affected creatures are {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} to you. Each creature may view you differently, but doesn't notice the discrepancy between its perception and the perception of others around it.

As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can hear the surface thoughts of a creature within 10 feet of you that sees you in this way. A suspicious creature can ascertain your true nature with a successful Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) check against your spell save DC. Creatures with {@sense Truesight|XPHB} or that are {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|immune} to the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition see you as yourself.

spell.name: Steadying Stone
entries: You connect a creature directly to the raw power of the earth, making it as sturdy as a mountain. Until the spell ends, the target's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} becomes 25 feet and can't be increased or reduced in any way. The target can't be lifted from the ground, and it's {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immune} to the {@condition Grappled|XPHB}, {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB|Paralysed}, {@condition Prone|XPHB}, {@condition Restrained|XPHB}, and {@condition Stunned|XPHB} conditions. If the target had any of these conditions when the spell was cast, the conditions are suppressed for the duration.

spell.name: Storm's Eye

components.m: a vial of water and a flame

entries: You conjure a furious storm that rotates in a 60-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you. You can also choose to create an area safe from the storm's effects in an {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} extending up to 15 feet from you. The storm's area is {@variantrule Heavily Obscured|XPHB} and {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}. A creature that enters the storm for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes {@damage 3d8} Cold, Lightning, or Thunder damage (your choice when you cast this spell) and is knocked {@condition Prone|XPHB}. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage only. A creature that fails the save by 5 or more is also {@condition Frightened|XPHB} of you until the start of its next turn.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d8} for each spell slot level above 5.

spell.name: Unified Flight
entries: You gain a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} of 30 feet and create a magical breeze in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you for the duration. Creatures of your choice that start their turn in the area or enter it for the first time on a turn gain a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} of 30 feet until they leave the area. When you move, each affected creature in the area can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to move with you until the end of the turn.

spell.name: Work Smarter
entries: You touch a willing creature and allow it to subconsciously draw on your knowledge and resourcefulness. Until the spell ends, whenever the target makes an {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, it can choose to use your Intelligence modifier instead of the ability modifier it would normally use for that roll.

spell.name: Phantom Bridge
entries: You touch a willing creature and imbue its steps with a fragile magical structure. For the duration, the target can move atop liquids and gases (including air) as though they were solid ground, though they can't change elevation when moving in this way. For example, the target can walk on water or across the air to traverse a chasm. If the target moves less than its normal {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} (even if its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced) on its turn, the spell ends early and the target falls if nothing is holding it aloft.

spell.name: Scapegoat

time.condition: which you take before making a saving throw against damage

entries: You draw in the full force of a hazard. You gain {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to the damage of the triggering effect. If another creature would take damage from failing the same saving throw, it has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to that damage. If it would take half damage from succeeding, it takes no damage if it succeeds instead. This doesn't prevent other effects of the saving throw.

spell.name: Disappearing Act
entries: You magically prepare yourself to avoid an onslaught of attacks. For the duration, whenever you're hit with an attack, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to disappear in a cloud of smoke, gaining {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to any damage dealt by the triggering attack and teleporting to an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet of yourself.

spell.name: Feathered Fury
entries: You summon a flock of angry, spectral chickens to descend on a creature you can see within range. At the start of each of the target's turns, it makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 4d4} Piercing damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. The spell ends early if the target succeeds on its saving throw three times.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The Piercing damage increases by {@dice 2d4} for each spell slot level above 2.

spell.name: Hunter's Hound
entries: You summon a Small or Tiny spectral dog, which appears in an unoccupied space within range. The dog is incorporeal and can't be targeted by attacks or effects, has {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} with a range of 5 feet, and shares what it sees with you telepathically. The spell ends if it's ever more than 120 feet away from you.
On your turn, you can move the dog up to 30 feet to a surface that can support it (no action required), and you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and command it to hunt, attack, or heal.

items.name: Hunt
entries: When the dog hunts, it makes an {@skill Investigation|XPHB}, {@skill Perception|XPHB}, or {@skill Survival|XPHB} check (your choice) using your spellcasting ability and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

items.name: Attack
entries: When the dog attacks, make a melee spell attack against a creature within 5 feet of the dog. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 2d8} Force damage. After the dog hits a target with an attack, the spell ends.

items.name: Heal
entries: When the dog heals, one creature within 5 feet of it regains {@dice 1d8} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. After the dog has healed twice, the spell ends.

spell.name: Wealth of Health

m.text: up to five coins worth 1+ CP each

entries: You infuse restorative magic into the coins used in the spell's casting. For the duration, a creature can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to consume an infused coin it is holding to regain {@dice 1d4} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. When the spell ends, any remaining coins lose this magic.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: When you cast this spell using slots of a higher level, greater denominations of currency restore more {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} when consumed: Silver Pieces ({@dice 2d6}) at level 4, Gold Pieces ({@dice 3d8}) at level 6, and Platinum Pieces ({@dice 4d10}) at level 8.

spell.name: Void Form
entries: You become one with emptiness, a vassal of power that perfectly channels magical energy. You resist Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage, and are {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|immune} to the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} and {@condition Frightened|XPHB} conditions. Spells you cast that use a spell slot are treated as being cast at one level higher than the spell slot expended to cast them.

spell.name: Bloodpact
entries: You attempt to forge a bloodpact between yourself and a creature you can see within 30 feet. The target makes a Charisma saving throw. On a fail, for the duration of the spell, any time you take damage, the target takes {@damage 2d4} Necrotic damage. The target can take this damage in this way a number of times per turn equal to the level of this spell.

spell.name: Strangling Vines
entries: Vicious, choking vines burst into existence and attempt to ensnare a creature you can see within range. The target makes a Strength saving throw. On a fail, it takes {@damage 12d6} Bludgeoning damage and is {@condition Grappled|XPHB} for 1 minute (escape DC = your Spell Save DC). A creature {@condition Grappled|XPHB} in this way is also {@condition Restrained|XPHB}, and takes {@damage 4d6} Bludgeoning damage each time it makes an attack roll or ability check. On a successful save, the target takes half damage only.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using A Higher Level Spell Slot
entries: All Bludgeoning damage increases by {@dice 1d6} for each spell slot level above 6.

spell.name: Opening Salvo
entries: You conjure a spiraling barrage of magical ammunition that streaks towards a creature within 60 feet of you. Make a ranged spell attack roll against the target. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 3d8} Force damage and the next attack roll made against it within the next minute has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: Increase the damage by {@dice 1d8} for each slot level above 2nd.

spell.name: Closing Statement
entries: With a word or phrase of power, you attempt to drain the lifeforce from a creature who can hear you within 60 feet. The target makes a Charisma saving throw, taking {@damage 6d12} Necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much on a success. If this damage reduces a target to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you regain one expended spell slot of 5th level or lower.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: Increase the damage by {@dice 1d12} for each slot level above 5th.

spell.name: Magma Vortex
entries: You conjure a tumultuous vortex of magma that surrounds a creature within range. The target takes {@damage 8d6} Fire damage and makes a Strength saving throw. On a success, the spell ends. On a fail, the target is {@condition Grappled|XPHB} by the vortex and it takes {@damage 8d6} Fire damage at the start of each of its turns. While {@condition Grappled|XPHB} in this way, it is also {@condition Restrained|XPHB}. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can move the vortex up to 30 feet. If you move it into the air, the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} target is supported by the vortex while it remains. A creature {@condition Grappled|XPHB} by the vortex can use its action to repeat its saving throw, dispelling the storm on a success.

spell.name: Rigor Mortis
entries: You focus a blast of necrotic energy towards a creature you can see within range. The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or have its body stiffen painfully for the duration. {@status Bloodied|XPHB} creatures have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on this saving throw, and creatures without muscles or similar anatomy automatically succeed on it.

While its body is stiffened, the target takes {@damage 2d6} Necrotic damage at the start of each of its turns, and it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Strength- and Dexterity-based {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB|D20 Tests}. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: You can target one additional creature for each spell slot level above 2.

spell.name: Dissonant Knell
entries: A necrotically infused wave of thunderous energy erupts from you in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}. Each creature of your choice in the area makes a Constitution saving throw, taking {@damage 2d8} Necrotic damage and {@damage 2d8} Thunder damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
Creatures of your choice with 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} in the area regain 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} instead of making the saving throw.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The Necrotic damage increases by {@dice 1d8} for each spell slot level above 3.

spell.name: Invoke Lycanthropy
entries: You weave a fleeting spark of lycanthropy over a willing creature you touch. The target gains 15 {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}, and gains the following benefits until the spell ends:

items: Its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 15 feet.

It can use your spellcasting ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls of its {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes}, and for calculating the save DC when attempting to grapple or shove a creature.
Its {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} deal {@damage 2d8} Slashing damage on a hit, instead of the normal damage for an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}.
It has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage from nonsilvered weapons.
It can make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

entries: If you cast this spell on a target for the full duration every day for 365 days, the curse makes a home within the target. Casting this spell on that creature no longer requires {@status Concentration|XPHB}.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} increases by 5 for each spell slot level above 3.

spell.name: Invoke Vampirism
entries: You weave a fleeting spark of vampirism over a willing creature you touch. The target gains the following benefits for the duration:

items: While {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, it regains 10 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} at the end of each of its turns.
It has a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and can hover.

Once per turn, when the target deals damage to a creature, that creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, the creature is {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by the target for 1 minute. The creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

The target can use its {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to bite a creature within its reach, making a melee spell attack using your spellcasting ability. The attack automatically hits a creature that is {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by the target. The attack deals {@damage 3d8} Piercing and {@damage 3d8} Necrotic damage on a hit, and the target then gains {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the Necrotic damage dealt.

entries: If you cast this spell on the same target for the full duration every day for 365 days, the spark makes a home within the target. Casting this spell on that target no longer requires {@status Concentration|XPHB}.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The Necrotic damage dealt by the bite attack increases by {@dice 2d8} for each spell slot level above 5.

spell.name: Vile Polymorph
entries: You attempt to transform a creature that you can see within range into an Undead. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or shape-shift into an Undead form for the duration. That form can be any Undead you choose that has a Challenge Rating equal to or less than CR 10, but of a CR no higher than the target's current CR or level. The target's game statistics are replaced by the stat block of the chosen Undead, but the target retains its alignment, personality, creature type, {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, and {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}.

items: The target gains a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} of the Undead form. These {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} vanish if any remain when the spell ends. The spell ends early on the target if it has no {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} left.
The target is limited in the actions you can perform by the anatomy of its new form, and it can't speak or cast spells.
The target's gear melds into the new form. The creature can't use or otherwise benefit from any of that equipment.

If you transform the target into a form that is of a CR 4 or lower, it is {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by you and obeys your commands (no action required by you) until the spell ends. If you issue a command, such as "Run over there," or "Attack that creature," the target uses its next turn to attempt to heed your instruction. If you issue no commands, the target defends and preserves itself to the best of its ability.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The maximum CR of Undead you can transform a target into, and the CR of the target you are able to command, both increase by 2 for each spell slot level above 6.

spell.name: Zombify
entries: You weave a fleeting spark of zombification over a willing creature you touch. The target gains the following effects for the duration:

items: It cannot cast spells or speak.
It has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Necrotic and Poison damage, and has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.

If damage reduces the target to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it makes a Constitution saving throw (DC 5 plus the damage taken), unless the damage is Radiant or from a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}. On a success, it drops to 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} instead.

entries: If you cast this spell on the same target for the full duration every day for 365 days, the spark makes a home within the target. Casting this spell on that target no longer requires {@status Concentration|XPHB}.

entries.name: Forward
entries: High fantasy is more than emerald green medieval Europe with pointy ears. But when people come to your table with an idea of what they want already in their heads, giving them something completely alien or new doesn't always go over well. These are games of collective hallucination—if we aren't all on the same page, then the fantasy doesn't work. That's why the trick is to "push" the fantasy to keep things fresh. You start with something familiar/comfortable, and then once all the players are in the groove, you add new context to it. The giants came from outer space? The orcs are humans trapped between dimensions? At worst, everyone comes away with an interesting night to remember... but more often than not, you'll strike everyone's curiosity and embark on a legendary fantasy campaign. Try this on for size!

An Untimely Mirage is an era-spanning time-travel adventure that plunges 4–6 level 1 heroes into a battle between goblin bandits and an elven town. The initially typical adventure setup is flipped midway through, as a terrible storm drops the heroes into a mysterious civilization and time period where everything is different. Will the heroes return home the same people they were before? Can they use the lessons of the future to build a better present?

entries.name: Background
entries: It's said that the vast Sanoshir Desert has existed since before time began and will be here long after the end of time too. No structure persists for very long on its endless dunes; massive sandstorms completely erase villages and settlements without warning. Nonetheless, the desert hosts several civilizations today, each built around its own modest oasis.

One such civilization belongs to the wood elves of Bochifera. They've weathered sandstorms for over three centuries and have established themselves as a small trading hub and resting place for wayward wanderers lost in the desert. Bochifera owes its good fortune to a lack of raiders threatening to take over their oasis (up until now).

The Pringle are a group of roving {@creature goblin||Goblins} that once belonged to the massive Pringala City before it was swept away. They have been attacking traders bringing supplies into Bochifera and are building an arsenal. It won't be long before the Pringle are ready to storm the village and claim the settlement as their new home.

The secret of the Sanoshir Desert is that the chaotic storms that sweep through the desert are in fact a single storm that is temporally locked. The storm rages eternally; it is the same storm blustering today as it was 5 years ago and will be 500 in the future, simply phasing in and out of various time periods. The debris it leaves in its wake is typically laid to waste across time and impossible to identify. Pringala City, miraculously, was flung into the distant future and continued to develop, unbeknownst to the Pringle goblins or any desert inhabitant living today.

entries.name: Setup
entries: You can introduce this adventure as the players travel to a large settlement somewhere beyond the Sanoshir Desert. Any wood elf heroes amongst the party will certainly have contacts in Bochifera—if you are running this adventure as your first session in a campaign, any elven characters may live in the village, meeting the rest of the party as they first arrive in town.

The heroes are approached by the village guard (use the {@creature bandit captain} stat block), a stocky, strong-willed wood elf named Flurel. She requests that they join her to rout out the goblin raiders camped just outside before they raid the village. The Pringle have been threatening to take over Bochifera for weeks now, and she's afraid that they're strong enough to pull it off. She's willing to offer 10 GP to each hero to retrieve the supplies they've stolen, or 20 GP each if they make sure to leave no goblins alive.

entries.name: Quickly! Attack Now!
entries: {@adventure Map 1|AnUntimelyMirage|1|Adventure Map 1}

The Pringle encampment is in a canyon an hour away from the village. Most of the stolen supplies are lodged into the canyon walls and hidden from sight, allowing the goblins to keep a low profile. Two {@creature Goblin Lookout|DMSecretWeapon24|Goblin Lookouts} are posted on top of the canyon, while three standard {@creature goblin||Goblins} and the Pringle captain {@creature Goblin Captain Lobert|DMSecretWeapon24|Lobert} are training below. The goblins have a climb speed equal to their running speed and can quickly move between the two levels as needed.

The heroes can approach from the North or the South on the map. The goblins aren't immediately aggressive; {@creature Goblin Captain Lobert|DMSecretWeapon24|Lobert} is willing to talk to the heroes about resettling the Pringles if they approach peacefully. The goblins only attack if they find the heroes are sneaking around, the heroes draw steel, or the heroes make headway in their negotiations and provoke a very frustrated Flurel to shout: "What are you doing? Kill every last one of them!"

The players are fighting 3 {@creature goblin||Goblins}, 2 {@creature Goblin Lookout|DMSecretWeapon24|Goblin Lookouts}, and {@creature Goblin Captain Lobert|DMSecretWeapon24|Lobert}. Flurel does not take a turn in the battle, except to administer a {@item Potion of Healing} on {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} count 0 to a hero who has taken damage.

On {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} 20 of the third round of combat, the winds begin to whip and howl. The goblins drop their weapons and flee into the canyon before a massive curtain of sand rolls into the area and consumes the heroes. Players retain their position in {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} as they brace for the impact of the temporal storm.

entries.name: Time for a Sandstorm
entries: It's dark inside the storm, only lit by infrequent bolts of purple lightning. Massive chunks of rock ride the winds and slam into the ground over and over. Waves of magical energy thrum loudly and pulse through the area at regular intervals.

The heroes are forced to avoid debris, look for cover, and withstand the brunt of the gales and energy waves until the storm subsides. The players maintain their position in {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}.

On their turn, a hero must make a {@dc 10} Dexterity saving throw, followed by a {@dc 11} Wisdom saving throw, followed by their choice of a {@dc 13} Constitution or Charisma saving throw. If a hero fails a saving throw, another hero can use their {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to allow them to reroll the failed save (they must use the new result). Flurel automatically fails her saving throws, unless a player uses their {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to intervene. If they do, she automatically succeeds instead.

When everyone has taken a turn, each hero counts up their total number of successes. If a player used their {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to aid another player's save, they can add 1 to their total. The result determines the hero's appearance when the storm subsides:

rows: Your size is Small (or Tiny if you are normally a Tiny creature). Whenever you take 5 or more damage in a single instance, you must succeed on a {@dc 13} Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition Frightened} of the source of that damage until the end of your next turn.
Your size is Small (or Tiny if you are normally a Tiny creature). Your passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) is halved.
You were unaffected by the storm.
Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by 5 feet. Your passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) is halved.
Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by 10 feet. Whenever you regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you only regain half the {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} you would normally receive.
footnotes: These transformations are physical in nature; they do not affect a hero's ability scores or memory. However, you can encourage your players to explore how this transformation might affect their voice, or how they carry their gear, or how regularly they need the bathroom, etc., when moving forward with the adventure.

entries.name: Wait a Minute...
entries: {@adventure Map 2|AnUntimelyMirage|1|Adventure Map 2}

As the sand settles, the heroes find themselves amid a shabby town with unusually geometric masonry and metal work. The canyon, Lobert, and the goblins they were interacting with are nowhere to be found.

Any heroes who wish to identify their surroundings can attempt a {@dc 14} Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check. On a success, they identify the misplacement of stars and constellations in the sky above them, suggesting the very placement of the planet has been altered. Heroes who beat the DC by 4 or more correctly identify that the position of the stars indicate the year to be some 500 calendar years ahead of the time period they occupied before the storm struck. Characters with proficiency in {@item Navigator's Tools|XPHB} identify this immediately, without the need for a Survival check.

While the heroes get their bearings, Flurel is being stalked by a {@creature Feral Elf Alpha|DMSecretWeapon24} that waits on all fours from the corner of one of the buildings until they find a moment to dash out and bite. Any creature with a passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) of 14 or higher can point out the elf before they pounce, imposing {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on its {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} roll.

The feral elf fights until it is reduced to half {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} before scurrying off. When the threat is gone, several tall, slender, and green humanoids wrapped in cloaks come out of the buildings to greet the heroes. Any player that succeeds on a {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check notices that they look like overgrown goblins.

Among the residents is a particularly muscular individual named Berlotti, the leader of Pringala City. He graciously offers the heroes water and towels to clean themselves after braving the storm. Unfortunately, he can't offer more than that; the city has just finished lockdown preparations ahead of the incoming feral elf hunting pack.

If the heroes still appear to be relatively healthy, Berlotti asks if they can help with their current operation. The scouts estimate that the full brunt of the pack should be arriving in about 30 minutes. If the elves can be kept at bay for long enough, then the Pringala defense force can scare them off for good with well timed explosives.

Berlotti eyes Flurel and any wood elf heroes frequently while talking to the party but doesn't say anything disparaging or withhold any help. If pressed about it, he apologizes and is unsure of why the elves look familiar to him. Flurel doesn't notice, either, as she's still processing the events up until this moment.

entries.name: Clocking the Feral Elves
entries: Five Pringala goblins (standard {@creature goblin} stat block) begin their preparations for a coordinated artillery blast atop the tallest structure at the north of the map.

The heroes can set up anywhere on the map. Waves of feral elves will appear at the start of each round, entering from the southern and eastern edges of the map, usually prioritizing the nearest green-skinned creatures they can see. They aim to kill the goblins setting up the artillery, but will fight any heroes standing in their way. Each round alternates between 1 {@creature Feral Elf Alpha|DMSecretWeapon24} or 4 {@creature Feral Elf|DMSecretWeapon24|Feral Elves} arriving and entering {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}. If the goblins preparing the artillery explosives can survive for four rounds, they rain explosions down on the remaining elves, forcing them to flee. Use the {@creature Goblin Lookout|DMSecretWeapon24} stat block to represent the artillerists.

Should the invading elves succeed in killing the goblins preparing the artillery, Berlotti and the Pringala residents go into hiding as the elves overrun the city. Just as the heroes are cornered, another sandstorm sweeps across the area. Progress to {@adventure Deja Vu|AnUntimelyMirage|0|Deja Vu}.

If the plan succeeds, the Pringala residents come out of hiding and celebrate in the streets once the feral elves are driven out. Berlotti is thankful for the heroes' help and provides them with one of their explosive metal wands (a {@item Wand of Magic Missiles}).

He also informs the heroes that his scouts detected a sandstorm should be hitting the canyon about an hour away from the city. "No idea who'd be crazy enough to chase down a storm," he says with a wink. "But if you walked out of one alive, you could probably handle three more before it becomes a problem."

entries.name: Deja Vu
entries: The next storm is less intense than the first. The heroes and Flurel weather it without additional effects and arrive on the other side at their proper ages.

When the sands settle, the party finds themselves back at the canyon, just before their first encounter with the goblins. The Pringle encampment is untouched, and Lobert and the others are unaware of the heroes' journey. Flurel is still resolved to protect Bochifera, but is unsure of how to proceed after everything she's witnessed.

It's up to the heroes to decide how to proceed. Do they want to complete their original job and rout the goblins, broker peace with the goblins and find them a new home, or manipulate the Sanoshir sands to connect the people in the desert separated by time?

data.name: An Evil Unsealed
entries: A 2-session long adventure for 4–5 5th-level characters.

entries.name: Synopsis
entries: Deep within the Oroborus Jungle lies the unassuming settlement of Argen-Tor. Though not a popular traveler's destination, the small town hides a huge secret.

Long ago, warriors of old sealed a great evil at the base of a vast, jungle-cradled canyon. The villagers then constructed a door to block off the pathway leading down there. It has been nearly two thousand years since that day. History has become legend, and legend has become fairy tale. The town still celebrates this triumph with the Sealing Festival every year in mid-spring.

The great evil is a fiend named {@creature Zanthropus|DMSecretWeapon24} (Zan-THROH-poos) whose malicious influence has trickled out of the gate over the last two thousand years. His {@creature Cultist||Cultists} have operated in secret throughout Argen-Tor's history, and this year they have an opportunity to open the door, unsealing {@creature Zanthropus|DMSecretWeapon24} and allowing him to walk the world once more.

entries.name: Story Hooks
entries: Argen-Tor is out of the way, so characters probably won't find it by chance while traveling. Use these story hooks to get them to the town:

items.name: Shipment Escort
items.entry: The characters were hired to escort a shipment of fish and other supplies not commonly found in the jungle to Argen-Tor for the Sealing Festival (for a reward of the GM's choice). If so, they'll be looking for a dwarven woman named Amea to drop the food off to.

items.name: Fiendish Influence
items.entry: A faction or organization the characters belong to has heard reports of a fiendish presence in Argen-Tor and asks the characters to investigate.

items.name: A Major Lifetime Event
items.entry: The 2,000-year anniversary of the sealing is a big deal. One of the characters or an NPC they know is from Argen-Tor, and they feel the need to return to observe this holiday.

entries.name: The Sealing Festival
entries: ({@adventure Map 1|AnEvilUnsealed|1|Adventure Map 1})

The town of Argen-Tor winds its way back and forth amongst the towering plant life of the Oroborus Jungle. Stone walkways lead to small, single-story houses with tiled roofs. Fat fruits tremble on swinging branches in the breeze, ripe for harvest, and people hurry to and fro. Many are gathered at the lion statues at the base of the town, laughing, dancing, and enjoying street food. At the top of the town squats a colossal red gate, sealed shut by four iron chains with links larger than a human. Moss and lichen grow on the chains and their mechanisms; they haven't moved in an age.

The characters have the chance to enjoy the festival and meet the townsfolk. If they came here because of the fiendish influence story hook, they may also want to search for anything connecting to fiends. Run the Festival Attractions section for as long as you'd like. When you're ready to move on, see the next section ({@adventure The Plot Exposed|AnEvilUnsealed|0|The Plot Exposed}).

entries.name: Festival Attractions
entries: The heroes have the chance to participate in festival games, try food, and engage in other activities.

entries.name: Street Food
entries: A dwarven woman named Amea (Ah-MAY-uh) has set up a barbecue near the stone lion steps, where she sells seasoned skewers of meat to passersby. She has several meats the characters perhaps haven't tried before. The menu is a preview of what the heroes may find if and when they venture into the jungle: {@creature Axe Beak|XMM}, {@creature Owlbear|XMM}, roasted vegetables, spiced fruits, or a strange "mystery meat." She charges tourists 5 GP for each skewer.

entries.name: Mystery Meat
entries: Amea isn't sure what the mystery meat is (thus the mystery). The hunters who brought it to her described a coal-black four-legged creature with large fangs. The meat tastes blackened, even though that's not the technique Amea's using to barbecue. With a successful {@dc 18} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana} or {@skill Nature}) check, a character can identify this as the meat of a {@creature Hell Hound|XMM}.

entries.name: Shipment Escort
entries: If the characters used the shipment escort story hook, they can take the shipment here to Amea. She pays the characters and begins cooking the food immediately. She also offers each character their choice of a skewer for free.

entries.name: Fiend-Felling Dance
entries: Close to the gate, a trio of string musicians plays a jaunty tune. Villagers here take turns performing a dance that has been practiced in Argen-Tor for generations. An elven man named Navite (Na-VEE-teh) is teaching children the dance.

entries.name: Navite's History
entries: If the characters speak with Navite, he explains that this dance is the Fiend-Felling Dance, a collection of steps that mirror the fight between the Great Hero and the Great Evil. Two thousand years ago, these steps served as self-defense instruction. Now, it is just tradition. Navite is the great grandson of the Great Hero. This dance has been passed down in his family for only three elven generations, meaning its steps have not been changed much with the years as it would with a human tradition.

Navite invites the characters to join a lesson. A character who succeeds on a {@dc 18} Charisma ({@skill Performance}), Strength ({@skill Athletics}), or Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check learns the steps of the dance. They can use an action to perform the dance. When they do, they cast {@spell Protection from Evil and Good} on themself without using a spell slot once per day. The save DC for this spell is determined by the ability the character used to learn the dance (Charisma, Strength, or Dexterity).

entries.name: Boon Too Good?
entries: Learning how to cast a spell permanently just from succeeding one ability check might be too powerful of a reward for your table. That's okay! If you'd like, you can make it so that the Fiend-Felling Dance only works while the characters are in Argen-Tor and the surrounding area. Perhaps the dance is calling on the spirits of the jungle for protection, and if the heroes are too far away the spirits cannot come to their aid!

entries.name: Play of the Great Hero
entries: In the town center, performers put on a spectacle. It's a play, a recreation of the battle between the Great Hero and the Great Evil. It depicts an elven monk sealing a white, spiky devil into the ground at the base of the jungle canyon, and then ordering the gate be built to seal the canyon path off from Argen-Tor and the rest of the world.

Characters who watch this play can make an Intelligence ({@skill History} or {@skill Religion}) check to recall or intuit a few more pieces of the story. The roll they get determines how much information they glean. A higher roll indicates that the character surmised everything that a lower roll would have granted them:

items: {@b 15:} The Great Evil from the story is a type of devil.
{@b 18:} This Great Evil has the power to manipulate living creatures from beyond the seal.
{@b 22+:} The method the Great Hero used to seal away the devil is imperfect. Even now, pieces of his fiendish magic should be seeping into the cracks of the seal.

entries.name: The Troll Cage
entries: A bored cleric sits beside an iron cage with a cheerful {@creature Troll} standing inside. People can choose to step into the cage and take a beating by the troll. The cleric heals the injured after the troll has beaten them {@condition Unconscious}. If anyone can withstand 18 seconds locked in the troll cage (3 rounds), they will receive a prize: the valuable {@item Sneezing Beret|DMSecretWeapon24}.
If a hero chooses to take the challenge, the following rules apply:

items: They must enter the cage alone, and last 3 rounds without falling {@condition Unconscious} from the troll's attacks.
The player cannot take any {@variantrule Action|XPHB} while in the cage, only stand there.
The troll attacks at {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}. It makes one attack per round, has a +11 to hit, and deals {@damage 2d10 + 6} Bludgeoning damage on a hit. It attacks non-lethally.
Although heroes cannot take {@variantrule Action|XPHB} while inside the cage, there is no rule preventing them from casting a spell in advance, or preparing in some other way.
Heroes outside the cage may try to aid their companion in the cage, but they must be subtle. Any visible displays of magic made to aid their ally will result in disqualification.

entries: Players are restored to full HP after leaving the cage by the bored cleric.

entries.name: Pin the Wand on the Orcus
entries: A charming illustration of the great fiend Orcus has been painted onto the trunk of a large tree. Festival patrons are taking turns blindfolding each other and attempting to pin a wand onto Orcus at the right spot.

If a hero would like to try, they can make an attack roll at {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} using the {@item Counterfeit Demon Wand|DMSecretWeapon24} as an {@variantrule Improvised Weapons|XPHB|Improvised Weapon}. Creatures with {@sense Blindsight} or demonic heritage ignore the {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the attack. An attack roll of 18 or above is a success. Each hero can only make one attempt.
On a fail, a hero receives a small pin that reads "I'm bad at games."
On a success, a hero can keep their {@item Counterfeit Demon Wand|DMSecretWeapon24}.

entries.name: The Plot Exposed
entries: ({@adventure Map 2|AnEvilUnsealed|1|Adventure Map 2})

The sun sets on the Sealing Festival, and the fires go up. At first it's the torches and lanterns of the townsfolk. But the scent of sulfur and brimstone wafts from on high. Five men in red robes stand near the gate with open arms over a fire of their own making. There is a flash of light, and devils erupt from the fire. They chase the villagers into their homes as the lead cultist busies himself with the mechanisms to the sealed door.
The characters, having made their way to the center of town near the lion steps, must now climb the steps and put a stop to this before the gate is unsealed. Roll Initiative.

Immediately in front of the party is a {@creature Bearded Devil} who seeks to halt their ascent. Four {@creature Cultist||Cultists} are also blocking some of the alleyways and quicker passageways up. At the top near the gate, the {@creature Devil Cult Master|DMSecretWeapon24} and four {@creature imp||Imps} are attempting to get the gate open.

entries.name: Opening the Gate
entries: The cult master and the four {@creature imp||Imps} act on {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} count 20. During the devil cult master's turn, they use their action to attempt to undo the mechanisms that unlock the gate, and the {@creature imp||Imps} take the {@action Help} action (giving {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the check). The master must succeed on a {@dc 14} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) check (modifier +2) to unlock one lock. There are four mechanisms and four chains. After four successes, the gate is opened (see "{@adventure What Happens Next|AnEvilUnsealed|0|What Happens Next}").

If the party gets too close to the door while it is still being opened, the {@creature imp||Imps} will split off one-by-one to slow them while the master continues to open the gate. If the party reaches the door with no allied devils or {@creature Cultist||Cultists} to protect the master, he will turn and attempt to kill the party himself before opening the door.

entries.name: Make it Harder!
entries: This encounter assumes you're throwing these enemies at the players all at the same time. Since the monsters are spaced out, if your party is well prepared to maintain distance, you can throw some extra spanners in the works! If your players are a little too alive and well, add one {@creature Bearded Devil}, two {@creature Cultist||Cultists} or one more {@creature Cultist Fanatic} that bursts from the fire just before they reach the gate!

entries.name: What Happens Next
entries: Whether the characters stopped the {@creature Cultist||Cultists} before they could get the door open determines the next path of this adventure.

entries.name: Mission Success: Cultists Stopped!
entries: If the heroes succeed in stopping the {@creature Cultist||Cultists} before all four chains are unlocked, read or paraphrase the following:

With the {@creature Cultist||Cultists} subdued, the town breathes a sigh of relief. Smiles once again begin to return to the people of Argen-Tor. As the string trio strikes up a tune to celebrate, tiny cracks spread across the door and glow a malignant red. The door bends under the weight of the magic, then explodes into millions of tiny pieces. Beyond the destroyed door is a trail leading down into a canyon of darkness.

Since the {@creature Cultist||Cultists} couldn't complete their mission, {@creature Zanthropus|DMSecretWeapon24} had to use all the energy he'd been storing up on this plane to bust the door through. Since he has not yet stepped through the portal, this move has significantly limited what he can do on this plane at the moment.

entries.name: Mission Failure: Cultists Opened the Door
entries: If the {@creature Cultist||Cultists} succeed in disabling all four chain mechanisms, read or paraphrase the following:

The chains rattle and shake away from the door, kicking up moss and dirt and dust. The massive door, sealed shut for two thousand years to this very night, rumbles. With a loud, creaking groan the doors open inward, revealing a trail leading down into a canyon of darkness.

A wave of fiendish energy, palpable and thick with the scent of sulfur, crashes over the town of Argen-Tor, washing the town in a terror they've not known for generations. The {@creature Cultist||Cultists} rejoice, only for their cackles of delight to morph into screams of pain as the devilish energy saps their bodies, siphoning each remaining cultist's lifeforce for the benefit of their master.
Each creature within 30 feet of the gate must make a {@dc 14} Charisma saving throw. On a failure, a creature takes 9 ({@damage 2d8}) Psychic damage, or half as much on a success.

entries.name: To Stop a Devil
entries: ({@adventure Map 3|AnEvilUnsealed|1|Adventure Map 3})

The climb down the canyon is steep and difficult. As you get lower, the forest disappears from view. In the place of ripe plants and sweet aromas are blighted vegetation and the bitter chill of night. An unsettling energy fills the thinning air, along with howls, hoots, and growls.

entries.name: Encounters on the Descent
entries: The descent into the canyon is not easy; the heroes will face opposition as they approach the pit. For this series of encounters, use the bottom half of {@adventure Map 3|AnEvilUnsealed|1|Adventure Map 3}.

entries.name: First Encounter: One Owlbear and Two Axe Beaks
entries: An {@creature Owlbear} and two {@creature Axe Beak||Axe Beaks} scratch around at the blighted vegetation in the canyon. They block the only path down, though it may be possible to sneak by should the party wish to avoid unnecessary combat.

entries.name: Zanthropus's Influence
entries: If the {@creature Cultist||Cultists} opened the door in the previous section before the heroes could stop them, Zanthropus's influence is felt throughout the canyon. In this encounter, the monsters have the following changes:

items: The monster's creature type is Fiend.
The monster is resistant to Fire damage.
Magical {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB} does not impede the creature's vision.

entries: The party can attempt to bypass the monsters with a collective {@dc 15} Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check. On a fail, the monsters attack.

entries.name: Second Encounter: The Devil Tree's Game
entries: Out of the earth, a flaming tree sprouts before the party, its branches wreathed in fire that sends dancing embers out into the night. On its trunk, a hateful, sneering face glares down at the heroes. The tree will let them pass but only if they can answer its riddles, or defeat it in battle (use the {@creature Burning Treant|DMSecretWeapon24} stat block).
If the heroes offer an incorrect answer to a riddle it immediately attacks. If they answer all three correctly, it allows them to pass down the canyon path.

items.name: Riddle 1 (Easy)
entries: I am not alive, but I grow; I don't have lungs, but I need air; I don't have a mouth, but water kills me. What am I? ({@b Answer: Fire}).

items.name: Riddle 2 (Medium)
entries: I have no end, but I am the end of all that begins. What am I? ({@b Answer: Death}).

items.name: Riddle 3 (Hard)
entries: I am your first and greatest guardian against all that does you harm, / But every time I rear my head you cower at my charm, / There is no creature living who doesn't think of me with dread, / But without me as your watchman you'd very soon be dead, / You've met me many times, and will meet me many more, / I shine brightest when a life grows dim, in heartbreak, and in war, / Answer this last riddle, friend, or you'll face me now, again. / What am I? ({@b Answer: Pain}).

entries.name: The Canyon Pit

entries: At the pit of the jungle canyon sits the shrine of the Great Hero, complete with a stone statue depicting the elven monk. Red and purple light glow from the Great Hero's three eyes, as well as indentations in the surrounding stone. Before him in the ground is a round portal made of white hot energy. The statue of the Great Hero splinters, then shatters.

Gurgling comes from the pit-like portal, a pitiful attempt at mirth and laughter, as a devil rises from within. {@creature Zanthropus|DMSecretWeapon24} is all bones, his spiky limbs tipped in blood, wings calcified, and snarl pronounced. "At last," he cries. "After two thousand years, I'm free!"
Run this encounter on the top half of {@adventure Map 3|AnEvilUnsealed|1|Adventure Map 3}, using the {@creature Zanthropus|DMSecretWeapon24} stat block.

entries.name: Zanthropus's Special Actions
entries: Now that {@creature Zanthropus|DMSecretWeapon24} has desecrated this place, he can bend the environment to his will. At the end of Initiative Count 20, he can take one of the following actions:

items: Acid bubbles up on a 15-foot square on the ground within 50 feet of {@creature Zanthropus|DMSecretWeapon24}. All creatures who start their turn in that area or enter the area for the first time in a turn must succeed on a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw or take 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Acid damage. This effect lasts until the start of Initiative Count 20.

Zanthropus's own bones jut out even farther. Whenever a creature makes a melee attack against {@creature Zanthropus|DMSecretWeapon24}, they take 5 ({@damage 2d4}) Piercing damage. {@creature Zanthropus|DMSecretWeapon24} can take this action 4 times in total (to a maximum of {@damage 8d4} Piercing damage).

{@creature Zanthropus|DMSecretWeapon24} flares the lights and gives himself an otherworldly appearance. All creatures within 50 feet of him must succeed on a {@dc 15} Wisdom saving throw or become {@condition Frightened} of {@creature Zanthropus|DMSecretWeapon24} until the end of their next turn.

entries: If Zanthropus' {@creature Cultist||Cultists} failed to open the gate, forcing him to expend his own power to do so, roll a {@dice d20} at the start of {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} count 20 each round. On a 10 or lower, {@creature Zanthropus|DMSecretWeapon24} can't take an environmental action this round.

entries.name: Conclusion
entries: With {@creature Zanthropus|DMSecretWeapon24} defeated, Argen-Tor is safe once more. As the characters return from the jungle's pit, the villagers emerge from their homes. Though it is very late at night, the band strikes up a tune and the people dance. Amea's skewers are on the house for the champions of the millennium.

Navite offers the characters the sword passed down through his family since the time of the Great Hero (a {@item +2 Longsword}). Now that {@creature Zanthropus|DMSecretWeapon24} is defeated, he has no use for it.

data.name: Mush! Food Rush!
entries: MUSH! There's nothing in the rule book that says a dog can't be the hero. Heroes overcome all challenges in their way and arrive in the nick of time to save the people who need them, which are all qualities within the capabilities of a canine. Sometimes there's no one better suited for the job than a dog (and his entire party, of course).

Mush! Food Rush! is an adventure for 4 level 2 heroes and 1 dog hero transporting emergency provisions across a winter wasteland to the kids in a remote dwarven enclave. These heroes must take care to protect their cargo from the harsh elements and a very dangerous, very hungry winter spirit.

entries.name: Background
entries: The dwarven compound Vy Nomburo is nestled into a remote valley of the Godfinger mountains. Most of the year they're able to trade with their neighbors without issue, but the travel routes disappear under harsh snowfall come the winter season. Vy Nomburo has to rely on the nearest neighboring town of Sicklepick to send them crates of food and medicine via sled teams until the travel routes open back up.

This year, the Godfinger mountains have been bombarded by an especially terrible snowstorm. The angry spirit of the first sled wolf has taken control of the weather and now deliberately attacks the sled teams as they leave Sicklepick. No sled has made it to Vy Nomburo this year, nor have they returned to town.

The dwarven compound is running out of time, and Sicklepick is running out of sleds. The fate of the men, women, and children of Vy Nomburo rests on the back of a stray flickerhound who's ready to brave the storm.

entries.name: Mondo
entries: Mondo is a shaggy, sassy {@creature Flickerhound|DMSecretWeapon24|flickerhound} who teleported into Sicklepick from the Feywild over a year ago and still hasn't found a way back. While he can't talk, he's quite intelligent and understands the situation the compound is facing.

Mondo can be controlled by the GM or a hero player for this adventure. Mondo's main goal is to keep the sled out of danger and protect it from hungry enemies, but the dog is also capable of supporting his comrades with magic.

entries.name: Setup
entries: The (non-canine) heroes can begin the adventure in one of two ways:

items: The heroes are residents of Sicklepick. They are called upon to meet with the burgomaster on time sensitive business.

The heroes are traveling between towns when they encounter Mondo hooked up to a sled just outside of Sicklepick. Mondo does everything he can, pulling on clothes, stealing items, or playing dead, in order to lead the heroes to the burgomaster.

entries: If Mondo doesn't meet the heroes outside, then he's already with the burgomaster. The burgomaster is worried sick and feels bad relying on Mondo, but they have no other choice.

Upon meeting with the burgomaster, they are tasked to protect the last remaining food sled set to travel into the Godfinger mountains towards Vy Nomburo. If they can't reach the dwarven compound in two days, the people could starve. The burgomaster is willing to pay 10 GP to each hero upfront, and another 5 GP if they return safely.

The heroes may choose to donate their fee to the people of Vy Nomburo. Doing so grants each hero and Mondo a point of {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB} and 10 {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}, as the gentle, guiding magic of the universe responds to their generosity in kind.

entries.name: The Food Sled
entries: The sled creaks loudly, barely holding up its cargo off the snow. It is considered a Large object, and while Mondo is hooked up to it, the sled moves directly behind him. Each time the sled takes a total of 15 damage, it loses a crate of food. If it loses three crates of food, there will not be enough food to feed Vy Nomburo. A hero can repair the sled and its cargo, allowing it to regain 15 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} during a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Don't Lose Hope
entries: Should the sled lose too many crates of food, there's still a chance of finding lingering crates from the recent expeditions. Once per hour, a hero can make a {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check; on success, they uncover a lost crate, allowing the heroes to increase their own crate count by 1. Mondo can aid one such check with his heightened sense of smell, granting {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the heroes' first attempt.

entries.name: Mush!
entries: When the heroes are ready, they can take off towards the Godfinger mountains. The snowstorm swirls and blisters just outside of town, and only grows more violent the deeper into the valley they travel. If the heroes stay in place for longer than 1 hour without cover from the elements or a {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold damage, they lose one unspent {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Die}. If they have none remaining, they instead take {@damage 1d6} Cold damage.

Vy Nomburo can be reached in a day and a half at a hurried pace. The heroes will only be able to take 1 {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} and 1 {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} during the journey. If they face any setbacks that force them to lose time, they can replace their {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} with 1 additional {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: The Howling Storm
entries: {@adventure Encounter Map 1|MushFoodRush|1|Adventure Map 1}

1 mile away from town, the storm clouds thicken and carve themselves into the shape of a giant wolf head in the sky, staring down the heroes and their sled. If the heroes try to press onward, the wolf head howls, conjuring a {@creature Polar Wolf|DMSecretWeapon24|polar wolf} and two {@creature ice mephit||Ice Mephits} out of snow that immediately attack.

The heroes start at the south end of the map and their goal is to either defeat all enemies or reach the north end of the map without losing the sled. The mephits focus on attacking the sled, while the polar wolf aims to kill the closest threat.

entries.name: Into the Valley
entries: {@adventure Encounter Map 2|MushFoodRush|1|Adventure Map 2}

The only noise disturbing this area is the whipping of wind and the crunching of snow beneath the heroes' feet. High above the valley, massive amounts of snow pile precariously on the Godfinger ridge. Any hero with a passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) of 12 or higher can tell that any loud sound might cause an avalanche.

If the heroes decide to proceed through this area quietly, they can make a {@dc 13} group Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check to muffle their noises. If at least half the group succeeds, they pass through the valley entrance without incident. Otherwise, or if they don't bother to move quietly, the rumble of snow booms through the valley and threatens to overtake the expedition.

In the event of an avalanche, the heroes start two squares in from the south end of the map and roll for {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}. The heroes must reach the north end of the map with the sled in one piece. At the end of every other turn, the snow overtakes a 5-foot row of the map, moving northward. If the snow enters a creature or object's square, they must succeed on a {@dc 12} Dexterity saving throw to take {@damage 1d4} Cold damage and be pushed into an unoccupied square 5 feet northward. If they fail, they take {@damage 2d6} Cold damage and are {@condition Restrained} by the snow until an adjacent ally dislodges them as a bonus action during their own turn.

Should the heroes be overcome by the avalanche, they fall {@condition Unconscious}. They awaken 30 minutes later, being pulled from the snow by Mondo, with a single hit point each and 2 crates lost from the sled.

entries.name: Bad Lake
entries: {@adventure Encounter Map 3|MushFoodRush|1|Adventure Map 3}

The valley walls rise to 80 feet high, while the valley trail lays flooded and frozen over. The heroes start at the south end, and there's little other option but to skate across the ice until the heroes reach the north.

Each time a creature or object steps onto a 5-foot square of ice, the square cracks and fractures under pressure. If a square is entered three times, it breaks and drops its contents into the icy water below. A creature who falls into the water or starts their turn in it takes {@damage 1d10} Cold damage and must succeed on a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition Paralyzed} until the start of their next turn. An object sinks 10 feet at the end of each round, to a maximum depth of 30 feet.

When the heroes make it halfway across the ice, the heroes hear a howl; six {@creature ice mephit||Ice Mephits} snap off from the valley walls and attack. The mephits purposefully move across fresh ice and attempt to hamper the sled from moving forward. If the sled makes it to the other side of the map, any remaining mephits shatter and blow away in the wind.

entries.name: Lingering Crate
entries: The wreckage of a previous expedition sits near the eastmost side of the lake. A hero with a passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) of 14 or higher near the middle of the ice, or a hero that makes a {@dc 14} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check notices the broken sled and one crate of food still intact. Retrieving the crate and bringing it back to the party's sled allows the heroes to increase their own crate count by 1. If the party has no crates at the time of discovering the sled, they recover 2 instead.

entries.name: The Final Bluster
entries: {@adventure Encounter Map 4|MushFoodRush|1|Adventure Map 4}

1 mile away from the compound, the heroes stand opposite the storm made manifest. A massive, ethereal wolf refuses to let them enter Vy Nomburo without a fight. The heroes can attempt to calm the spirit down, using Mondo to communicate with them.

If the heroes succeed on a {@dc 16} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check, the wolf howls to clear the storm and then disappears. On a failure, or if the heroes draw steel, the {@creature Ethereal Wolf|DMSecretWeapon24|ethereal wolf spirit} attacks.

entries.name: Delivery!
entries: Making it through the storm is no small feat. Upon reaching Vy Nomburo, the heroes are met with a crowd of hungry, thankful dwarves ready to prepare meals and play rowdy music. Before the night is over, a dwarf will have already sculpted a marble statue of Mondo and the team near the front of the compound so that future generations may know their story.

data.name: The Stage of Stories, Act I
entries: Our heroes often need a reminder of why we call them heroes. If you get lost in an adventure felling evil and growing in power, sometimes a good heroic story is enough to rekindle your spirit.

Five level 12 heroes can take part in The Timeless Show and perform in a series of heroic scenes while an ancient lich keeps them on stage. The heroes must decide when is the right time to strike against the boss, balancing their own resources while whittling the lich down with their theatrics.

entries.name: Background
entries: Legends tell of a bard who knew of a million stories by heart. He spent his entire life traveling the land and collecting tales of grandeur. But he wasn't satisfied by the time he reached his deathbed. He craved more and more stories, refusing to die until he had his fill—he inadvertently became a lich.

Legends follow that the bard constructed a spirit jar theater deep in the tundra to force the souls he collected to perform his stories. He now stalks the land in disguise, appearing to heroes as a traveler or a friendly brass dragon, and stealing away new victims in hopes of feeding his insatiable, storied hunger.

entries.name: Setup
entries: This adventure can be played on its own or as a side story in a larger campaign using one of the following hooks:

items.name: The Storyman
items.entry: On the road, the party encounters an old traveler who asks each hero to tell him a tale of how they saved someone in their past. Their surroundings subtly change as they each share a story, until they finally realize they're at a campsite and the traveler is nowhere to be seen.

items.name: Strangers in Paradise
items.entry: Each hero groggily awakens in a clearing, having never met any of the other heroes with them before. The players take turns describing how their hero was knocked out as they get their bearings straight.

entries.name: Overture
entries: {@adventure Map 4|TheStageOfStories|2|Adventure Map 4}

The sky turns overcast and a chill breeze sweeps through the grass. It isn't long before a small hooded figure runs past the heroes while chased by 10 hungry {@creature wolf||Wolves}. The {@creature wolf||Wolves} scatter and flee at the first sign of any threat from the heroes.

The figure is secretly a {@creature Vampire} disguised as a human child, but a hero can see through his disguise with a {@dc 20} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check. If the heroes save him from the {@creature wolf||Wolves}, he starts crying and tries to get close to any hero he can before surprising them with a bite. Alternatively if the heroes see through his disguise, he laughs before shifting into his true appearance and resummoning the {@creature wolf||Wolves} to fight on his side.

When the {@creature Vampire} is defeated, the heroes hear clapping. A spotlight cuts through the clouds and shines down on them. The grass and dirt beneath their feet turns hard and smooth. The illusion disperses, completely giving way to a stage with a single audience member.

entries.name: The Curtain Rises
entries: {@adventure Map 1|TheStageOfStories|2|Adventure Map 1}

The Storyman ({@creature The Elder Storyman|DMSecretWeapon24|Elder Storyman}), a gaunt lich patrician in vibrant gold and blue silk robes with a gaudy velvet headdress, sits alone in the balcony watching the heroes. The crackle and snap of his bones echo through the halls with his every move. "I want... heroes. I want the stories of great warriors. Only... grandeur gives me life."
The lich points a finger at the stage. "You are trapped within my spirit jar. You must venture forth and show me true heroism, or your souls are forfeit."

The Storyman tells the heroes that they can move stage left to venture forth towards the next scene of their adventure. He also allows the heroes to declare that they'd like to enact The Finale at any time, where he finally appears on stage to challenge them. The heroes cannot leave the stage without The Storyman's permission until he is defeated.

entries.name: Upon the Stage
entries: Each time the heroes exit stage left, they appear on the stage from the other side. If they completed the previous scene when they exit the stage, they enter into a new scene with the following changes to the audience:

items: Any bystanders the heroes let die in the previous scene take front row seats. They are unable to talk or act; they stare at the heroes in silence.

Any enemies defeated by the heroes take seats in the balcony and jeer loudly. Once per scene, when a hero makes a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, The Storyman can reduce their roll by 1 for every five enemies in the audience.

The Storyman becomes younger. The maximum {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} in his stat block reduces by 30. After five completed scenes, he becomes a young man and his stat block changes into {@creature The Wandering Storyman|DMSecretWeapon24}. In this form, his maximum {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} are reduced by 20 for each subsequent completed scene. A hero can gauge how young he's become with a {@dc 14} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check.

entries: The Storyman will attempt to enact the Finale after eight scenes, unless the GM chooses to add additional scenes and allows the heroes to continue performing. Should the players run enough scenes, it may be possible to de-age The Storyman to "death" by reducing his maximum {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} to 0, defeating him at his own game without ever fighting directly. It's up to the players to determine when they're confident enough to enact The Finale, should they choose to do so before The Storyman does.

entries.name: Interludes
entries: Should the heroes feel the need to take a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} between scenes, they can ask The Storyman to clear the stage for them. In exchange, The Storyman requests a true tale of heroism from one of the heroes' past adventures. The hero must then succeed on a {@dc 20} Charisma saving throw, or lose all memory of their story and the people involved in it.

entries.name: The Scenes
entries: The scenes can be played in the order presented or chosen by the game master. Each scene includes its completion requirements along with the map variant required to play it.

entries.name: Who Do You Save?
entries: {@b How to Complete:} Save the commoner, save the nobles, or allow all four of them to die.
{@adventure Map 2|TheStageOfStories|2|Adventure Map 2}
The stage burns endlessly. The air hangs thick with smoke. {@creature imp||Imps} dance along the curtains as the heroes enter the scene.

Three {@creature horned devil||Horned Devils} torment three {@creature noble||Noble Dwarves} and one {@creature Commoner} human. One devil carries the human by their foot in midair and threatens to drop them. The second devil corners the nobles on the other side of the stage with their pitchfork. The third stands before the heroes and addresses them directly.
"You've arrived too late! We claim these souls! Try and stop either of my siblings and the other will slay their quarry. Come for both and you'll have to face me, too."
The devil flicks a heavy tail against the ground as the flames grow hotter. The only sounds louder than the crackle of burning wood are the screams of the helpless.

The players have 1 minute to discuss their options before the {@creature horned devil||Horned Devils} kill their prey. The devils won't help each other unless the heroes attempt to save both groups of victims.

{@b "Oh by the way,"} Should the heroes question the reality of their circumstances or the people in it, The Storyman's voice booms over the fire to let them know every soul in this theater is as real as their own.

If you are playing this adventure as a part of a larger campaign, any victims the heroes encounter can be replaced with people they've met before. They'll make it out alive and return to their homes after the adventure as long as the heroes can save them.

entries.name: A Roc And A Hard Place
entries: {@b How to Complete:} Save the roc's eggs, allow them to be destroyed, or the roc dies.
{@adventure Map 1|TheStageOfStories|2|Adventure Map 1}
Winds whip across the stage. Massive stones hang in the air. It feels as though the theater relocated to the peak of a mountain, making it nearly impossible to breathe.

A {@creature Roc} screeches as it soars through the theater while two {@creature clay golem||Clay Golems} climb the stones. The golems are after the eggs in a nest atop the highest floating stone. When the heroes enter the scene, the {@creature Roc} treats them as if they are a threat and relentlessly attacks the heroes.
There are eight huge stones above the stage that hang about 15 feet apart from each other. The golems relentlessly leap from stone to stone until they reach the eggs or go berserk.

A hero can attempt to calm down the roc and turn its attention to the golems with a {@dc 25} Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling}) check. Each time they fail, however, the roc makes a single beak attack against the hero, no action required.

entries.name: What Is Your Justice?
entries: {@b How to Complete:} Execute the giant or set her free.
{@adventure Map 3|TheStageOfStories|2|Adventure Map 3}
The heroes enter onto a submerged stage. The water is breathable, but dense. A massive shell, flanked by coral and rock, takes center stage.

A {@creature Storm Giant} named Kilza Typhoon sits inside the shell, magically shackled to its mouth. She's been atoning for her crimes at the bottom of the ocean for centuries. When she sees the heroes, she can only hang her head in shame.
"Thousands of smallfolk. Sailors earning their living. Lovers on the dock. Civilizations along the coast."
The giant hardly moves. Barnacles bubble all along her skin. Her gaze is fixed upon her scarred, open palms.
"Cast your judgement upon the wretched Typhoon. My life is owed for the many I've taken."
Kilza invites the heroes to kill her. If they accept, roll for {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, but have her do nothing on her turn.

Alternatively, the heroes could set the giant free. Breaking the shackles requires a {@dc 30} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check. The DC is reduced by 10 if any hero provides a strong reason for letting Kilza go free (other than wanting to complete the scene).
If the shackles are broken, she wordlessly stares at each hero for a long time before swimming upwards into the black void of the ceiling.

entries.name: The Blood Between Us
entries: {@b How to Complete:} Kill the vampire, or fend off the doppelgangers before they kill the vampire.
{@adventure Map 4|TheStageOfStories|2|Adventure Map 4}
The moon hangs above a dark, foggy stage and paints an eerie glow atop the gnarled trees. A large stake takes center stage in front of an angry crowd chanting "Kill the vampire!"

A {@creature Vampire} with only 20 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} is tied to the stake, while 21 humans jeer at them with torches. In truth, the one old man {@creature Commoner} is alone among 20 {@creature doppelganger||Doppelgangers} in disguise who had taken over his village. The vampire used to be the old man's daughter, but wanted to stay in the village to protect him until he died.
When the heroes enter the scene, one of the jeering "humans", an older woman, greets them and provides them with their task.

"Thank goodness you're here!" the lady exclaims. "This vampire has been feeding on our villagers, but we've finally caught her. However, we worry that as soon as we stake her, she'll fly into a rampage and attack!"
"Please. Would you do the deed, heroes? Or would you leave us to our fate?"
The heroes only have enough time to ask three questions before the crowd light the stake on fire. If they do so, or the heroes attack the vampire, she breaks free and attacks the heroes.

However, if the heroes are suspicious of the crowd, they can see through a doppelganger's disguise with a {@dc 16} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check. Revealing a doppelganger forces the crowd's hand; half of them go after the vampire while the other half attack the heroes.

entries.name: Intermission
entries: {@adventure Map 1|TheStageOfStories|2|Adventure Map 1}

Should the Storyman run out of scenes, he clears the stage for the heroes and provides them with a chance to take a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} while he prepares the next set. The show picks back up in {@adventure Act II|TheStageOfStories|1} after the heroes are rested and the lich is back in his seat.

data.name: The Stage of Stories, Act II
entries: When last we left our heroes, they were trapped in the sick stage show of the Storyman, a terrible lich who feeds on tales of grandeur and becomes younger. The longer they perform, the better their chances will be to finally take on their captor and escape!

entries.name: Returning From Intermission
entries: {@adventure Map 1|TheStageOfStories|2|Adventure Map 1}
When the Storyman returns to his seat, he provides the heroes with an opportunity to change an outcome of a scene they've previously completed.
The lich extends an open hand to the stage in a slow, smooth flourish. There was no crunching of bones or sprays of dust; he now had weight and youth in his movements.
"If you could change the story," he started. "Save a life lost, or find justice knowing what you know now... which scene would you change? Tell me, and we'll rewrite it together."

If the heroes decide to change the outcome of a scene they've completed, any creatures in the audience from that scene completely disappear and the heroes regain one additional {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Die}. However, the Storyman also gains 30 maximum {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} as he ages after changing the past.

entries.name: The Scenes
entries: The scenes can be played in the order presented or chosen by the game master. Each scene includes its completion requirements along with the map variant required to play it.

entries.name: Value of a Life
entries: {@b How to Complete:} Free the prisoner or take the treasure.
{@adventure Map 6|TheStageOfStories|2|Adventure Map 6}
The room is darkly lit and the air tastes stale. Two unmarked iron doors are embedded into the back curtains, now hanging stiff like a stone wall.

The heroes come across two {@creature Sphinx of Valor|XMM|sphinxes of Valor}, one red and one blue, each guarding a door. One door leads to a room containing 10,000 GP and 6 diamonds worth 500 GP each. The other door locks away a {@creature Commoner} Gnomish prisoner in a tiny cell. You can flip a coin to determine which sphinx's door contains which room. The sphinxes attack anyone who attempts to open or discern what's behind a door before engaging with their trial.
The red sphinx hails the heroes over to hear her riddle.

"Behold, heroes. We grant you access to one door. One opens to grand riches. The other saves an air-breathing, innocent man. The door you choose causes the other to collapse and destroy its contents."

The sphinx puffs out her chest and gazes sharply at her audience. "You may ask the two of us a single question. I may lie—my brother always talks true, but speaks only in numbers. Your question must be factual, no hypotheticals nor conditionals."
