Asking any question to either sphinx about what the other sphinx would say causes them to use their First Roar action. Hypothetical questions don't count. If any hero suggests numbering the doors, the doors begin to suddenly move in circles along the surface of the curtain, independently of their sphinxes.

The most canonically "correct" question to this riddle is posed to the blue sphinx who speaks truthfully in numbers about anything pertaining to the number of heartbeats or breaths taken behind a door. The heroes can also ask the blue sphinx the value hidden behind a door; he responds with a number if the room contains treasure and can only look down at the ground if the room contains the prisoner.

When the heroes have asked their question, the red sphinx calls upon them to choose a door. The door that isn't picked melts to the floor (amid the sounds of crying if the heroes didn't save the prisoner). Both sphinxes then exit the stage, leaving the heroes alone with their choice.

entries.name: The Iron Maiden
entries: {@b How to Complete:} The iron maiden takes a life.
{@adventure Map 1|TheStageOfStories|2|Adventure Map 1}
A massive metal cabinet looms open center stage, lined with rows of rusty spikes hungry for blood. A young orc man stands contemplating in front of it.
When the heroes enter, the orc {@creature Commoner} beckons them over to listen to his dilemma.
"Isn't this interesting?" the man asks, gesturing at the iron maiden. "I've been trapped in this dungeon for three years. Three years without seeing my family! And finally, I've found the exit."
"Apparently the only way we'll escape this place is if someone dies in that thing."
The orc lets out a deep sigh, scratches his head, and shrugs. "I kinda wish I never found the exit."

The way forward won't open until a creature enters the iron maiden and is killed by it. The man will pace back and forth and delay for five game minutes before finally stepping inside unless a hero takes his place.

Regardless of who steps into the iron maiden, the lights go out in the theater as soon as the door is closed on the cabinet. When the lights turn back on, the iron maiden is gone without a trace and the heroes can continue onward.

If a hero made the choice to sacrifice themself, they take damage equal to half their {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and appear {@condition Prone} on the stage floor where the cabinet was. If the hero survives, the Storyman laughs from his seat and shouts at the heroes, "A fine performance, but I won't let you leave that easy!"

entries.name: Breathtaking
entries: {@b How to Complete:} Break out of the room, or the elves die.
{@adventure Map 6|TheStageOfStories|2|Adventure Map 6}
A thick green haze covers the stage. It rapidly swirls and billows, but never flows into the audience.

The stage is filled with noxious gas. A {@spell Prismatic Wall} encases the stage on all sides except the way the heroes enter from. A small family of three {@creature Commoner} elves huddle and hold their breaths in the center of the stage, while a {@creature Cloud Giant} looms over them laughing maniacally.

Roll for {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}. The heroes have 2 rounds total to save the elves. For every two turns that pass, they must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or gain a level of {@condition exhaustion}. The DC is equal to 16 + the number of turns that have passed.

The {@creature Cloud Giant} only takes action if she is attacked. Should the heroes reduce her to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, she chuckles and tells them "you should have turned around as soon as you stepped foot out here," before keeling over.

Any hero can take the {@action Search} action on their turn to examine their surroundings for a clue. Determining that the prismatic wall doesn't encase the way they entered the stage has a {@dc 16}, unless a player realizes the truth on their own.
If the heroes can lead the elves off the stage from the way they entered, the gas and the wall both clear after 10 turns and they're able to proceed forward.

entries.name: Feed the Beast
entries: {@b How to Complete:} Convince the priests to flee, defeat the tongue, or allow the priests to be eaten.
{@adventure Map 1|TheStageOfStories|2|Adventure Map 1}
The wooden floor bends and squishes like a marsh. Hot, sticky air sweeps across the stage rhythmically.

The heroes arrive to find four halfling {@creature priest||Priests} equidistantly spaced out along the edge of the stage, sitting with their eyes closed, ready to sacrifice their lives for a protective creature known as "Oth." The titan has saved their region from countless invaders and requires regular tribute for their service. If these priests don't make the sacrifice, Oth will completely erase their civilization.

The players must convince the priests not to give their lives, or allow them to die to escape. A hero that makes an argument to a priest can convince them with a successful {@dc 18} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check. Every 30 seconds or after each {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} the heroes make, the floor slides each priest 5 feet towards the back curtains, until eventually falling into a massive, gaping throat.

After convincing one priest, or after all priests have been slid halfway across the stage, a massive tongue unfurls from the back curtain and slams onto the ground. Oth's tongue (use the {@creature Purple Worm} stat block) attacks the heroes and attempts to eat them while they talk to the priests.
Whenever a creature would be "swallowed" by the tongue, they are, instead, pulled behind the curtain into the stage's throat.

entries.name: Finale
entries: {@adventure Map 1|TheStageOfStories|2|Adventure Map 1}

When the heroes invite The Storyman to join the performance, all NPCs vanish and the stage darkens. Lit by a spotlight, the lich floats to the stage and attacks the heroes. The battle spans the entire theater, no longer limited to the stage.

The Storyman can use the crowd to protect himself. Whenever he would take damage, he can use a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to summon a creature from the crowd to take half the damage for him, completely destroying their soul.
Should the heroes defeat The Storyman, the entire theater clears out. A light shines from the exit behind the lich's seat in the balcony. The heroes can head home.

entries.name: Encore?
entries: If the heroes find clever means of escaping the theater early, or they felt the finale ended too abruptly, The Storyman will refuse to let the story conclude.
Upon exiting the theater, the heroes find themselves in a cold, blustery snowscape. They stand opposite an {@creature Adult Brass Dragon} bearing The Storyman's face.

The heroes can choose to contend with the dragon directly, or attack the entrance to the theater. The gateway is a structure that has AC 20, 50 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Necrotic, Poison, and Psychic damage. The dragon and the theater slowly fade away when the gateway is destroyed.

data.name: The Lighthouse Keeper
entries: The Lighthouse Keeper is an adventure for four level 3 heroes that requires the party to use their skills and resourcefulness to survive a shipwreck, explore a ransacked harbor, and face off against the fiery monster responsible for its destruction.

entries.name: Background
entries: Though Craggy Island's rocky coastline renders it a challenging port to navigate, its strategic position along naval trading routes makes it a popular stop for sailors needing to restock or undertake vital ship repairs. The more accomplished crews have even learned to navigate around the craggy outcroppings by night in emergencies, using the port's famous lighthouse as a guide.

The heroes are sailing on a well-established merchant ship heading to Craggy Island to replenish supplies. The captain, venerated for his prowess in navigating Craggy's treacherous outskirts, is well-acquainted with its beacon lighthouse. Though he had planned to anchor at sea, a storm rushed in, forcing him to attempt a nighttime mooring. However, by unfortunate coincidence, tonight, the lighthouse is in darkness. Disaster strikes as the ship's hull dashes against a rocky outcropping, the crew scattered into the sea and the captain going down with his ship.

The heroes must swim away to the harbor, discover the terrified dockmaster hiding amid the ransacked wreckage, and learn that the lighthouse keeper has somehow transfigured into a fiery monster. The dockmaster begs the party to help, if not for him, at least for the many ships sailing ever closer to their own rocky demise...

entries.name: Shipwreck

entries: Having lifted anchor this morning beneath clear skies and atop gentle waves, none of you anticipated such a vicious storm come nightfall. The sails are torn, the masts splintered, and the deck drenched as the ship pitches and rolls in the tempest. Though your captain intended to anchor at sea and dock at Craggy Island by daylight, he has no choice but to attempt an emergency mooring in the pitch black of night.

What's worse, the lighthouse that ordinarily provides a way marker is in darkness. Despite your scrambling efforts to obey the captain's every order, suddenly, you crash into a rocky outcrop, the waves hammering your ship against it over and over, smashing your hull to splinters...

The heroes are cast into the ocean and must swim to shore, 150 feet away. For every turn a character spends in the water, they must succeed on a {@dc 10} Constitution saving throw. On four or more failures, they gain 1 {@condition Exhaustion} level. On {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} count 0 each round, the GM should also roll on the table below:

rows: Underwater vents erupt, creating columns of scalding hot water. Characters must succeed on a {@dc 13} Dexterity saving throw to avoid the columns or take {@damage 1d4} Fire damage.

Sulphuric bubbles burst on the water's surface. Characters must succeed on a {@dc 13} Constitution saving throw or they have the {@condition Poisoned} condition until they next roll for {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} or regain any number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

entries.name: Ransacked Harbor

items: {@b Map For Players:} {@adventure Map 1|TheLighthouseKeeper|1|Adventure Map 1}
{@b Labelled Map for GM:} {@adventure Map 1 (GM Version)|TheLighthouseKeeper|1|Adventure Map 1}

entries: The heroes wash up from the east, clambering onto the pier. The harbor is in {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}, rendering characters without {@sense Darkvision} blind. Not a soul is stirring.

The bodies of sailors and dockhands lie strewn across the harbor and the rocks below. If it weren't for the strange condition of their bodies—some burned, some half-eaten, and some, both—you may have thought the site had been pillaged. A sulphurous odor lingers and not a soul is moving. You sense something far more sinister than piracy has stricken Craggy Island...

Below is the suggested progression for exploring the harbor, but the party do not have to follow this progression, provided they don't beeline for the lighthouse without first meeting the dockmaster at L3 (See {@adventure GM Labelled Map|TheLighthouseKeeper|1|Adventure Map 1}). The GM may also challenge the party with an additional encounter against a {@creature Chuul} or three {@creature giant octopus||Giant Octopuses} at their discretion. Upon emerging victorious in this encounter, the heroes uncover treasure in the form of a random Uncommon magic item.

entries.name: L1. The Pier
entries: The pier itself is slick with surface water and seaweed, and the waves are still raging, sending moored boats crashing into it. Save the clothes on their back and any gear carried on their person, the heroes have lost everything in the shipwreck, but among the wreckage of the pier, they see smashed crates and tangled rigging, crabbing cages and bobbing barrels—supplies everywhere! They can secure resources as follows:

items.name: Torches
items.entry: {@dc 12} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check to heave this waterlogged crate from the wreckage. 3 {@item Torch|XPHB|Torches} are still dry enough to use.

items.name: Rope (50 ft.)
items.entry: {@dc 15} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) check to untangle it from some rigging.

items.name: Crowbar
items.entry: {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check to spot this beneath a splintered boat.

entries.name: L2. Signal Tower
entries: The signal tower looms over the harbor, a proud structure boasting a colossal bell to warn ships away from the coast when the lighthouse has failed or become obscured in fog. Now, however, its bell is silent and its walls are blackened with soot.

Inside, the party find the bell's hammer has crashed through the upper floors, the chain that once held it melted to slag. They can fix the bell with their salvaged {@item Rope} or by locating repair tools with a successful {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check. Reattaching the hammer requires a successful {@dc 15} Strength check. If players devise other methods to raise the bell, their ingenuity should be rewarded by lowering the DC of checks required. By ringing the bell, the heroes warn away offshore ships, saving several crews from their fate.

entries.name: L3. The Dockmaster

entries: Over the eerie gusts of wind wailing through chinks in the harbor's fortified walls, you hear another, distinctly human, sound—a cry for help. Through the lashing rain, you make out the cowering form of a man hiding behind a makeshift wall of sandbags. He is trapped beneath a fallen storage crate and badly injured, debilitating burns covering the right side of his body. He identifies himself as the dockmaster, Gavinu.

The party can free Gavinu with a {@dc 14} Strength check. Once released, Gavinu explains that the lighthouse keeper, Nimali, has been experimenting with methods to make the lighthouse glow automatically at nightfall to relieve himself of the burden. He'd been calling on ancient volcanic spirits of the island to assist, despite Gavinu's repeated cautions. Nimali seems to have made a grave miscalculation, however, and has been transfigured into a glowing, fire-breathing abomination, all sanity and reason eclipsed by a depraved hunger for destruction.

Gavinu begs them to end Nimali's reign of terror, pointing them to the lighthouse (L5). If the party heals Gavinu at all, he remembers to warn them of the {@creature Lava Crab|DMSecretWeapon24|Lava Crabs} infesting the harbor (presumably summoned by Nimali) and advises that the creatures are Vulnerable to Cold.

entries.name: L4. Recent Shipwreck
entries: {@adventure Map 2|TheLighthouseKeeper|1|Adventure Map 2}

Here, the bodies of the crew are barely more than skeletons, their flesh picked to the bone. Yet, the wreckage itself appears recent, its precious cargo still strewn across the rocks. The heroes find {@dice 3d6} GP, two {@item Potion of Healing||Potions of Healing}, and one {@item Potion of Vitality}. As they attempt to leave, {@dice 1d10} {@creature Lava Crab|DMSecretWeapon24|Lava Crabs} ambush them, swarming a single target (they all take the same turn in {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}).
Unless the party has been warned by Gavinu, they are {@status Surprised} by the attack. The crabs fight to the death, burning their targets before feasting on their charred flesh.

entries.name: Lighthouse Keeper
entries: {@adventure Map 3|TheLighthouseKeeper|1|Adventure Map 3}

At the top of the lighthouse (L5) is the lantern room where the heroes find {@creature Nimali, Elemental Abomination|DMSecretWeapon24|Nimali}, radiating an unearthly heat. He crouches atop a giant brazier, gazing through the lantern's lens into the darkness beyond, the scattered bones of charred victims surrounding him. When the party enters, he turns to look at them, his eyes like lumps of coal struck through with molten venom, all humanity lost. He immediately attacks, using Noxious Steam to devastate enemies before moving into melee range. When Nimali is {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, {@dice 2d4} {@creature Lava Crab|DMSecretWeapon24|Lava Crabs} are conjured from his elemental body, which attack the heroes at random and take their turn on {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} count 0.
When Nimali is defeated, read the following:

With a blast of heat so intense it feels as if it erupted from the very bowels of hell, Nimali bursts into flame, his body disintegrating into cinders in mere seconds. Then, just as swiftly, the fire dies, leaving a large pile of sparkling black ash in its wake. Beneath the ashes, a glow begins to emanate, growing ever brighter.

entries.name: Conclusion
entries: Despite the carnage Nimali inadvertently wreaked upon Craggy Island, he did in fact succeed in his ambition—at the cost of his life. From the ashes, the heroes recover a glowing orb, bright enough to power the lighthouse. It responds to the time of day, beaming brightly from dusk 'til dawn and returning to a gentle glow at sunrise.

The party may claim this as their reward, but it has no additional magical properties and a limited market. A more profitable or charitable alternative is to place it in the lighthouse lantern. If they do so, Gavinu erects a donations tin in the heroes' honor with a plaque detailing their bravery. He encourages every crew using Craggy Island harbor to make a donation. The party can choose to benefit directly or select a local cause as the beneficiary. The former generates an income of {@dice 2d20} GP per month, but they must return to the port to collect it, while the latter casts them as legends all along this naval passage, and any crew who has benefitted from their support will aid them however they can in the future.

data.name: The Library of Living Dreams
entries: The Library of Living Dreams is an adventure for four level 7 heroes that requires the party to enter a magical library that exists only on the Plane of Dreams, rescue an esteemed scholar from his worst nightmares made manifest, and bring him safely back to the Material Plane.

entries.name: Set Up
entries: The party are visiting the Everdusk Academy to expand their arcane knowledge when a professor inadvertently gets stuck in the perilous Library of Living Dreams, which exists in the Dreamscape. Here, nightmares are made manifest and the longer the manifestations persist, the more frightening they become. The party are called upon to rescue the professor from the Dreamscape, which may require facing off against their own nightmares too!
Before beginning the adventure, draw from your own knowledge of the heroes to flavour a special {@creature Manifested Nightmare|DMSecretWeapon24} stat block for each of them.

entries.name: The Rescue Mission
entries: The ancient Everdusk Academy is a sprawling, fortified building with towering turrets and winding staircases, where the party has been granted access to all but its most restricted libraries. One library, however, perilously borders the Plane of Dreams; everyone at the academy knows never to fall asleep there. The veil that separates the academy's Nocturn Library from the terrifying Library of Living Dreams is but a fine gossamer, all too easy to slip through.

While the party are visiting the academy, they are called upon by Headmaster Artemis to rescue an unfortunate professor who was conducting vital research in the Nocturn Library when he inadvertently fell into a slumber and straight through the veil. The Headmaster is not unkind, but she is brusque, to the point, and very matter-of-fact in her interactions. She offers the party 150 GP to rescue Professor Thaddeus from the Dreamscape and bring him back to the Material Plane.

She explains that it's not only the terrain of the Dreamscape and its native horrors that pose a risk, but also the plane's power to wield a hero's worst nightmares against them. Worse yet, nightmares in the Dreamscape compound into exponentially more powerful manifestations over time; it is imperative that the party be as quick as possible on their mission!

entries.name: Slipping into Perilous Slumber
entries: {@adventure Map 1|TheLibraryOfLivingDreams|1|Adventure Map 1}

When they have accepted their mission, Headmaster Artemis leads the party to the academy's highest tower and into a candlelit library. The moment the heroes enter, exhaustion begins to weigh them down, like a heavy blanket draped around their shoulders.

At the far end of the library is a towering angel statue, beneath which, Artemis explains, is a portal where the veil between planes is thinnest. Though the party can fall asleep and slip into the Library of Living Dreams from anywhere in the Nocturn Library, once they are in the Dreamscape and wish to return to the Material Plane, they must first reach this portal.

Artemis provides them with a sleeping draught each and a waking potion each, plus one for Professor Thaddeus. The sleeping draught will send them instantly into a deep slumber and transport them to the Library of Living Dreams. When they have located Professor Thaddeus, they must get to the portal and consume the waking potion, at which point they will awaken back in the Nocturn Library.
She reminds them about the dangers their own dreams may pose if they are made manifest and urges them to resist any encroaching nightmares as the sleeping draught takes effect.

Headmaster Artemis slips you each a small vial of silvery liquid with a suspension of shimmering sand—the sleeping draught. Then, she slips you the waking potion in a second vial, along with one extra for Professor Thaddeus. Its contents are rich dark brown, warm to the touch, and, even when corked, emanate a tantalizing aroma.

When the heroes take the sleeping draught, they each must roll a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw to resist their own dreams taking form. On a failure, their nightmares are made manifest and will later present an additional encounter.

entries.name: GM Note
entries: If a player refuses to take the sleeping draught, regardless of how much they explore the Nocturn Library, they will find no trace of Professor Thaddeus, other than his dishevelled research notes written in a shorthand only the professor knows.

entries.name: Crossing the Dreamscape
entries: {@adventure Map 2|TheLibraryOfLivingDreams|1|Adventure Map 2}

The towering shelves of starlit tomes hem you in, the ceiling a tapestry of celestial bodies twinkling down at you. Though you haven't felt the sleeping draught taking effect, the library begins to shift in ways that don't make sense. The shelves begin to slide past you as if each row is on a conveyor belt emerging from the walls. As you turn to try to discern how the shelves are materializing like this, you suddenly notice the door has disappeared, swallowed by an infinite aisle of books. Ah, you are the one moving, of course, not the shelves—but even as you decide this, the shelves grind to a halt and their movement changes again, rising from the ground this time, the tops of the shelves stretching higher and higher into the open sky... but wasn't there a ceiling there before? Ah, you realize, the sleeping draught has done its work. You are no longer in the Nocturn Library, but in its planar counterpart—the Library of Living Dreams.

Each hero awakens simultaneously at the southern door and may begin exploring the library. The library is divided up into roughly 5 sections: the room at the south (where the party awakens), the balconies on either side of the library, the open-plan southern half of the library, the northern half of the library with the sprawling bookshelves, and the Northern Circle.
Each section of the library takes 30 minutes for the heroes to explore, and for every hour that passes, the professor's nightmare gains power.

Roll on the Dreamscape Encounters table each time the party explore a new section of the library, with the exception of the northern circle. In the case of the Literature Riddles, a famous riddle from a book inside the library comes to life. It takes the form of a shade, and poses its question to the party. If they answer correctly, each hero gains a point of {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB}. Otherwise, they each take {@damage 3d10} Psychic damage.

entries.caption: Dreamscape Encounters
rows: {@dice 2d6} {@creature Book Worm|DMSecretWeapon24|Book Worms} attack the party. They can be defeated in combat, or placated by feeding them with stories they've never heard before. Placated Book Worms can act as a hero's familiar, as with the {@spell Find Familiar} spell.

The library appears to be a shimmering meadow where the blossoms, clouds, and treetops have a wispy texture, reminiscent of candyfloss. When touched, the hero immediately remembers a pleasant dream that melted into the ether upon waking. They receive {@dice 1d4} {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}, and whatever they touch disintegrates into sand and trickles to the ground as if through an hourglass. The heroes can consume candyfloss up to 12 candyfloss dreams (although {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} do not stack). Each time a hero does so, an hour passes in the Dreamscape. This should be hinted at by things like the sound of a ticking clock, the toll of a clock tower, a shift in the lighting, etc.

Gravity shifts depending on one's direction of travel. Each hero must succeed on a {@dc 16} Dexterity saving throw or be slammed into the ground as gravity changes, taking {@damage 4d6} Bludgeoning damage.

Inky puddles on the ground, formed from distilled dreams, coalesce into friendly spectral creatures. The creatures remind the heroes that dream forms are resistant to physical damage, that {@creature Book Worm|DMSecretWeapon24|Book Worms} can be tamed by telling them a story they do not know, and warn them that in some sections of the library, time and gravity behave differently. This grants the heroes {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on their Dexterity saving throws if they encounter Shifting Gravity.
If this player failed their Constitution saving throw earlier, their {@creature Manifested Nightmare|DMSecretWeapon24} attacks them. Otherwise, nothing happens.
If this player failed their Constitution saving throw earlier, their {@creature Manifested Nightmare|DMSecretWeapon24} attacks them. Otherwise, nothing happens.
If this player failed their Constitution saving throw earlier, their {@creature Manifested Nightmare|DMSecretWeapon24} attacks them. Otherwise, nothing happens.
If this player failed their Constitution saving throw earlier, their {@creature Manifested Nightmare|DMSecretWeapon24} attacks them. Otherwise, nothing happens.
This thing all things devours; / Birds, beasts, trees, flowers; / Gnaws iron, bites steel; / Grinds hard stones to meal; / Slays king, ruins town, / And beats mountain down. / {@b Answer:} Time

First think of the person who lives in disguise, / Who deals in secrets and tells naught but lies, / Next tell me what's always the last thing to mend, / The middle of middle and end of the end? / And finally give me the sound often heard, / During the search for a hard-to-find word. / Now string them together, and answer me this, / Which creature would you be unwilling to kiss? / {@b Answer:} Spider

entries.name: A Nightmare Compounded
entries: Either when the party enter the northern circle after exploring at least three other sections of the library, or after they've finished exploring all other sections, the angel statue towering above the portal between planes suddenly transforms into a {@creature Manifested Nightmare (Compounded)|DMSecretWeapon24} and attacks Professor Thaddeus (use the {@creature Mage} stat block).

The {@creature Manifested Nightmare (Compounded)|DMSecretWeapon24} appears with {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to 10 × the number of hours the party have spent in the Dreamscape. Professor Thaddeus is {@condition Incapacitated} and cannot move while the {@creature Manifested Nightmare (Compounded)|DMSecretWeapon24} exists.

Suddenly, a screech echoes out through the aisles and you turn to see one of the three stone angels transform into a terrifying oversized owl. The ends of its feathers have been sharpened into quills, spattering red ink across the library as it swoops down to attack a {@status Bloodied|XPHB|bloodied} and trembling Professor Thaddeus, who has stumbled from his hiding place, wand outstretched. "Not again," he screams, anguished. "I am not scared of you. I'm not, I'm not!" But the tremor in his voice and the terror in his eyes tell another story...

At this point, any player who failed their Constitution saving throw in the "{@adventure Slipping into Perilous Slumber|TheLibraryOfLivingDreams|0|Slipping into Perilous Slumber}" section, and whose {@creature Manifested Nightmare|DMSecretWeapon24} has not already been defeated, is attacked by their {@creature Manifested Nightmare|DMSecretWeapon24} also. These nightmares focus on the character from whom they originated, but if that character is killed or neutralized, it will attack other party members at random.
The nightmares fight to the death.

entries.name: Returning to the Material Plane
entries: When the heroes have either defeated all the Manifested Nightmares and/or managed to make it to the portal with the professor in tow, they may consume their waking potion. They instantly awaken in the Nocturn Library on the Material Plane, just as Headmaster Artemis had promised.

Professor Thaddeus is rattled, but very grateful to the party. As a gesture of his own gratitude, he quickly jots down his shorthand cipher, which grants a +1 bonus to each character's {@skill History}, {@skill Nature}, and {@skill Religion} checks.

Headmaster Artemis is so relieved to have Professor Thaddeus safely returned that she not only gives the party the promised 150 GP but also grants the heroes access to the academy's restricted archives. Here, any spellcasters in the party can discover a new Wizard spell of a level they can cast to add to their spell lists. Wizards instead find lost knowledge to enhance their magic, learning an additional spell of a level they can cast from the Wizard spell list and increasing the number of spells they can prepare each day by 1.

data.name: Carnival of Charms
entries: Carnival of Charms is an adventure for four level 4 heroes in which the party competes in carnival games to win tickets they can cash in for prizes. Many of the prizes are precious artifacts gambled away by previous patrons, and the party have been hired to reclaim an ancient amulet ({@item Amulet of Health}) for the esteemed Lady Marjorie.

entries.name: Set Up
entries: The Carnival of Charms travels from town to town, offering challenges, spectacle, and intrigue—at a hefty price. In its wake, it leaves townsfolk flustered, confused, and disproportionately purse-lightened.

The handsome Carnival Master, Enriquio, is silver-tongued and charming in the truest sense of the word. Armed with a flaming whip, he tricks carnival-goers into gambling away their most valuable artifacts, which he then displays as prizes to be won.

entries.name: The Games Begin
entries: {@adventure Map 1|CarnivalOfCharms|1|Adventure Map 1}

On arrival at the carnival, the party are greeted by a motley-clad carnie who takes payment of 5 GP in return for 20 tickets. These can be used to compete in various challenges in a bid to win more tickets. The carnie provides a map highlighting the various challenges, which each cost 5 tickets to enter but offer the opportunity to multiply their tickets.

He also encourages them to visit the prize tent to survey potential prizes, to visit the oracle for tea-leaf reading, and to be sure to enter the Final Showdown to increase their ticket winnings a hundredfold.

entries.name: 1. Whack-a-Mole
entries: Armed with a foam bat, contestants win points by whacking the heads of surfacing moles before they scurry back into their warren.
{@b Ability check:} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) + Strength ({@skill Athletics})

With a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling}) check, a hero realizes the poor moles are trapped and desperately trying to escape. If the heroes free the moles, they become a helpful distraction in the Final Showdown.

entries.name: 2. Sing-Off
entries: The hero has the chance to outshine the carnival's resident bard, Pip Whistledown, in a performance of their choice, the outcome of which is judged based on the crowd's cheers. For Pip, use the {@creature Cultist Fanatic} stat block, replacing {@spell Hold Person} with {@spell Mass Suggestion}. Pip gives an enchanting performance—literally—casting {@spell Mass Suggestion} to target the twelve patrons in the front row to cheer raucously at the conclusion of their performance (save {@dc 11}). The twelve patrons consist of {@creature Commoner||Commoners} plus the hero's allies. Any non-player characters automatically fail the saving throw to resist {@spell Mass Suggestion}.
The hero makes a Charisma ({@skill Performance}) check contested by Pip's Charisma ({@skill Performance}) + additional cheers from the front row (Pip has a +2 to their {@skill Performance} checks).

entries.name: 3. Acrobat Beam
entries: Pitted against a {@creature Carnie Acrobat|DMSecretWeapon24} and balancing on a horizontal ladder, the contestant must attempt to knock the acrobat from the ladder before falling themselves, using only a foam {@item Quarterstaff|XPHB}, which deals half the damage of a normal {@item Quarterstaff|XPHB}.

Each time either combatant takes damage, they must succeed on a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw to avoid falling 10 feet to solid ground below. Damage sustained is real and the potential winnings reflect the risks involved. If a combatant falls to half their {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, they fall from the ladder. A successful {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check identifies the {@creature Carnie Acrobat|DMSecretWeapon24}'s {@item Quarterstaff|XPHB} as a {@item Lesser Quarterstaff of the Acrobat|DMSecretWeapon24}.

entries.name: 4. Mirror Maze
entries: The contestant must navigate a labyrinth of mirrors that are enchanted to display increasingly sinister reflections. Tickets are awarded according to speed.
Ability check: Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) + Intelligence ({@skill Investigation})

If a hero's result is lower than 27, they stumble into the cursed heart of the labyrinth, where the mirrors are enchanted to summon ghastly reflections from the Mirror Plane. {@dice 1d4} {@creature Pseudo-Self|DMSecretWeapon24|Pseudo-Selves} leap from the mirrors and attack.

entries.name: 5. The Oracle
entries: The fortune-teller, Giselda, is a gifted {@creature Druid}, who sells tea-leaf readings ({@spell Augury}) for 2 tickets. She can perform other Divination spells ({@spell Divination} or {@spell Scrying}) if her palm is crossed with coin (1 SP). If the party win Giselda's respect ({@dc 15} Charisma check), she warns them that some challenges are rigged, most are dangerous, and no one has ever won the Final Showdown. With a result of 18 or higher on the Charisma check, she hints that Enriquio derives his power from a sinister source but will say no more.

entries.name: 6. Enriquio's Trailer
entries: Enriquio's trailer is inconspicuous, but the carnies can direct the party there if they ask the right questions. Alternatively, they can find it through surveillance of the trailers or Enriquio.

When vacant, the door is locked. This can be picked discreetly using {@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB} ({@dc 15} {@skill Sleight of Hand}) but the lock is trapped with a Venom Needle, which deals {@damage 2d8} Poison damage to the lockpicker each time they attempt to pick the lock. Alternatively, the door can be battered down (AC 15; 18 HP), but this will attract the attention of {@dice 1d4} passing carnies ({@creature Guard||Guards}), who will attempt to stop the heroes.

Inside, the party find a ritualistic shrine composed of sigils, candles, and an altar. A {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check reveals this to be related to a Warlock's commune with a Fiend of the Lower Planes. A further {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check uncovers a journal, listing various artifacts the carnival has secured and noting that, so far, none are adequate to unlock Enriquio's patron from its infernal prison—the carnival's clandestine goal. Discovering these details puts the heroes on guard against Enriquio's magic, granting {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Saving Throws against being {@condition Charmed}.

entries.name: 7. Pop Corn Stalls
entries: An array of stalls offer delicious treats at surprisingly reasonable prices (cotton candy 1 CP; popcorn, 2 CP; fried cheese wedge, 5 CP). However, the food is cursed, giving anyone who consumes it {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on their next Wisdom saving throw. This is discernible with a {@spell Detect Poison and Disease} spell, {@spell Identify} spell, or a {@dc 18} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check.

entries.name: 8. The Prize Tent
entries: Here, a circular display unit is set behind a stall, staffed by a {@creature Guard Captain|XMM} and three {@creature Guard||Guards}. Any attempt to steal an item triggers an immediate attack. The following prizes are on display:

entries.caption: Prize Table
rows: {@item Amulet of Proof against Detection and Location}

entries: Clearly, the party have little hope of attaining enough tickets to win Marjorie's amulet without entering the Final Showdown. A {@dc 17} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check reveals that many of the other prizes have personalized inscriptions and the party may deduce that these were once cherished possessions.

entries.name: The Final Showdown
entries: {@adventure Map 2|CarnivalOfCharms|1|Adventure Map 2}

Shrouded in mystery, all the party know is that the Final Showdown is the only opportunity to multiply their tickets a hundredfold. Players must have a minimum of 60 tickets between them to enter. However, it also requires each contestant to gamble their most prized possession, to be claimed by the carnival if they lose. If they have enough tickets, each player can decide independently if they wish to compete given the terms, but the party stand a better chance as a team.

As the concierge pulls back the tent's velvet entrance curtain with a dramatic flair, the final challenge unfolds before you: lion-taming. The prize stall now stands resplendent at the center of the tent, its treasures gleaming under twinkling light. Your attention, however, is drawn to three {@creature Lion||Lions} skulking around it, teeth bared and growling at the crowd, while three flaming hoops send sinister shadows dancing across the arena floor. Crowds are packed into tiered benches surrounding the arena.

"Welcome to the Final Showdown!" a voice bellows over the crowd—Enriquio in a bedazzling red rhinestone cape and clutching a flaming whip. "Here your contestants must simply walk to the center of the arena and select their prize. Easy! Watch!"

Enriquio strolls into the midst of the lions, cracks his whip, and sends them bounding through the flaming rings, while he approaches the stall unscathed. He grasps a solid gold medallion, holding it up victoriously to the enraptured crowd.

Throughout Enriquio's performance, he uses his Flaming Whip action on the three {@creature Lion||Lions}, discernible with a successful {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check. A result of 15 or higher reveals his magic is that of a warlock bound to a primal demonic entity.
Enriquio withdraws to the sidelines, making way for the heroes to begin.

All the heroes must do is walk between the lions and flaming rings to claim the medallion, which they can offer at the prize booth to multiply their tickets hundredfold. Participating heroes roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} to determine turn order.

If a hero passes within 10 feet of a flaming ring, Enriquio uses his Flame Thrower reaction to send a flame leaping towards them. If any hero gets within 60 feet of the medallion, Enriquio uses his Flaming Whip action to command a {@creature Lion} nearest to them to attack, which enters {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} immediately at the end of the current turn. A {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check after either of these actions reveals his tricks.

If the party attack Enriquio, or get within 20 feet of the prize tent, he unleashes the full force of his demonic power on them with direct attacks and attempts to charm them into turning on one another. At this point, the {@creature Lion||Lions} act on their own volition each round, targeting the hero nearest to them, regardless of distance from the prize stall. If they are not already in {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, they enter on {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} count 0.

If the heroes previously freed the moles, they will burrow through the arena floor and distract the lions should they attack, with 1 mole surfacing on {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} count 0 each round. Roll a die to randomly determine which lion it surfaces next to—that lion uses its next action to lunge towards the mole rather than attack a party member.

entries.name: Conclusion
entries: If the party defeat Enriquio, the {@creature Lion||Lions} immediately flee the carnival's clutches. The carnies begrudgingly relinquish Marjorie's amulet to the party, in exchange for 6,000 tickets. They also agree to either grant the party one additional prize of their choosing in return for their discretion, or to return the other prizes to their original owners.

If the party return Marjorie's amulet to her, she thanks them for their service and pays them 2,000 GP, as well as promising her ongoing favor in the town. If the party opt for the carnies to return their ill-gotten gains to their original owners, their reputation as heroes spreads, granting them {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma checks when entering a nearby town.

data.name: Omenspire
entries: Omenspire is an adventure for 4 level 6 heroes that requires the party to summit a treacherous peak, repair vandalized observatory equipment, and redirect a plane-warping meteor on a collision course with the earth.

entries.name: Set Up
entries: The party have voyaged to the icy base of Starshadow Peak. Their destination: Omenspire Observatory. When they arrive, they discover the astrologists in a tizzy over the untimely and, frankly, very suspicious, death of their lead astrologist, Seer Millinus III. Not only was the Seer about to locate the impact zone of a fiery meteor that's been blazing through the sky for the last twelve days, but equipment vital to deflecting the meteor has somehow become broken. The party must investigate the death and the broken equipment, which leads them to discover an infestation of body-snatching, hive-minded planar invaders. These invaders from a distant plane of existence have been using the equipment to guide the blazing meteor—the dagger to puncture a hole between realms—to the ground, where the invading species will infest the bodies of the native population and claim the Material Plane as their own.

entries.name: Intro
entries: {@adventure Map 1|Omenspire|1|Adventure Map 1}

Weary and teeth-chatteringly chilled, you have at last reached the base of Starshadow Peak, where the Omenspire Observatory dominates the crest of the stepped and craggy mountain. Greeting you is an unexpected flurry of anxious activity concentrated around the foot of the first switchback staircase. Through the crowd of astrologers and astronomers you can just make out a body, limbs splayed at crooked angles and head haloed by a scarlet wreath of blood, stark against the crisp white snow.
If the party make enquiries, the NPCs in the crowd reveal the following:

items: The body belongs to Seer Millinus III, their senior astrologist, who fell to his death sometime in the night.

He had been studying the path of the blazing meteor and believed it was on a course for impact. He was working on a complex series of arcane sigils to project into the night sky and divert the meteor away.
The sigil beam has suddenly become broken.

Millinus was clutching his research notes as he fell and they are now scattered across the icy tundra, many seemingly blown away on the wind. (The party observes a scattering of parchment around Millinus's body.)
Access to the Observatory is now being strictly regulated by the Omen-Keeper, who is head of security.

entries.name: The Omen-Keeper
entries: When the party identify themselves to the Omen-Keeper, he requests assistance in fixing the broken equipment so they can forecast and alter the meteor's trajectory. The consequences of failure are cataclysmic. With a {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check, the party determines he is omitting something and when pressed, he admits he suspects some of the astrologists have been hampering efforts to deflect the meteor, though he can't fathom why.

He's concerned Millinus's death and the broken sigil beam may be more than coincidence. Thus, he welcomes external help as he doesn't know who to trust internally. He will remain at base to monitor and control access to the Observatory.

entries.name: Prepare and Investigate
entries: There are various ways the party can progress. The Omen-Keeper may offer some direction should the party require it:

items: With a successful {@dc 15} group Dexterity check, they quickly gather Seer Millinus's scattered notes. A further {@dc 14} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check reveals a correlation in the missing notes: the pages preceding them suggest that Millinus was about to reveal key information regarding the meteor's trajectory, flight path anomalies, and the consequences of its impact.
With a relevant {@dc 15} Charisma check, a character can persuade an NPC to equip them with {@item Boots of the Winterlands} for the task at hand. Each character can attempt this only once.

If the party investigate Seer Millinus's body, a successful {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check reveals defensive wounds on his arms. A result of 15–17 additionally reveals a transparent slime on his cloak and hands, and a result of 18 or higher additionally uncovers a broken candlestick beneath his body, the jagged end coated with slime and blood.

entries.name: Summiting the Peak
entries: {@adventure Map 2|Omenspire|1|Adventure Map 2}

The trek to the summit is treacherous as the party are exposed to {@hazard Extreme Cold|XDMG} while clambering up ladders and across rope bridges, balancing on narrow shelves, and trudging up stairwells carved into the mountainside.
Halfway up the mountainside, they literally stumble upon a hive of {@dice 1d10} {@creature Disembodied Snatcher|DMSecretWeapon24|Disembodied Snatchers}, who attack immediately.

The ground here is also randomly dotted with {@dice 1d6} 10-foot squares of {@hazard Slippery Ice|XDMG}. A creature who enters an area of {@hazard Slippery Ice|XDMG}, or starts its turn there, must succeed on a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw or fall {@condition Prone}.

entries.name: Ground Floor
entries: {@adventure Map 3|Omenspire|1|Adventure Map 3}
When they reach the summit, the party enter the observatory on the ground floor, where Millinus's quarters are housed to the east.

A sombre hush permeates the ground floor of the observatory, which has clearly been vacated suddenly and in haste. Parchments are strewn across the dashboards and quills left dripping ink on star maps. Suddenly, a door to the east creaks open and a figure shuffles out, freezing when she notices you...

The NPC is Isolde, Millinus's assistant, who has been claimed by a {@creature Snatcher (Lesser)|DMSecretWeapon24} and is responsible for killing Millinus. She has been rummaging in Millinus's desk to try to ascertain if anyone else knew the secret of Omenspire's infestation. Isolde presents as dazed, which she attributes to shock and grief. However, a {@dc 14} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check reveals this is actually due to a stab wound in her side. It oozes a sticky slime mixed with blood. If the party recovered the broken candlestick from Millinus's body previously, they recognize this is the same substance that coated it. If they did not recover it, a further {@dc 17} Wisdom ({@skill Medicine}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check reveals smaller injuries on Isolde's arm and neck, consistent with a recent struggle. Unless the party fight and defeat her, Isolde will obstruct all their attempts to progress in an increasingly suspicious and hostile fashion.

If the party defeat Isolde, the snatcher occupying her dies and she is granted a brief reprieve before succumbing to her injuries. She reveals that Omenspire has become infested with snatchers, aberrations from a distant plane who are trying to guide a meteor to crash in the valley below and puncture a hole between planes of existence, through which to invade.

Millinus was attempting to deflect the meteor and Isolde was forced to intervene by the snatcher controlling her. She broke the equipment and attacked Millinus directly. Before she is able to offer further insight, she takes her dying breath.

If the party investigate her body, they find Millinus's missing notes, detailing the trajectory of the meteor, and a diagram depicting a complex pattern of arcane sigils that must be mapped onto the night sky.

entries.name: Upper Floor
entries: {@adventure Map 4|Omenspire|1|Adventure Map 4}

The party make their way to the observatory dome, where a huge arcane telescope stretches towards the heavens. Though the telescope rotates freely, the sigil beam attached to its tip is jammed in place. A character can investigate by climbing the telescope, requiring a successful {@dc 12} Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) or Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check. Here, they find half a candlestick jammed into the gears, preventing the sigil beam from moving (no check required).

If a hero removes the candlestick, the sigil beam rotates as it should and can now be used to trace constellations in the night sky, creating star-powered sigils that will alter the meteor's path. The party must attempt to use the sigil beam to trace the pattern outlined in Millinus's notes. Their degree of success depends on rolling 3 successful {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) checks before 3 failures, as outlined in the Success Table. These checks do not need to be completed by the same character, but as a party they must achieve 3 successes before suffering 3 failures.

entries.caption: Success Table
rows: {@b Failure.} The party fail to change the meteor's path and it crashes into the valley below as planned.
{@b Partial Success.} The meteor is deflected to land in a nearby ocean, devastating the local environment, but not puncturing a hole between realms.
{@b Success.} The meteor is deflected into a gravitational orbit that pulls it back into space. The snatchers' plan is significantly delayed.
{@b Total Wipeout.} The meteor is deflected into a meteor belt that destroys it.

entries: As the party begin attempting to trace these sigils into the sky, the Omen-Keeper, now infested by a {@creature Snatcher (Greater)|DMSecretWeapon24}, storms in and immediately attacks. This is the snatchers' final opportunity to guide the meteor to shatter the boundaries between planes of existence.

The Omen-Keeper is joined by two {@creature Snatcher (Lesser)|DMSecretWeapon24|Snatchers (Lesser)} on {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} count 0 each round (maximum of 3 on the battlefield at a time). During combat, a character attempting to use the sigil beam must use their action to roll the required {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check and must maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB} on their task for the entire round of combat. Broken {@status Concentration|XPHB} is not treated as a failure but negates the possibility of success in this round.

entries.name: Conclusion
entries: The party can snatch victory from the invaders either by defeating them in combat or destroying the meteor in a Total Wipeout (see the Success Table). A Total Wipeout destroys the meteor and, therefore, the entire infestation of snatchers—tethered to this realm by its magic. Any infested NPC regains control of their bodies.

If the party deflect the meteor back into space with a Success (see Success Table), Omenspire is granted a temporary reprieve—the snatchers will attempt to flee, but if they succeed, they will regroup and form a new strategy to guide the meteor to earth.
If the party secure a Partial Success (see Success Table), the snatchers will flee and rendezvous with the meteor, drawing from its power to facilitate more devious plans in the future.

Finally, if the party fail to redirect the meteor (see Failure on the Success Table), it crashes into the valley below, shaking Starshadow Peak right to its summit. The party's very bones shudder with the impact as a burst of aberrative energy surges over the land. Endless aberrations clamber through a rift that has been torn between planes of existence.

The heroes' only hope of survival is to escape Omenspire Observatory as it will soon be overrun. The party will be accosted by {@dice 1d6} {@creature Snatcher (Lesser)|DMSecretWeapon24|Snatchers (Lesser)} before they clear the danger zone. If they fail to take action after they escape, the invasion spreads with exponential speed. However, if the party wishes to take action against the invaders, it provides a perfect follow-up adventure in which they can gather allies, prepare supplies, and mount a counterattack on Omenspire's invaders to seal the rift.

data.name: Heather Heights Manor Heist
entries: Heather Heights Manor Heist is an adventure for four level-3 heroes requiring stealth and wit to plan and execute a heist on a wealthy lord's manor. The target: a valuable gem rumored to be secured in the basement vault.

entries.name: Setup
entries: The affluent city of Heather Heights is home to the land's wealthiest gentry, where lords and ladies vie for social status, primarily by occupying the most extravagant houses. Lord Fennelby recently acquired such a house from the unfortunate Lord Witherington, purchasing and consolidating his many gambling debts, and forcing him to sell his home as payment.

Rumor has it Fennelby set his sights on the Witherington house for its secure basement vault, where he hides a precious gem. Following a recent spate of disappearances, a more nefarious rumor circulates that the basement hides the bodies of those missing persons.

Vengeful and desperate, Witherington hires the party on a deal—he has a buyer for the gem and will supply the party with information to break into the vault if they allow him to sell the gem and split the profits.

He provides a layout of the ground floor and basement (show the players {@adventure Maps 3 and 4|HeatherHeightsManorHeist|1|Adventure Map 1}). He also shares knowledge of the three vault entrances he is aware of:

items: Behind the fireplace in the drawing room (G3). He instructs the party to twist the left antler of the mounted stag's head to open the door. {@b GM Note:} The opening mechanism has since changed, unbeknownst to Witherington. See {@adventure G3|HeatherHeightsManorHeist|0|Ground Floor} below for details.

A larder beneath the kitchen (G4), where a door disguised as shelving only opens when the number of spice jars on each side is equally balanced. {@b GM Note:} The opening mechanism has since changed, unbeknownst to Witherington. See {@adventure B3|HeatherHeightsManorHeist|0|Basement} below for details.
A wardrobe in the butler's quarters (G8) has a false back, requiring an ordinary key to open it, which Witherington was forcibly dispossessed of.

entries: Witherington has no information about any additional security features Fennelby has implemented, but he does know that, tonight, Fennelby is out of town, accompanied by half his guards.

entries.name: The Heist
entries: {@adventure Map 1|HeatherHeightsManorHeist|1|Adventure Map 1}

entries.name: GM Note
entries: As the party progresses through the manor, you can refer to the specific obstacles and key information that can be found in each room using the guide in the {@adventure Ground Floor|HeatherHeightsManorHeist|0|Ground Floor} section. The labelled map given to the party by Witherington labels each room, which you can also refer to as the party explore the manor.

entries.name: House Exterior
entries: The grounds are enclosed by a 50-foot wall, with a single gate to the front, manned by two {@creature Guard||Guards} around the clock and locked each evening at sunset. Sneaking past the guards requires a group {@dc 12} Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check, increasing to {@dc 18} if the party attempt to pick the lock without distracting them. The lock can be picked with a {@dc 12} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) check using {@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB}.

A 100-foot path leads from the gate to the front door, forking west to a courtyard entrance and a disused chapel. The lawns surrounding the path are waterlogged, making it {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}, perceptible with a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check. A searchlight sweeps the grounds every minute, immediately alerting the guards to an intruder if caught in its beam.
Sixteen house guards (using the {@creature Guard} stat block) defend the manor house—two stationed at the front gate, six patrolling the grounds, and the remainder resting.

entries.name: House Entrances
entries: There are four potential ways of entering the manor; each room is explained in further detail in the {@adventure Ground Floor|HeatherHeightsManorHeist|0|Ground Floor} section.

items: The front door, leading to the entrance hall (G1), is flanked by two Fire-Casting Statue traps. Each creature that moves within 10 feet of this door must succeed on a {@dc 14} Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 3d6} Fire damage. The statues spit flame at each creature once per minute while within 10 feet of the door.
An entrance to the back foyer (G7) via the courtyard. A forgetful guard has left it unlocked.
An entrance to the greenhouse (G5) via the courtyard. It is never locked, but the plants inside prove to be vicious (see {@creature Savage Snapper|DMSecretWeapon24|Savage Snappers} stat block).

A door (AC 13; 4 HP) to the kitchen (G4) via the courtyard. The door is locked but can be picked with a {@dc 15} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) check using {@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB}, or broken, attracting the attention of a patrolling {@creature Guard}.

items.name: G1
items.entry: A grand entrance hall, draped with tapestries, leading to G2 or G6. There is nothing of note here.

items.name: G2
items.entry: The dining room, adorned with valuable, oversized oil paintings and cabinets displaying fine china and sparkling silverware worth 200 SP. It leads to G3 or G1.

items.name: G3
items.entry: A large drawing room, lined with bookshelves, leading to G2 or, through the hidden entrance, to B2. A majestic stag's head is mounted above an imposing fireplace and an elegant {@item Rapier|XPHB} is displayed atop the mantelpiece. The fireplace hides a door to the basement, as Witherington said, but Fennelby has changed the opening mechanism. Twisting the stag's antler will be ineffective, but a {@dc 17} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check reveals the gleam of metal within the stag's mouth—a keyhole. A search for a matching key reveals the sword beneath it fits perfectly. When inserted and turned, the fireplace slides back, revealing a tunnel sloping underground.

items.name: G4
items.entry: The kitchen, leading through the pantry to the kitchen stores ({@adventure B3|HeatherHeightsManorHeist|0|Basement}). There is nothing of value here, but it is connected to a pantry where the party can replenish two portions of {@item Rations|XPHB} each.

items.name: G5
items.entry: The greenhouse, where {@dice 1d4} {@creature Savage Snapper|DMSecretWeapon24|Savage Snappers} immediately attack if the party enters. If the party defeat the Snappers, a {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Nature}) or Wisdom ({@skill Medicine}) check reveals the vine sap contains healing properties, which they can use to mix two {@item Potion of Healing||Potions of Healing}.

items.name: G6
items.entry: An intimate sitting room leading to G7 and G8, as well as to a small whiskey store, where a successful {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check reveals a rare bottle of whiskey (worth 1,000 GP).

items.name: G7
items.entry: The back foyer, leading to G8 and G6. There is nothing of note here.

items.name: G8
items.entry: The butler's quarters, currently vacant, leads to G7 or, via a secret door inside the wardrobe, to B1. A key to the door can be found in a bedside table with a successful {@dc 16} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check, but Fennelby has installed a Poisoned Darts trap inside the wardrobe.

items.name: G9
items.entry: The servants' quarters, accessible only via the courtyard. Inside are eight sleeping {@creature Guard||Guards}, who are awoken by the sound of the door unless opened with a {@dc 18} Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check. If awoken, they attack. If any {@creature Guard||Guards} escape, they call for assistance from the six patrolling {@creature Guard||Guards}.

items.name: G10
items.entry: Outhouses, stables, and outer stores. There is nothing of value here and if the party spend too long exploring, a patrolling {@creature Guard} discovers them on his way to the outhouse and alerts the eight sleeping {@creature Guard||Guards}.

items.name: G11
items.entry: A disused chapel from a long-forgotten religious era. A {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check unearths a copper chalice with silver filigree worth 250 GP from debris beneath the altar.

items.name: G12
items.entry: A mausoleum containing an empty sarcophagus (AC 17; 27 HP). When broken open, it reveals stairs leading to the crypt below.

entries.name: Basement
entries: {@adventure Map 2|HeatherHeightsManorHeist|1|Adventure Map 2}

items.name: B1
items.entry: Entrance via wardrobe in G8, or via any of the basement passageways. The coffins here house {@creature Crystal-Eyed Golem|DMSecretWeapon24|Crystal-Eyed Golems} which serve as the final encounter; see {@adventure Final Combat|HeatherHeightsManorHeist|0|Final Combat} for more information.

items.name: B2
items.entry: Entrance via fireplace in G3.

items.name: B3
entries: Entrance via the pantry off G4. As Witherington advised, the door to the vault is disguised as floor-to-ceiling shelves containing a range of spices. Again, Fennelby has updated the security mechanism here, so Lord Witherington's instructions are ineffective. Investigating the shelves reveals that the labels of the spice jars are written in lower case, except for a single, seemingly random, letter in their names, which is capitalized. The capital letters form an anagram, which, when solved, reads OPEN SESAME.
The spices are currently in alphabetical order, labelled as follows:
The door will open when the jars are ordered in the following sequence:
When arranged as above, the password glows orange and the door swings inward. If the players struggle with the puzzle, the GM may offer clues.

items.name: B4
items.entry: Entrance via the shaft of the well above, 150 feet deep and slick with slime, making it impossible to climb without {@item Rope|XPHB}.

items.name: B5
items.entry: Entrance via the mausoleum and through the crypt. A {@spell Glyph of Warding} is inscribed on the sarcophagus hiding the vault entrance. When triggered by touching the sarcophagus, it casts {@spell Create Undead}, causing 3 {@creature Ghoul||Ghouls} from the surrounding sarcophagi to attack.

entries.name: Final Combat

entries: As the door creaks open, a fiery red glow floods the tunnel, so bright you shield your eyes on instinct. As your eyes adjust, you make out a large square vault before you where a circle of eight coffins surrounds a glowing red gem...

Inside each coffin is a {@creature Crystal-Eyed Golem|DMSecretWeapon24}, victims of Lord Fennelby's greed, spawned from the recent spate of missing persons: street urchins and brothel madams lured to the manor home with false promises of riches. Now, they lie entombed in varying stages of crystallization. The magical red gem at the center siphons arcane energy into the coffins, crystallizing their eyes, brains, and bones. As the ritual is interrupted, they are torn from their metamorphosis and will stop at nothing to guard the red gem, their life source.

Each coffin remains shut until triggered by an attempt to open or damage it. When triggered, a {@creature Crystal-Eyed Golem|DMSecretWeapon24} jumps from its coffin and uses its actions to defend itself while moving to open another coffin. Each time a coffin opens, a {@creature Crystal-Eyed Golem|DMSecretWeapon24} joins the fight at {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} count 0 and attempts to open another coffin as quickly as possible. If the party attempt to retrieve the red gem, any closed coffins immediately open, releasing the remaining Golems. If the party exit before defeating all the Golems, they must use an action to secure the door, or the Golems pursue them into the night.

Should the GM wish to engage in additional challenges, they can impose a group {@dc 15} Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check to escape the manor undetected. On a failure, they draw the attention of {@dice 1d4} {@creature Guard||Guards} each round until all sixteen join. If any Golems are in pursuit, the party automatically fail this check. Only upon defeating all {@creature Guard||Guards} and Golems (if pursued) can the party leave.

entries.name: Conclusion
entries: If the party successfully steals the red gem and brings it to Lord Witherington, he remains true to his word, selling it and paying the party half the proceeds—amounting to 1,500 GP.

If the party is able to identify the Golems they encountered as missing persons, they can inform their families or friends of the tragic fate of their loved ones. Though grief-stricken, they are relieved to finally have answers.

Lord Fennelby is brought to justice, either by the party reporting him to the city guard, or by Lord Witherington doing so. Witherington is reinstated to his manor house and grants the party hospitality there whenever they pass through the area.

data.name: A Divine Dream
entries: {@adventure Map 1|ADivineDream|1|Adventure Map 1}

The heroes have just arrived in a verdant land that glimmers and whispers with fey magic. As they settle down for a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, the goddess Boann visits them in a mystical shared dream.

As you drift into a deep sleep, the land begins to seep into your dreams—shifting like a kaleidoscope from lush green fields to turquoise coasts; golden shores to moss-carpeted forests; secluded glens to gorse-yellow mountains. At last it settles on a luscious valley, at the center of which stands a well amidst rune-inscribed arches. A goddess peers into its depths. You know her to be a deity—the dream deems it. Her silver hair cascades down her back, while her sea-blue eyes fix on you. When she speaks, it is as the soft trickle of water down a rocky riverbed.
"Welcome, weary souls,
to the glen of faerie rings,
To the Well of Segais,
where wisest water springs,
I bid you grant me but one sip,
and I'll bestow to you,
The answer to one question each,
and I shall answer true.
For I long to taste its wisdom,
but my husband grasps it tight,
Sending forth his cupbearers
at first and final light.
They turn the platforms,
'til runes align,
And seek the Wisdom archways
through which the sun does shine.
You must join the ranks of cupbearer,
should you undertake my quest,
For it is they who hold the goblet
to safely plunge its depths."

The vision fades, as if soaring up into the sky. From this vantage point, you have a bird's-eye view of the valley's glen with the Well of Segais at its center. A winding path through a forest leads southwest where you see four sleeping figures. As you descend towards one, you realize it to be you. You gain speed, diving towards your body. Just as you crash into your sleeping form, you jolt awake.

The party wakes as tendrils of dawn streak the sky. As they reflect on the poem, any character with fey heritage or who succeeds on a {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill History} or {@skill Religion}) check recalls ancient folklore about a mythical well said to contain transcendent wisdom, and remembers that "Well of Segais" means "Well of Wisdom." Legend has it that mortal minds are too weak to taste its waters and live.

They surmise that the goddess is Boann. She is the wife of the god Nechtan, who guards the Well. The poem contains clues as to how the party must progress to fulfil Boann's Quest. The heroes should be able to interpret the poem as below, but if they are struggling to understand, the GM can offer hints, or give insights in response to any hero's successful {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check.

entries.name: GM Guide: The Secrets of Boann's Poem
entries: The following details the information the party must uncover from Boann's poem:

items: There is a well at the center of this valley that contains water which will grant its drinker True Wisdom.
Boann's husband has deemed that only his cupbearers can draw from it.
They do so daily at dawn and dusk.
She is commissioning them to infiltrate the ranks of cupbearers to draw a gobletful of water for her.
In return, she will answer them one question each.

entries: There is more to Boann's poem, but it will be difficult for the party to understand without first investigating the Well.

As the party discusses the dream, their curiosity and investigation draws the attention of a mischievous {@creature Púca|DMSecretWeapon24|Púca}, creatures that feed on thought and reflection. Any hero who has not made a Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check to determine an element of the poem makes a {@dc 13} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check to spot the púca. Should they fail, its ambush is successful, and the party is {@status Surprised} as it attacks.

After defeating the púca, if the heroes do not kill it, they may be able to solicit its help as a guide. The púca is known to respect wit, courtesy, and humor, so the party may be able to win its favor through a toast, a riddle, or a humorous story or joke. If the party befriend the creature, it becomes a helpful guide, leading them to the Well of Segais.

entries.name: Finding the Well
entries: To find the Well, the heroes must retrace the route from their vision. The Well of Segais is the center circle on the adventure map and the party begin at the southwestern corner. Following the path requires a group Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check, yielding the following results (if the party were led here by the púca, treat any roll as a natural 20):

rows: The heroes stumble across a faerie ring (use {@adventure Map 2|ADivineDream|1|Adventure Map 2}). After defeating or escaping the faerie ring, they find the path again, arriving at dawn.
They follow the path and arrive at the Well at dawn.
They follow the path and arrive before dawn, giving them time to investigate the Well before any locals arrive. See "Secrets of the Well" below for its description and discoveries they may make.

entries: As the tree line thins, you see a clearing that shimmers with a golden hue and you immediately recognize it as the vision from your dream. A stone causeway ahead of you leads through an archway and towards the Well, raised up on a three-tiered platform. To the north, east, and west are identical causeways, all with overlapping arches.

If the heroes arrive before dawn with a {@skill Survival} score of 19+, they have time to investigate the Well. The party makes a collective Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check, uncovering the following information depending on their result:

entries.caption: Secrets of the Well
rows: The well oozes a deeply magical and dangerous aura. Clearly, it cannot be drawn from safely yet; there must be more to do before attempting to retrieve some water.
The archways surrounding the well can be moved. Various runes adorn each archway, written in Sylvan.
Moving the archways can cause them to spell out different words in Sylvan: Truth, Lies, or Wisdom.
Boann's poem made reference to the arches spelling out Wisdom, and that only a special goblet can draw water from the well safely.

entries: At dawn, Nechtan, God of knowledge and guardian of the well, manifests in the center of the well. As lord of this domain, he is immediately aware of the heroes' presence.

entries.name: Entreating With Nechtan

entries: As the sky transforms from rose to lilac, a figure appears from the northern causeway, gliding towards the Well. Though clothed in simple linen robes, his very presence exudes majesty and his eyes are deep wells of wisdom that immediately fix upon you. His voice is weighted with the rich gravitas of the earth itself as he speaks to you: "What has brought you to my domain, adventurers?"

Nechtan is not intended to be fought, and laughs off any attempts to deal damage to him. As a deity in his own realm, he is immune to all damage and conditions, and automatically succeeds on all saving throws. Should a stat block be required, a GM can use the {@creature Archmage} stat block with the addition of the {@spell Gate} spell.

If the heroes state they wish to be cupbearers so they might draw from the well, Nechtan offers them a chance to prove themselves worthy by allowing them to draw a gobletful of water from the Well of Segais. He presents them with a riddle to help them draw the water safely.

entries.name: Nechtan's Riddle

entries: "Three cupbearers stand side by side—The Truthful, The Liar, and The Wise One. They will each answer you one question. The Truthful always speaks truly. The Liar always lies. The Wise One sometimes lies and sometimes speaks truly. You must find their identity. Each cupbearer will speak only one clue—listen well. All the information you need to identify each one is contained within these clues.
When you have discerned their identity, take the Goblet held by The Wise One, for only this goblet can safely draw the water."
As Nechtan finishes speaking, three cupbearers, standing side by side, appear before the party, their rune-inscribed goblets outstretched.

items: {@b The Leftmost cupbearer speaks thus:} The Truthful cupbearer stands in the middle.
{@b The Middle cupbearer speaks thus:} I am The Wise One.
{@b The Rightmost cupbearer speaks thus:} The Liar stands in the middle.

entries: The cupbearers will speak nothing more, but will repeat their clue if asked.

entries.name: Solution
entries: This is a logic puzzle set by Nechtan. With only these three pieces of information, the party can identify all three cupbearers. The solution is as follows:

items: {@b Left} = The Wise One
{@b Middle} = The Liar
{@b Right} = The Truthful

entries.name: The Logic of the Puzzle
entries: The left cupbearer claimed the middle one is The Truthful; therefore, the left cupbearer cannot be The Truthful (because there cannot be two Truthfuls). The middle cupbearer said he was The Wise One; therefore, he cannot be The Truthful (because if he was the Truthful, he would have truthfully identified himself as such). Thus, the right cupbearer MUST be The Truthful. According to him, the middle cupbearer is The Liar and as a result, the left cupbearer must be The Wise One.

entries.name: Hint!
entries: If the party needs help, Nechtan will also tell them:
"Wisdom is oft found between the path of truth and falsehood, but not on this occasion."

The party must take the correct goblet from The Wise One by solving Nechtan's riddle or by guessing. With the hint, the riddle becomes quite simple, but even a party that must resort to a guess have a 50/50 chance by this point.

If the players take too long to solve the riddle, consider imposing a time limit to maintain the pace of the adventure. Even if they get the answer wrong, the adventure can progress—they will realize their mistake when the {@creature Spirit of Segais|DMSecretWeapon24} attacks later.

Whether they take the correct goblet or not, Nechtan will warn the party to not draw water for anyone other than themselves. He offers a reward of great Wisdom if they draw water and return it to him, but the party must betray any offer from others who seek the well, and answer only to his call.

entries.name: The Well of Segais
entries: {@adventure Map 3|ADivineDream|1|Adventure Map 3}

When the heroes are ready to attempt the water-drawing ritual, the archways are not oriented correctly. The party must arrange the runes on the archways to spell the word "Wisdom" in Sylvan. The party can investigate the well at this time, if they were not able to do so earlier (see {@adventure Secrets of the Well|ADivineDream|0|Finding the Well}).

If the party rotates the archways correctly, the sun shines through the Wisdom archway at dawn or dusk, illuminating the pool in the center with trembling, golden light. So long as the sun is shining through the archway, the party can safely draw water from the well using the Goblet of Wisdom.
If the heroes attempt to draw water without the sun shining through the Wisdom gate, or using the wrong goblet, they disturb the {@creature Spirit of Segais|DMSecretWeapon24}.

entries.name: Disturbing the Spirit of Segais
entries: The {@creature Spirit of Segais|DMSecretWeapon24} is Nechtan's guardian of the Well. When disturbed, it rises up in ferocious aggression, attempting to drag the characters to their watery deaths. If a hero begins their turn in the Well, they take {@damage 3d4} Psychic damage as they are overwhelmed by the omniscience of the water. If all members of the party are ever unwillingly submerged in the well simultaneously, the wellspring bursts its walls, flooding the land.

entries.name: The People Yearn For Blood!!
entries: Looking for a more cinematic conclusion? GMs should feel free to include the {@creature Spirit of Segais|DMSecretWeapon24} battle to challenge their party if they feel it will make for a more satisfying or thrilling conclusion. The "reward" for correctly solving all the puzzles of the well is not disturbing the spirit, but if your games are more combat-focused, such a battle could well be its own reward. GMs might consider giving the party an additional gift at the conclusion, should the heroes defeat the spirit AND correctly solve all the puzzles.

entries.name: Conclusion
entries: If the party correctly solves the puzzle, or defeats the {@creature Spirit of Segais|DMSecretWeapon24}, they safely dip their goblet into the Well and, as if in response, all the runes of the well turn to shining gold. Boann appears at the eastern edge of the clearing. Her voice is like trickling water as she calls to the party: "Well done, my heroes. Bring forth the water and I shall grant you one answer to any question you seek." Nechtan, meanwhile, has retreated into the northern edge of the forest, and awaits the party there.

The party must now decide which deity they wish to honor and which to betray. If they honor Boann, she is true to her word and grants a truthful answer to a single question from each character. She also pronounces a blessing over them that grants a +1 to all Intelligence checks and Intelligence saving throws.

If they betray her and bring the water to Nechtan, he pronounces his own blessing over them, granting them a +1 bonus to all Wisdom checks and Wisdom saving throws. They may also choose to remain with Nechtan as a cupbearer.
