Should they do so, they are bound to the Well of Segais and Nechtan's service, but in return, they receive Nechtan's blessing once per year, increasing their Wisdom modifier by +1 each time. It is a simple life with few challenges, but if a character is seeking retirement from adventuring, it could be a fitting closure.

entries.name: Introduction
entries: Isle of the Beast Folk, inspired by H. G. Wells' {@i The Island of Dr Moreau}, is an adventure for four level 9 heroes, with themes of body/medical horror. Our heroes awaken on a mysterious island with animal parts grafted to their bodies. Though these body parts grant them enhanced innate abilities, they herald a certain descent into bestial savagery unless the party can reverse the changes.

When the party are attacked by a feral beastman having reverted to a monster ruled by mindless animal instinct, they discover the same fate awaits them unless they can break into Moonrow's compound, find his experiment notes and reverse their changes.

entries.name: The Adventure Begins
entries: {@adventure Map 1|IsleOfTheBeastFolk|1|Adventure Map 1}

Our adventure begins with the heroes on an epic sea voyage when their vessel is struck by a sudden storm. The party is knocked {@condition Unconscious} and carried by the waves to the shore of a mysterious island.

You awaken to birdsong, overlaid upon the soft rhythm of waves lapping on a sandy shore. The sun beats down on you and the humidity is stifling. In a haze of confusion, your memories begin bobbing to the surface of your consciousness—the voyage, the storm, the shipwreck. Gingerly, you push yourself up from the ground, testing each limb as you rise, only to notice something peculiar...

entries.name: Bestial Boons
entries: Each player rolls on the Bestial Boons table to discover which animal part has been grafted to their body, and what boon they gain as a result. At the GM's discretion, player characters that are Constructs have no grafts, or have been grafted with a complex meld of organic and mechanical components.

rows: You can detect static vibrations through your electrosensitive platypus bill. You have {@sense Blindsight} out to 10 feet, which increases to 30 feet while submerged in water, and you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Lightning damage.

You can breathe in water. While {@status Bloodied|XPHB} but not {@condition Unconscious}, you regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Constitution modifier at the end of each of your turns.

You are coated in a layer of camouflaging mucus. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks, and you can cast the spell {@spell Disguise Self} without a spell slot or components, but you can only change your physical appearance when you cast it, not that of what you wear or carry.

Your lizard's eyes grant you {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks based on sight, and you can use a Bonus Action to take {@damage 1d6} Necrotic damage, which can't be reduced in any way. Doing so allows you to unleash a burst of blood at a creature you can see within 10 feet of you. The target must succeed on a {@dc 16} Dexterity saving throw or be {@condition Blinded} for the next minute, or until it uses an action to wipe the blood away.
Once per turn, you can expend 10 feet of movement to leap up to 30 feet. You ignore the first 30 feet you fall when calculating falling damage.
You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Acid and Poison damage, and you have a 10-foot Burrow Speed.

You can use a Bonus Action to strike with your scorpion's tail. It is an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} that deals {@damage 1d6} Piercing damage on a hit, and the target must succeed on a {@dc 16} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition Poisoned} until the end of your next turn. Your reach is increased by 5 feet when making {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} with your tail.

You gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your level anytime you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. While you have these {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} from this trait, you have a +2 bonus to your AC as long as you aren't wearing Heavy Armor.

You can freeze your own body at no harm to your internal organs. You have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Cold damage, and as a Bonus Action, you can freeze your body. While frozen, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is 0, and any creature that hits you with a melee attack takes {@damage 1d8} Cold damage. You remain frozen until you use a Bonus Action to unfreeze yourself, or you take Fire damage.
Roll {@dice 2d9}, rerolling any duplicates, and gain both features rolled.

entries.name: Reverter Attack
entries: Once the party have discovered their gifts, a terrified Beast Folk stumbles out of the island jungle, pursued by a vicious {@creature Reverter|DMSecretWeapon24}—a creature bearing grafted mutations not dissimilar to those the party now bear. The maddened monstrosity turns its ravenous assault upon the party.

The {@creature Reverter|DMSecretWeapon24} is Humanoid... or it once was. The shades of a person remain under a mass of bestial grafts, and its expression is devoid of sound mind, overcome by the instinct to hunt.

When the party have defeated the {@creature Reverter|DMSecretWeapon24}, the Beast Folk, who looks like a dwarf with rabbit's ears, composes himself and explains that they all have been the subjects of {@creature Doctor Moonrow|DMSecretWeapon24|Dr Moonrow}'s gruesome vivisection experiments. The crazed scientist aims to create a {@creature Super-Beast|DMSecretWeapon24}. What Dr Moonrow didn't anticipate was that the Beast Folk would quickly revert to their bestial state, losing all sense of morality and self-awareness.

He continues attempting to perfect his experiment, but for those already transformed, the clock is ticking on their sanity. The only hope to avoid reverting to an animalistic intellect is to break into Moonrow's lab and use his equipment to reverse the process and remove their grafted body parts. Otherwise, the party are destined to become {@creature Reverter|DMSecretWeapon24|Reverters}. He directs the heroes to Moonrow's compound, but is in no fit state to assist.

Hereafter, for each hour that passes in-game, the heroes lose 1 point of Intelligence. If a hero's Intelligence score falls to 3 or below, they become feral—the DM controls their character and they mindlessly attack the creature nearest to them each turn.

entries.name: Dr Moonrow's Compound
entries: {@adventure Map 2|IsleOfTheBeastFolk|1|Adventure Map 2}

Moonrow's compound is set deep within the tropical forest that makes up the island, two miles from the party's location. The path leading there is overgrown, carved only from the light foot traffic of Moonrow and a few of his remaining sound-minded Beast Folk. On a successful {@dc 18} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check, a hero notices Humanoid birds watching from the treetops—{@creature Spyfolk|DMSecretWeapon24}.

entries.name: Perimeter
entries: The compound is guarded by three {@creature Spyfolk|DMSecretWeapon24}, servants of Dr. Moonrow, that fly circuits around the perimeter.

A 50-foot fence encloses the compound, concealed from the {@creature Spyfolk|DMSecretWeapon24} by thick, overhanging canopy. On a successful {@dc 15} Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) or Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check, a hero can scale the fence unseen by the {@creature Spyfolk|DMSecretWeapon24}. On a failure, the hero falls to the other side, taking {@damage 5d6} falling damage and attracting the {@creature Spyfolk|DMSecretWeapon24}.

Alternatively, the party may attempt to pick the lock on the front gate, which is unobscured by forest canopy and requires a {@dc 15} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) check with {@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB}. If the party detected the {@creature Spyfolk|DMSecretWeapon24} with a successful Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check, they can spend 10 minutes in-game tracking their flight patterns and may pick the lock during a reprieve from their watchful eyes. On a failed check, the attempt takes too long and a {@creature Spyfolk|DMSecretWeapon24} spots them, calling to its allies.

The party may also attempt a collective {@dc 18} Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check to enter the compound another way. The DC falls to 13 if the party are aware of the {@creature Spyfolk|DMSecretWeapon24}. On a failure, they are noticed by the {@creature Spyfolk|DMSecretWeapon24}.

If a {@creature Spyfolk|DMSecretWeapon24} spots the party, it squawks in an all-too-human voice to alert the other two {@creature Spyfolk|DMSecretWeapon24}, and they attack in unison. If the party were unaware of their presence, the heroes are {@status Surprised}.

entries.name: Compound Interior
entries: {@adventure Map 3|IsleOfTheBeastFolk|1|Adventure Map 3}

entries.name: The Foyer
entries: The entrance opens directly into a spacious foyer resembling a hybrid of a butcher's shop and an alchemist's lab—slabs covered in animal parts and viscera glow under floating arcane lights, while surgical instruments and vivisection models are scattered atop various crates and barrels. Four cells line the foyer, with butchered {@creature Reverter|DMSecretWeapon24|Reverters} inside.

entries.name: The Lab
entries: Beyond the foyer, Dr Moonrow's operating theatre hums and glows with activity, arcano-graft beacons focused on a huge operating table at its centre, where a huge monstrosity lies {@condition Unconscious}.

{@creature Doctor Moonrow|DMSecretWeapon24|Dr Moonrow} is so engrossed in his most ambitious vivisection experiment to date that the heroes can attempt to sneak past, requiring a successful {@dc 8} Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check, or to surprise Dr Moonrow if they attack.
If they sneak past, they can explore the desk and the storage rooms.

entries.name: The Desk
entries: The desk contains Dr Moonrow's experiment notes, which the party can locate with a {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check. A character studying the notes can piece together instructions on reversing their vivisection—they must ingest a specific potion (Potion of Dissection) before exposing themselves to the arcano-graft beacons.

With a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check, a character reading the notes also notices in the scribbled marginalia a note about a certain venom that weakens the Beast Folks' defences. Next to this note is the symbol of a gryphon skull and wings.

entries.name: The Storage Rooms
entries: The storage rooms are brimming with potion ingredients, glimmering bottles of pre-mixed potions and gleaming surgical instruments. With a {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check, the party locate the Potion of Dissection.

In the eastern storage room, on a successful {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check, the party also locate a bubbling green potion marked with a gryphon skull and wings. If they have read Dr Moonrow's notes, they will recognise it as the venom that weakens Beast Folks' defences. Beside it is a syringe and needle, which the party can fill with the venom. When a hero hits the {@creature Super-Beast|DMSecretWeapon24} with this needle by making a melee attack (treat the syringe as a {@item Dagger|XPHB}), it gains {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to all damage types for 1 hour.

entries.name: Combat
entries: When combat begins, {@creature Doctor Moonrow|DMSecretWeapon24|Dr Moonrow} uses his {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} upon rolling {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} to awaken his {@creature Super-Beast|DMSecretWeapon24}. Thereafter, he uses his movement to maintain a distance from the party, striking with his syringe if anyone moves within reach.

The {@creature Super-Beast|DMSecretWeapon24} fights strategically, perceiving the greatest threat to itself and focusing its attacks there. It fights to the death as long as Dr Moonrow is alive, but if Dr Moonrow falls to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} before the {@creature Super-Beast|DMSecretWeapon24} does, its loyalty ends, and it can be reasoned with if {@status Bloodied|XPHB}. A {@dc 18} Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check reveals that the {@creature Super-Beast|DMSecretWeapon24} will work with the party as long as the relationship remains advantageous.

entries.name: Reversing the Vivisection
entries: Once the party have defeated Dr Moonrow and (optionally) the {@creature Super-Beast|DMSecretWeapon24}, they can set about reversing their vivisections. If they have not done so already, this requires locating Dr Moonrow's experiment notes from the desk and consuming the Potion of Dissection from the storage rooms, before exposing themselves to the arcano-graft beacons on the operating table.

Each hero has the option to roll a {@dc 25} Constitution saving throw if they would like to keep their bestial body parts. On a success, they feel the animal instincts that were threatening to consume them dissipate as the beacons react with the Potion of Dissection to remove the animalism from their bloodstream. Yet, when the procedure is finished, the bestial body parts remain. They sense, intuitively, that the risk of turning into a {@creature Reverter|DMSecretWeapon24} has been nullified. If the heroes have the {@creature Super-Beast|DMSecretWeapon24}'s help in the reversion process, they have a +5 bonus to this Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, their grafted body parts are removed safely, returning them to normal.

entries.name: Conclusion
entries: The party can choose to remain on Beast Folk Isle, mixing the potion and performing the vivisection reversal process on other willing Beast Folk and returning any {@creature Reverter|DMSecretWeapon24|Reverters} to their old body and mind. For any Beast Folk that is successfully returned to their natural state, the party receives a gift ranging from an honorary title or future hospitality in their city, to a cherished piece of jewellery worth 300 gp. If left alive, the {@creature Super-Beast|DMSecretWeapon24} will remain on the island. As Moonrow's "perfect creation", its mind will not degenerate, and its transformation cannot be undone.
When the party are ready to depart the island, they can find a cave beneath the lab, where Dr Moonrow has docked a boat large enough for twelve Medium-sized creatures.

entries.name: Puzzle of the Orbs
entries: {@b Timer:} 2 minutes

You enter a room with four floating orbs, each formed of a different substance: Glass, Ice, Metal, and Wood. This puzzle is called Puzzle of the Orbs. Your task is simply to arrange the orbs in the correct order.
{@i (Reveal the orbs, start the timer.)}

entries.name: Solution
entries: The Orbs need to be arranged so they spell the word "Orbs". The sequence is as follows:
{@b Glass, Ice, Wood, Metal}

{@b Fail.} If the orbs are arranged in the incorrect order, or are not arranged when the timer runs out, all orbs explode. Each exploding orb deals X damage to each player, where X is that character's level. The Glass orb deals Piercing damage, the Ice orb deals Cold damage, the Metal orb deals Lightning damage, and the Wood orb deals Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Mirror of the Poltergeist
entries: {@b Timer:} 90 Seconds

You enter a room filled with objects that is haunted by a {@creature Poltergeist}. There is a huge mirror adorning one wall. You have 90 seconds to identify any objects present in the mirrored room that are not present in the real one—these are the objects the poltergeist intends to use to attack you. {@i (Reveal both maps, side by side, and start the timer.)}

entries.name: Solution
entries: There are 8 items present in the mirror that are not present in the real room. Below is a version of the mirrored room with each object highlighted. The solution is as follows, from top to bottom:

items: Dice Tray Top Left Table
Wooden Stool Top Left Table
Wood Stool Central Table
Dice from Bottom of Dice Tray Central Table
Purple Crystal Central Table
Pink Crystal Bottom Right Table
Green Crystal Bottom Left Table
Small Red Crystal Bottom Left Table

entries.name: Royal Round Table Puzzle
entries: {@b Timer:} 5 Minutes
This puzzle uses a deck of cards, but can be done with pen and paper using a circle divided into 10 equal segments.

Royal dignitaries from two rival kingdoms have agreed to a summit, but treachery and risk run high. There are 10 people attending the summit, and they must sit at a round table. The attendees are as listed below.

items: King of Hearts
Queen of Hearts
Jack of Hearts
Ace of Hearts
King of Spades
Queen of Spades
Jack of Spades
Ace of Spades
Two Jokers

entries: You must arrange all attendees in a circle around the round table, in such a way that the summit is a success. There are complications, however:

items: The Jacks are handsome men, and the Kings are poor lovers. Neither King will tolerate a Jack sitting next to a Queen.
The Jokers are assassins; they can't be placed next to any Royal Card, unless an Ace is directly placed beside that Joker to keep watch. Royal Cards are Kings, Queens, and Jacks.
The Queens don't trust each other; they must sit directly across from one another to keep watch for treachery.
The Aces are secret lovers and dare not sit directly across from one another or directly beside each other, lest their loving gaze give their affair away.
The Aces are loyal to the Queen of their suit; they must be nearer the Queen of their suit than they are to any other Royal Card.
The summit's success hinges on the two royal houses getting to know each other. No two Royal Cards of the same suit can be sitting next to each other.
Each Joker knows the other is an assassin. They will not sit next to each other.

entries: You can use real cards arranged in a circle, or draw the round table and note the position of each card.

entries.name: Solution
entries: The correct order is as shown (note that this order of cards in the opposite suit is also correct):
{@b Fail.} The party take Psychic damage equal to their combined levels multiplied by 3. They can divide out this damage however they wish among themselves.

entries.name: Class Door Puzzles
entries: {@b Timer:} 5 Minutes
A series of four sentient doors bar this floor from the staircase beyond. Each of the following riddles is themed around a different D&D class.

entries.name: GM Only
entries: All doors are utterly impassable without correctly answering their riddle. All doors are {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|immune} to damage and effects, except the door that asks the Barbarian's Door Puzzle.

entries.name: Warlock's Door Puzzle

entries: I weigh very little, but hold a universe inside,
On your journey to knowledge, I'm the ultimate guide.
{@b Hint (if more than one minute has passed):} It's a type of Pact.
{@b Answer:} Tome

entries.name: Fighter's Door Puzzle

entries: I've travelled the world
but am blind all the same.
I'm deaf to the instruments sharing my name.
I'm lighter than feathers,
more fierce than great creatures.
When I don't come first
I am one of your features.
{@b Hint (if more than one minute has passed):} It's a 1st-level Fighter feature.
{@b Answer:} Second Wind

entries.name: Wizard's Door Puzzle

entries: I was here before you came,
And when you're gone I will remain,
Once spoken, I am broken.
{@b Hint (if more than one minute has passed):} The answer is a 2nd-level Wizard spell.
{@b Answer:} {@spell Silence}

entries.name: Cleric's Door Puzzle

entries: The wisest seek me every day,
But in teaching others you give me away,
What am I?
{@b Hint (if more than one minute has passed):} It's a Cleric Domain.
{@b Answer:} Knowledge

entries.name: Barbarian's Door Puzzle

entries: Do it, coward!
{@b Hint (if more than one minute has passed):} Thinking too much makes you want to smash things.
{@b Answer:} Break down the door. It shatters at any touch intended to break it.

entries.name: Civil Warfare
entries: {@i By Nicci-Grace Isbell}
{@b Timer:} 4 Minutes
This puzzle can be solved physically by printing out the tiles on the grid and allowing players to manually rearrange them, or simply creating a 4×4 grid for the heroes to draw the solution onto.
Before you is a 4×4 grid occupied by sixteen tiles. Each tile is one of four colours, and bears one of four icons.

At the moment, they are arranged in a manner suiting a time of peace. You must rearrange the tiles to represent a time of civil war, where no colour or icon is directly next to each other (diagonally adjacent is allowed) AND no column bears the same icon or colour twice. You have 4 minutes, go.

entries.name: Solution
entries: This puzzle has several solutions. So long as no tile is vertically or horizontally touching a tile of the same icon or colour, and no icon or colour appears in a vertical column more than once, the puzzle is solved.

data.name: Of Bone and Bayou
entries: A frontier town is caught in the middle of a deadly battle between two powerful Fey, both of which want to collect a tithe from the town and offer boons in exchange for allegiance. If nothing is done, there won't be a town left for either patron to "protect"!

entries.name: Introduction
entries: Of Bone and Bayou is a short sandbox adventure for four level 3 heroes, featuring the town of Haymire caught in the conflict between two powerful Fey Patrons: {@creature Momma Mulberry|DMSecretWeapon24} and the {@creature Rag and Bone Man|DMSecretWeapon24}.

{@creature Momma Mulberry|DMSecretWeapon24} has been protecting the town for generations, offering "protection" in exchange for an annual blood sacrifice to increase crop yields. However, the {@creature Rag and Bone Man|DMSecretWeapon24} has started lurking in the outskirts of the town, offering his own protection at a lower price: all the dead the town would bury or burn.

Both Fey send magical minions to attack the other, and the town is suffering in the crossfire. This adventure challenges the players to choose which side to back, if either. They could expel both Fey or team up with one to defeat the other.

Familiarize yourself with the Fey Patrons below and use the Previous Grievance Inspiration table or write your own to add drama to the conflict. This adventure is non-linear; GMs can use these tools for inspiration and improvisation, or are free to work with their players to craft their own motivations and history.

rows: Nature provides to those who respect it.
The sweat of your brow is yours to profit from.
Cordiality, agriculture, folk with dirt under their nails, barbarians, druids, rangers.
Directness, a good joke, cleverness, frugality, artificers, rogues.
Informality, industry, pollution, metal equipment, artificers.
Morality, flowery language, threats of violence.

entries.caption: Previous Grievance Inspiration
rows: Rag and Bone Man stole Momma Mulberry's bone hair pins.
Momma Mulberry stole the Rag and Bone Man's cat familiar (she loves it).
They know each other's True Names.
Rag and Bone Man is Momma Mulberry's rebellious son.
They fought over another village a century ago, to its ruin.

entries.name: Tranquility, Interrupted
entries: {@adventure Map 1|OfBoneAndBayou|2|Adventure Map 1}

The adventure begins with the heroes resting quietly in Haymire when a fight breaks out in the streets. A {@creature Trash Golem|DMSecretWeapon24} is fighting {@dice 2d6 + 4} {@creature wolf||Wolves}, and innocents are in danger!

You find yourselves enjoying a quiet evening meal at the Bubbling Bog Tavern in the remote village of Haymire. The air is thick with mead and hearth, which mask the oppressive humidity of the swamplands outside of town. Suddenly, there's a crash and a scream from outside! Chaos has erupted in the town square, where several civilians are caught in the crossfire of two warring groups: a golem made of trash and bone and a dozen angry wolves.

entries.name: Collateral Damage
entries: There are {@dice 2d6} total civilians caught in the conflict, which can be hurt by the collateral damage. At the start of each round, designate {@dice 1d4} civilians that are in danger. They might be at risk from falling debris, a monster, or some other danger. If they are not rescued by the end of the round with a successful ability check ({@dc 12}, determined by the threat) or by slaying a relevant monster, they are killed by the hazard. If all the monsters are slain, the civilians are safe.

entries.name: Local Superstition
entries: Once the monsters have been defeated, the heroes are able to gather information. The villagers are in dire straits, and are happy to provide the players with rumors about the mysterious Fey Patrons once the streets are clear. As explained in the introduction, the town is the battleground of two rival Fey, each of whom can offer "protection" to the town at a price.

Farmers tend to speak favorably of Momma Mulberry while crafters are fond of the Rag and Bone Man. Townsfolk will also direct the players to the lairs of the Patrons: The Heap and The Hut. The players must decide how they'd like to proceed: violence, negotiation, or something in between. Roll on the table below to determine rumors and tips the party can ascertain while interacting with the townsfolk.

entries.caption: Random Rumors
rows: Keep a dirty joke at hand in case you meet the Rag and Bone Man.
All the birds and bugs are spies for Momma Mulberry.
Some Fey love rules and formality; others loathe them.
Momma Mulberry's price may be high, but better to lose one than a dozen from famine.
The Rag and Bone Man promises to protect the town from undead gathering in the area.
Pick a random Previous Grievance to give as a rumor. Could be false!

entries.name: Negotiating with the Patrons
entries: If the players want to parley with either Fey Patron, refer to their description in the introduction for what they like and dislike. GMs can resolve social encounters with the Fey without asking for any Skill Checks, rewarding roleplay and participation. If you'd like to use Influence Checks, start with {@dc 18} and adjust as needed based on the behavior of the players. If the conversation goes poorly, the Patron might turn hostile and attempt to kill the players for their interference. Killing one of the Patrons immediately makes the other Patron friendly toward the players.
Each Patron can offer assistance in defeating the other, should the players ally with them in the battle (see below).

entries.name: Lair of the Rag and Bone Man — The Heap
entries: {@adventure Map 2|OfBoneAndBayou|2|Adventure Map 2}
"Well well well, what hideous creatures darken my doorstep today?" says a deep, mirthful voice from within the trash heap.

A stinking area on the edge of town, filled with all the town's detritus. The {@creature Rag and Bone Man|DMSecretWeapon24} lives in a hovel dug into the side of a large heap of bones and rotting wood. He is guarded by {@dice 3d6} {@creature skeleton||Skeletons} and 1 {@creature Trash Golem|DMSecretWeapon24}, which are not hostile to the players at first.

If the players convince him to help defeat Momma Mulberry, he provides 1 {@creature Trash Golem|DMSecretWeapon24} that listens to the verbal commands of the player that tells him the funniest joke. He offers to "protect" the town for nothing more than the corpses of those who die in Haymire. He is new to the area, aiming to usurp Momma Mulberry's "stranglehold" over the townspeople.

entries.name: Lair of Momma Mulberry — The Hut
entries: {@adventure Map 3|OfBoneAndBayou|2|Adventure Map 3}
"Bold is the soul that ventures into unknown lands. Hark unto me, traveler," calls a soft, but commanding voice from the shadows of a moldering hut.

A swampy, mosquito-infested area a mile outside of town, where birds and bugs watch the players' movement with intense interest. {@creature Momma Mulberry|DMSecretWeapon24}'s hut is an unassuming structure of wood, reeds, and mud sitting on stilts a few feet above the water line. She is guarded by {@dice 3d6} {@creature wolf||Wolves} and 1 {@creature Owlbear}, which are not hostile to the players at first, as long as they act with respect toward nature.

If the players convince her to help defeat the Rag and Bone Man, she provides 1 {@creature Owlbear} that listens to the verbal commands of the player that was the most cordial and respectful toward Momma Mulberry. She has "protected" the town for generations, at the cost of an annual human sacrifice from the townsfolk. Under her protection, the town has flourished, and she has lived here for generations.

entries.name: Choices
entries: It is up to the heroes how the adventure proceeds. They can side with either patron, attempt to eliminate both, or even broker a deal between the two (though this will certainly be extremely difficult). Do not be afraid to reward your players' creativity in finding a solution, no matter how unorthodox. What is certain, however, is that something must be done and soon, lest the entire town be destroyed in the conflict between Momma Mulberry and the Rag and Bone Man.

entries.name: Aftermath
entries: Haymire won't be the same after the conflict is resolved; the townsfolk will likely have lost one or more Patrons, and that void can lead to further adventure. Below are the Boons provided by each of the Patrons, should any of them still have a pact with the town. Consider what long-term impacts the players' decisions can have, either immediately or next time they come through Haymire.

entries.caption: Rag and Bone Man Wins
rows: Food runs short as crops fail.
A sickness spreads among the villagers.
Momma Mulberry's sisters come looking for her killer.

items.name: Tithe
items.entry: When a Humanoid dies within the town, the body must be brought to The Heap within 24 hours.

items.name: Town Boon
items.entry: Undead cannot willingly enter the town. Crafting and manufacturing yields are doubled.

items.name: Personal Boon (if the heroes win victory for the Rag and Bone Man)
items.entry: For 1 week after a player finishes a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} in the town, they have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Necrotic damage and have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on any saving throw forced by an Undead.

entries.caption: Momma Mulberry Wins
rows: Undead start wandering into town at night.
Craftsfolk abandon the town, leaving them without services.
A build-up of trash in town leads to conflict.
Momma Mulberry's sisters visit, increasing the power of their Coven.

items.name: Tithe
items.entry: At the Vernal Equinox, the villagers must sacrifice one Humanoid at Momma Mulberry's altar.

items.name: Town Boon
items.entry: While inside the town, creatures cannot contract diseases and have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Poison damage and the {@condition Poisoned} condition. Crop yields are doubled.

items.name: Personal Boon (if the heroes win victory for Momma Mulberry)
items.entry: For 1 week after a player finishes a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} in Haymire, they have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Poison damage and have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition Poisoned} condition, and on Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling}) checks and Intelligence ({@skill Nature}) checks.

data.name: Treasure Chest Puzzles
entries: In case you didn't know, I ADORE puzzles, and it all comes down to pacing. Puzzles are the ultimate tool for pacing in 5th edition, perfect for keeping everyone engaged in between epic combat and deep roleplay. It's a 10-minute detour with a healthy dose of brain teaser and lethal poison—if you're not breaking up a session every now and then with some old-fashioned riddles, you MUST try it. It's astonishing how transformative a slight detour from the core pillars of the game can be.

In that spirit, I present to you a puzzle format I've been enjoying recently, that I call Treasure Chest Puzzles. Though themed around treasure chests and mimics, they can easily be adapted to work in many situations, such as door puzzles, guard puzzles, etc.

These can also be fun to solve as a little minigame for yourself. If you fancy your hand at logic, give these a shot before checking the answer—I've included the logic behind each solution to help wrap your head around the solution if needed. Once you get used to these types of puzzles, they can be very fun to write!

entries.name: The Rules
entries: The room contains three magic treasure chests. One chest is constructed from Gold, another from Silver, and another from Bronze. All of them carry a {@spell Magic Mouth} enchantment, and will speak one sentence aloud to the heroes.

items: One chest will only be truthful
One chest will only lie
One chest will be either completely truthful or only lie
Only one chest contains treasure
Opening the wrong chest releases a deadly, necrotic gas. All heroes take Xd4 Necrotic damage when an incorrect chest is opened, where X is equal to the Average Party Level.

entries: The heroes must use logic to identify which chest contains treasure based on the words each chest speaks aloud. Opening the correct chest grants them a reward. Opening the wrong chest carries potentially lethal consequences.

entries.name: Treasure Chest Puzzle 1

items.name: Gold Chest
items.entry: I am the Gold chest.

items.name: Silver Chest
items.entry: The Bronze chest speaks the truth.

items.name: Bronze Chest
items.entry: I am empty.

entries: {@b Answer.} The treasure is in the Bronze chest.

{@b Logic.} The Gold chest is clearly speaking the truth. If the Silver chest were speaking the truth, that would mean the Bronze chest would also be speaking the truth, but there must be at least one lie among the chests. Therefore, the Silver chest must be lying, and the Bronze chest does NOT speak true. The Bronze chest claims to be empty, and because this must be a lie, it contains the treasure.

entries.name: Treasure Chest Puzzle 2

items.name: Gold Chest
items.entry: I contain the treasure.

items.name: Silver Chest
items.entry: I contain the treasure.

items.name: Bronze Chest
items.entry: The Silver Chest tells the truth and I contain treasure.

entries: {@b Answer.} The treasure is in the Gold chest.

{@b Logic.} The treasure can only be in one chest. Note that chests can speak only the truth or only lies. The Bronze chest claims to hold treasure and that the Silver chest is true. This is impossible, as the Silver chest claims to hold the treasure as well, therefore the Bronze chest must be lying (and only lying). Therefore the Silver chest must be lying, and Gold must be telling the truth.

entries.name: Treasure Chest Puzzle 3

items.name: Gold Chest
items.entry: My favourite colour is purple.

items.name: Silver Chest
items.entry: I do not hold treasure and Gold does not hold treasure.

items.name: Bronze Chest
items.entry: My favourite fish is the clownfish.

entries: {@b Answer.} The treasure is in the Bronze chest.

{@b Logic.} Silver says both it and Gold do not hold treasure. This must be true, because if it was false, two chests would hold treasure, which is impossible. Therefore, Bronze must hold treasure, and at least one among Gold and Bronze are lying, but it doesn't matter in terms of finding the solution to the puzzle (as to why they are lying about colours and fish, your guess is as good as mine).

entries.name: Treasure Chest Puzzle 4

items.name: Gold Chest
items.entry: I contain treasure and the Silver chest lies.

items.name: Silver Chest
items.entry: I contain treasure and the Bronze chest lies.

items.name: Bronze Chest
items.entry: I contain treasure and the Gold chest speaks the truth.

entries: {@b Answer.} The treasure is in the Silver chest.

{@b Logic.} Bronze cannot be true, as it is contradicted by Gold (both cannot contain treasure). Therefore Bronze is telling only lies, and it claims Gold speaks true. Therefore Gold is lying and Silver must be telling the truth.

entries.name: Treasure Chest Puzzle 5

items.name: Gold Chest
items.entry: I am the Bronze chest and I contain treasure.

items.name: Silver Chest
items.entry: No lying chest contains treasure.

items.name: Bronze Chest
items.entry: The Gold chest contains treasure.

entries: {@b Answer.} The treasure is in the Silver chest.

{@b Logic.} Gold is clearly lying. If Silver is lying, then Gold could contain treasure, but we know it can't because it is only lying. Therefore Silver must be true. Bronze claims Gold contains treasure, which must be false as we know Gold is lying. Therefore Bronze is lying and Silver must contain the treasure.

data.name: Field Testing
entries: A reckless artificer needs your help testing experimental, destructive inventions. Kick down that dungeon door and let loose! An adventure for four level 6 heroes.

entries.name: Introduction
entries: {@creature Fernda Erksbau|DMSecretWeapon24} is an Orc Artificer perpetually on the brink of an astounding discovery. The road to the future is paved in mistakes and explosions, but what's a few lost eyebrows (and test subjects) when the Future awaits? Fernda is found outside the Ruined Temple with a cart full of dangerous and strange magical inventions. She needs the party to test these contraptions out in real combat situations, as laboratory testing has reached its limits. The heroes will need to delve into a dungeon, but instead of traditional loot, they'll be achievement hunting—attempting to complete a specific task with their inventions to get the data Fernda needs and claim a reward.
Fernda will reward the players with 1 Uncommon magic item of their choice for each achievement completed.

entries.name: Arming Up

entries: "Well-met, adventurers! You look sturdy and willing to risk life and limb for the greatest cause of all: SCIENCE!"

Each player chooses an invention, either an Ordinance or a Serum. Be sure that they understand the Task for their chosen invention. Each player must select a different invention, with no duplicates, as Fernda needs test data on as many different inventions as possible.
"And no, you can't just use 'em on each other. Controlled circumstance data isn't useful to me now—get out there and blast some monsters!"

entries.name: Ordinance
entries: Ordinance are powerful objects that require two hands to wield and allow you to cast a specific spell at-will. Each has a chance to Backfire: when the item is used, roll a {@dice d20} and if it meets or beats the Backfire Roll, then the spell targets you or is centered on you, and affects no other creatures. Once an ordinance has Backfired, it cannot Backfire again until it has been recharged.
All Spells are cast at their base level, have a Spell Save {@dc 16}, and do not require {@status Concentration|XPHB}. The ordinance can be used 3 times before running out of power.

rows: Damage 8 creatures in a single cast.
Kill 2 creatures with a single bolt.
{@spell Hold Monster}, but the target uses Constitution for its saves.
Keep a target {@condition Paralyzed} for at least 2 consecutive rounds.
{@spell Spirit Guardians}, but deals Acid damage and the target uses Dexterity for its saves.
End your turn with at least 6 enemy creatures in the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}.

entries.name: Serums
entries: Serums are administered by Fernda. Each has an Effect and Drawback that lasts for 3 hours.

rows: Always deal maximum damage with Attacks and all {@dice d20} rolls that are below a 9 are a 9.
{@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB|Critical Hits} deal no extra damage.
Deal 50 damage to a single creature in one turn using Attacks.
Size becomes Large, Strength set to 22 if lower, and +{@damage 2d6} damage to Strength-based Attacks.
Automatically fail Dexterity saving throws and Intelligence becomes 6.
Keep a creature {@condition Grappled} for at least 3 rounds.
After taking damage, you gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to that damage type for 1 minute.
Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by 5 ft. for each damage type you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} or {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to.
Gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} or {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to at least 3 damage types.
Gain the benefits of the {@spell Haste} spell, which cannot be dispelled and doesn't require {@status Concentration|XPHB}.
If you end your turn without using your Action and all your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, you are {@condition Poisoned} until the end of your next turn.
Move at least 140 ft. before hitting a creature with a melee attack in a single turn.

entries.name: Dungeon: The Ruined Temple
entries: Fernda sits outside a darkened entrance to temple ruins. She had discovered the cavern entrance and has been using it to test her inventions. What she doesn't reveal to the players is that she's already sent multiple adventuring parties before, and they don't usually return with test data... or at all.
In reality, she is responsible for most of the monsters in the cave; the result of her own {@creature Failed Test Subject|DMSecretWeapon24|Failed Test Subjects} and grim experiments.

entries.name: GM Tip
entries: You don't need to use the provided dungeon! You can plop Fernda outside any dungeon in your regular campaign. Just make sure that there are reasonable ways to complete all the Achievements within the dungeon. Consider adding some {@creature Failed Test Subject|DMSecretWeapon24|Failed Test Subjects} to the dungeon as well.
There are two maps, one annotated for the GM's reference and one to use across the adventure; see {@adventure Adventure Map 1|FieldTesting|1|Adventure Map 1}.

entries.name: Entryway (1)
entries: A dark cavern awaits, with echoing, distant sounds from within.

entries.name: Cavern Path (2)
entries: A narrow passage of rough, unworked rock snakes deeper into the darkness. The clear sounds of scraping, gnawing, and chewing can be heard beyond.

Large or larger characters must make a {@dc 20} Strength or Dexterity check to break or squeeze through, causing considerable noise. Reward clever solutions to this problem, such as using oil to make a Large character slip through silently.

entries.name: Open Cave (3)
entries: A shard of light pierces the gloom of this open cavern, barely revealing the hunched forms of several figures.

{@dice 1d6} {@creature ghast||Ghasts} and {@dice 2d6} {@creature zombie||Zombies} gnaw on rotten bones scattered on the cold floor. Light streams in from a crack in the wall, allowing a peek into the {@adventure Grand Foyer (9)|FieldTesting|0|Grand Foyer (9)}. It's so small that only Tiny creatures can fit through.

entries.name: Flooded Paths (4)
entries: The brackish water of the flooded paths stinks of rot and decay. Sounds of desperate battle can be heard just beyond it.
There are no monsters in this area, but it's clear that a fight is just ahead. Broken pieces of adventuring gear and body parts are floating downstream.

entries.name: Forgotten Shrine (5)
entries: This alcove contains the muck-covered remains of an ill-kept shrine.

Alfone Urthay, a crazed {@creature Failed Test Subject|DMSecretWeapon24}, is fending off {@dice 2d6} {@creature ghast||Ghasts} and 1 {@creature Mummy}. He has been trapped down here since yesterday, with the rest of his adventuring party having been slain by monsters and the Backfires of Fernda's inventions. The backfire of whatever serum he has taken seems to have robbed him of any higher thought, and he attacks the party as savagely as he battles the Undead.

entries.name: Altar Room (6)
entries: A place of worship in bygone centuries, the altar is now unrecognizable amidst the rubble.

{@dice 1d6} {@creature winter wolf||Winter Wolves} are fighting {@dice 1d6} {@creature hell hound||Hell Hounds} over the corpses of a few adventurers. Next to them is the {@condition Petrified} statue of a warrior mid-fight, clearly turned to stone by a malfunctioning Adaptive Oil.

entries.name: Dangerous Walkway (7)
entries: Cobwebs cover the ground and walls of this large cavern, with narrow walkways traversing the space precariously.

{@dice 1d6} {@creature Mutated Spider|DMSecretWeapon24|mutated spiders} have made a nest at the bottom of a 40 ft. pit, attacking anyone that traverses the narrow pathways. Falling into the pit causes no damage, but the creature is automatically {@condition Restrained} in the web, as per the Acidic Web action in the mutated spider stat block. The mummified corpse of a previous test subject is also here, which holds a random, unused Ordinance invention.

entries.name: Tempting Treasure (8)
entries: Glittering loot awaits those who leap across the gap of this echoic cavern.
An ancient, gold-covered sarcophagus sits across a 20 ft. gap with a 100 ft. drop into a cold, hard cavern floor. The sarcophagus contains a {@creature Mummy} wearing a diamond necklace worth 500 gp.

entries.name: Grand Foyer (9)
entries: Ever-burning torches ring the remnants of this grand foyer. Debris and moldering skeletons are scattered about the floor.

2 {@creature ogre zombie||Ogre Zombies} are dragging {@dice 1d6} fresh adventurer corpses slowly toward a row of open sarcophaguses on the far wall. If any corpse is placed in a sarcophagus, it transforms into a {@creature Mummy} at the start of the following round.

entries.name: Throne Room (10)
entries: What was once a magnificent throne room for a forgotten lord has been reduced to a corpse-laden den of undeath.

A grotesque {@creature Test Subject Amalgamation|DMSecretWeapon24} is surrounded by its undead servants: {@dice 4d6} {@creature zombie||Zombies} and 2 {@creature ghast||Ghasts}. The Amalgamation reveals that they were one of Fernda's first test subjects, and were forever warped and cursed by her Immortality Serum. She cannot permanently die, instead reviving {@dice 1d4} days after being killed to continue to fill the dungeon with monsters. It appears that the curse is unbreakable.

In reality, the {@creature Test Subject Amalgamation|DMSecretWeapon24} can be cured with a casting of {@spell Greater Restoration} or {@spell Remove Curse} cast at 5th level or above. This is likely beyond the capabilities of the party right now, but if they choose to broker peace and later return, they may be able to rescue the Amalgamation.
The bodies of several decaying adventurers lay nearby. Searching their bodies reveals random malfunctioning and broken inventions, as well as {@dice 2d6 × 100} gp.

entries.name: Aftermath
entries: After the party returns to the surface, Fernda will reward the players with the promised magic items (1 Uncommon item per Achievement completed). GMs might consider having Fernda appear outside another dungeon in the future, hoping to test inventions the players didn't select or with new inventions for them to try out.

entries.name: Fighting Fernda
entries: If the players think Fernda's methods are too reckless or immoral, they may try to fight her to put a stop to her testing. She is a very powerful artificer, and it should be made clear to the heroes that they should tread carefully. GMs should make it very obvious that {@creature Fernda Erksbau|DMSecretWeapon24|Fernda} is likely beyond the heroes' power right now. If they do choose to fight, Fernda will not kill any heroes she defeats. Should a TPK ensue, the players regain consciousness outside the dungeon with 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} and one random magic item missing 12 hours later.
